Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_top_eq_top: The largest ideal sheaf assigns the whole ring to every affine open. Its sections on the indicated open are therefore the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.logDerivIdealSheafIterate_congr_hom: Identify the equal structural morphisms. They then give the same base algebra on every affine open, so the logarithmic derivative construction and every iterate agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_top_eq_top: Restriction pulls back ideal sheaves along the inclusion of the open. Extending a unit ideal along the induced section map sends one to one, so the restriction is again the unit ideal sheaf.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealIterate_le_iSup_logDerivIdealI: Split the n ordinary derivative steps into logarithmic steps and steps in the distinguished partial direction using the mixed-iteration bound. For a term with l partial steps, the partial iterate of L(0) lies in the sum of L(i) for i at most l. Apply the remaining n − l logarithmic steps and use monotonicity and the estimate for sums to bound each resulting term separately. Since i is at most l, increasing the logarithmic count from n − l to n − i only enlarges the ideal. Each enlarged term occurs in the desired sum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDerivIdealIterate_controlledTrans: At zero take the summand L(0). At a successor use monotonicity and the partial derivative bound for sums to apply the next step to each preceding summand L(i). Each i is below m and the one-step estimate puts its partial derivative ideal in the sum of L(i) and L(i + 1). Both indices are at most the new bound, proving the induction step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDerivIdeal_biSup_le: Apply the partial derivative estimate for sums first to the sum over indices and then to each internal sum over witnesses that the index is at most n.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDerivIdeal_controlledTransform_le: The target sum already contains L(i). At i below m the exceptional exponent in its defining identity is positive. The defining identity at i + 1 bounds the image of the derivative ideal of the previous source iterate with exceptional exponent one lower. Apply the chart partial estimate to these two successive identities. Every distinguished partial derivative of an element of L(i) therefore belongs to the sum of L(i) and L(i + 1).
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDerivIdeal_iSup_le: Each original ideal is contained in its partial derivative ideal, so their sum lies in the sum on the right. Each element of the original sum is a finite sum of elements of the summands. Apply additivity of the chosen derivative and use that each derivative lies in the corresponding partial derivative ideal. This gives the containment for every generator.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_natCast_iff_not_succ_le: If a is infinite it is greater than m and at least m + 1. If it is finite, discreteness of the natural order makes being at most m equivalent to failing to be at least m + 1.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_support_derivIdealSheafIterate_if: The support of the m-th derivative iterate is the order-at-least-(m + 1) locus of the input. Being outside this locus is equivalent to having order at most m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_controlledTransform_su: If the image were outside the original threshold locus, its order would be at most m. The controlled-transform bound would give order at most m at the chosen point upstairs, contrary to its belonging to the threshold m + 1 locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_controlledTransform_le: The given order bound at the image point makes the m-th derivative iterate of I the unit ideal in its stalk. Its pullback is still the unit ideal in the stalk upstairs. The blowup derivative bound at iteration m puts this pullback inside the m-th derivative iterate of the controlled transform, since the exceptional factor has exponent zero. Thus the latter stalk ideal is the unit ideal too. The blowup is smooth over the base because the center satisfies the normal crossing hypothesis. Apply the unit-stalk criterion upstairs to conclude that the controlled transform has order at most m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_controlledTransform_le_of_forall: The global hypothesis gives the required bound at the image of the chosen point. Apply the pointwise result there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_controlledTransform_le_of_not_su: The failure of the lower bound m + 1 is equivalent to order at most m. Apply the pointwise controlled-transform bound with this inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_controlledTransform_le_of_orderA: Apply the pointwise controlled-transform bound with the original point taken to be the image of x₁.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_le_iff_notMem_orderAtLeastLocus: The locus condition is order at least m + 1. The extended-natural order comparison identifies its failure with order at most m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_derivIdealSheafIterate_eq_top: A stalk ideal is the unit ideal exactly off its sheaf support. For the m-th derivative iterate this is exactly where the original order is at most m.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_of_smooth_over_field: A smooth morphism is locally of finite type. Over a field, the affine section rings of a locally finite-type scheme are Noetherian, so the scheme is locally Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_controlledTransform_le_of_isMark: Use the order assertion in the simultaneous induction for smoothness and the order bound, and evaluate it at x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_projectionToBase_comp_and_orderAt: Induct along the marked sequence. At stage zero the structural morphism is the original smooth one and the controlled transform is restriction by the initial open immersion. Order is invariant under this restriction. For the step, the center has strict normal crossings with the current boundary, so blowing it up preserves smoothness and the next scheme is locally Noetherian. The marked order condition along the center implies the required containment of the current ideal in the m-th power of the center ideal. The exceptional-divisibility identity identifies the next ideal with the one-step controlled transform by uniqueness. Apply the one-step order bound to the induction bound at all image points. This proves both assertions at the next stage.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.germ_coord_notMem_maximalIdeal_sq: The affine chart is étale over the polynomial ring, and the local ring at y is its localization at the point prime. The coordinate belongs to that prime, so its germ belongs to the local maximal ideal. The cotangent independence theorem for the chart gives a linearly independent family for the singleton containing this coordinate. Its cotangent class is thus nonzero, which excludes membership in the square of the maximal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_one_of_not_two_le: Infinity is at least two, so the hypothesis makes the extended natural number finite. An ordinary natural number below two is at most one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_one_of_restrictIdeal_eq_coord: The chosen generator gives order at most one by the coordinate-ideal upper bound. The point is on the support, giving order at least one.
The singleton coordinate ideal gives the upper bound of one. Membership in the support gives the lower bound of one, so the order equals one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_le_one_of_mem_of_restrictIdeal_e: Outside the support the order is zero. On the support, the germ of the chosen coordinate belongs to the stalk ideal because that coordinate generates part of the section ideal. The stalk ideal is contained in the maximal ideal, so the coordinate lies in the point prime. Its germ does not lie in the square by cotangent independence. The stalk ideal therefore cannot lie in that square, so the order is less than two.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_le_one_of_restrictIdeal_eq_coord: The index j is among the chosen generators. Apply the coordinate-ideal upper bound using that generator.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_eq_support_of_isDerivB: An order at least the positive m is at least one and hence places the point on the support. Conversely a point on the support has nonzero order. The derivative-balance dichotomy then gives order at least m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_zero_or_le_orderAt_of_isDeriv: At threshold zero the bound is automatic. Assume m is positive and the order is nonzero. Derivative balance at index m − 1 says that the m-th power of that derivative iterate is contained in I. Hence its order is at least that of I. The order of the power is m times the order of the iterate, so the iterate cannot have order zero. The point therefore belongs to its support, which is the order-at-least-m locus of I.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivationOfSurjectiveFun_add: Lift the two target elements to a and b in the source. Their sum lifts to a + b. The formula for the descended function reduces additivity to additivity of D and of f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivationOfSurjectiveFun_apply: The chosen lift of f(s) has the same image as s. Since the derivation preserves the kernel, the images of the derivatives of the two lifts agree. This gives the formula for the descended function.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivationOfSurjectiveFun_mul: Lift the two elements to x and y. Their product lifts to xy. Apply the Leibniz rule in S and map it to T. The images of the derivatives of the lifts are the descended values, giving the Leibniz rule on T.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivationOfSurjectiveFun_one: Lift the target unit element to one in S. A derivation sends one to zero, so the descended function also sends one to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivationOfSurjectiveFun_smul: Lift t to a in S. The scalar multiple of a lifts the corresponding scalar multiple of t because f is a k-algebra map. Apply k-linearity of D and of f to the formula for the descended function at this lift.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivationOfSurjective_apply: The descended derivation has the same underlying function used in its construction. Its value at f(s) is the image of D(s) by the formula for evaluating that function on a lift.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_derivation_eq_of_map_eq: If s and s′ have the same image, their difference lies in the kernel. The derivation preserves this kernel, so the derivative of their difference has zero image. Additivity gives equality of the images of their derivatives.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealIterate_add: Induct on r. At zero the equality follows from the identity iterate. Increasing r by one applies the derivative ideal operation to both sides of the equality for r. The recursive definition identifies these with the two sides at the successor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealIterate_le_of_le: Write r′ as r plus a nonnegative difference. The addition law expresses the r′-th iterate as the additional iterations applied to the r-th iterate. Iteration contains its starting ideal, giving the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealIterate_le_pow_of_le_pow: Induct on the iteration count. At zero the result is the given containment. For the successor, use monotonicity to put the next derivative ideal in the derivative ideal of the current upper power. The one-step estimate lowers that exponent by one with truncation at zero. This is the exponent n minus the new iteration count.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealIterate_one: One iteration applies the derivative ideal operation to the zero-th iterate, which is J itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealIterate_succ: The recursion defines the successor iterate by applying the derivative ideal operation once to the previous iterate. This is the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealIterate_zero: Zero iterations apply the identity to J by the definition of iteration.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_bot: The only element of the zero ideal is zero, and every derivation takes zero to zero. Every generator of the resulting derivative ideal is therefore zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_eq_sup_span: The derivative ideal is defined as the sum of J and the span of the values of all base-linear derivations on elements of J. This is exactly the expression in the statement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_iSup_le: The sum of the original family lies in the sum of its derivative ideals because each original ideal lies in its own derivative ideal. The sum of the originals is generated by their union. Every derivative of an element of this union lies in the derivative ideal of a corresponding member, and hence in the sum of the derivative ideals. The span argument extends that containment to derivatives of the whole sum. The containment criterion gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_le_derivIdeal: Apply monotonicity of the derivative ideal operation to the inclusion of I in J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_le_iff: The derivative ideal is generated by J and all indicated derivative values. It lies in K exactly when K contains the first summand and contains each generator of the second summand. These are the two stated conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_le_pow_of_le_pow: Monotonicity puts the derivative ideal of I in the derivative ideal of the n-th power of P. The power estimate bounds the latter by the power with exponent n − 1, with exponent zero when n is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_mono: If I is contained in J, every element of I belongs to the derivative ideal of J. Every derivative of an element of I belongs there as well, since the element is in J. The ideal containment criterion therefore gives monotonicity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_mul_le: The product IJ lies in the first summand on the right because J lies in its derivative ideal. The product ideal is additively generated by products of one element from each factor. By the Leibniz rule the derivative of a product is the sum of a term belonging to the first summand and a term belonging to the second. Additivity puts every derivative of the product ideal in their sum, proving the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_pow_le: For n equal to zero, the target is the unit ideal because the exponent is truncated at zero. For n positive apply the containment of the derivative ideal of a successor power in the preceding power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_pow_succ_le: The original power is J to the n-th power times J, and J lies in its derivative ideal. Every derivative of the original power also belongs to the stated product by the derivative estimate for powers. Apply the ideal containment criterion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_pow_succ_le_pow: The original power is contained in the preceding power because it is that power multiplied by J. Its derivative values are contained there as well by the Leibniz estimate. These two containments suffice by the definition of the derivative ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_top: The derivative ideal contains its input ideal. When the input is the unit ideal, this containment forces equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivation_apply_mem_derivIdeal: The element D(x) is one of the generators adjoined to J in the derivative ideal, since x belongs to J. It therefore lies in that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivation_apply_mem_of_mem_span: Induct through the ideal span. The derivative of every chosen generator belongs to T by hypothesis, and the derivative of zero is zero. Additivity handles sums. For a multiple ab of an element b already in the span, the Leibniz rule writes its derivative as a times the derivative of b plus b times the derivative of a. The first term is in T by induction and the second because b is in T. Thus every element of the span has derivative in T.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivation_apply_mem_pow_mul_derivIdeal: Induct on n. At zero every derivative of J lies in its derivative ideal. For the successor step write elements of the power as sums of products of an element from the previous power and an element of J. Differentiating the J factor gives a member of the derivative ideal of J multiplied by the previous power. Differentiating the other factor uses induction, and multiplication by the remaining J factor restores the exponent required on the right. Additivity extends the estimate to the sums.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivation_apply_mem_pow_of_mem_pow_succ: Induct on n. For n equal to zero the target is the unit ideal. At a successor, use additivity to reduce to a product of an element of the previous power and an element of J. In the Leibniz term differentiating the J factor, the other factor already belongs to the desired power. In the term differentiating the other factor, its derivative belongs to the power one smaller by induction, and the remaining factor of J restores the desired power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_derivIdeal: The derivative ideal is a sum of ideals one of whose summands is J. Therefore it contains J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_derivIdealIterate: At zero the iterate equals J. Each new iterate contains the previous one because the derivative ideal contains its input. Repeated inclusion gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_succ_le_pow: A product of an element of the m-th power and an element of J belongs to the m-th power, since it is an ideal. The products generate the next power, giving the containment.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_comp_derivation_apply: The derivation with values in T is constructed by applying the structure map to every value of the original derivation. Its value at s is the image of the original value at s.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivation_comp_algebraMap_apply: The restricted derivation is constructed by precomposing the given derivation with the structure map from S to T. Evaluating this composite on s gives the asserted value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivation_ext_of_coord: Each derivation factors through a linear map on the differential module. The coordinate differentials form a basis by formal étaleness. The hypothesis gives equality of the two linear maps on every basis vector, hence on the whole module. Composing with the universal differential gives equality of the derivations.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_derivIdeal_sum: The old partial derivations span all derivations of S. After applying the structure map, each of their values on J is a value of the corresponding partial derivation in T on the extended ideal. This gives containment of the extended derivative ideal in the new derivative ideal. Conversely the partial derivations in T span all derivations there. The partials for old coordinates give images of original derivatives on elements from J, and partials for extra coordinates give zero on those images. Thus all derivatives of the generators of the extended J lie in the extended derivative ideal. The Leibniz rule extends this to the ideal they generate, because that ideal is itself contained in the extended derivative ideal. This gives the other containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDeriv_inl_algebraMap: Compare the partial derivation for the old coordinate in T restricted to S with the corresponding partial derivation in S followed by the structure map on its values. Both take one on the indicated coordinate and zero on all the other coordinates of S. Since coordinate values determine a derivation, these maps agree on every s.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDeriv_inr_algebraMap: Restrict the partial derivation for the extra coordinate j to S. On each coordinate of S it vanishes, since that coordinate maps to a coordinate in the first block. Derivations on S are determined by the coordinate values, so the restricted derivation is zero.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.apply_mem_of_forall_partialDeriv_mem: The derivations whose values on X lie in K form a submodule because evaluation is linear and K is an ideal. By hypothesis each partial derivation belongs to this submodule. The partial derivations span the module of derivations, so all derivations belong to it, including D.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_map_le: The extension of J lies in the extension of its derivative ideal. All coordinate partial derivatives on the extended J belong to the latter ideal by the generator argument. They span all derivations over L, so the same containment holds for every derivative of every element of the extended J. Apply the derivative ideal containment criterion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_derivIdeal: The coordinate compatibility gives one inclusion by transporting the source partial derivatives. It gives the reverse by applying the target partial derivatives to generators of the extended ideal and then extending to all derivatives. The two containments give equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_derivIdeal_le: Each element of J maps into the extended J and hence into its derivative ideal over L. For each source coordinate partial derivation, its value on J maps to the value of the corresponding partial derivation over L on the image of that element. These images therefore belong to the desired ideal. Since coordinate partial derivations span all source derivations, this holds for every derivative generator. The extended derivative ideal is generated by these images together with the images of J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDeriv_algHom_apply: View each side as the value at f of a k-derivation from S to S′. On the left, the partial derivation over L is restricted to S through φ and is k-linear because the scalar map from k factors through L. On the right, apply φ to the values of the partial derivation over k. Since φ sends coordinates to the corresponding coordinates, both derivations have the same dual values on every coordinate of S. The coordinate differentials are a basis, so these derivations coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDeriv_mem_map_derivIdeal: The extended J is generated by the images of elements of J, and all those images lie in the extended derivative ideal. The chosen target partial derivative of any such generator is the image of the corresponding source partial derivative and so belongs to the extended derivative ideal. The Leibniz rule and additivity extend this membership from the generators to every element of the extended J.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdeal_map_le: The extended ideal itself lies in the extension of the derivative ideal. Any element x of the extended ideal is a fraction with numerator a from J and a denominator m that becomes a unit. For a derivation of the localization, the Leibniz rule on mx = a gives m² times the derivative of x as m times the derivative of a minus a times the derivative of m, with all elements read in the localization. The first term is in the extended derivative ideal by the cleared-derivation lemma, and the second belongs there because a lies in the extended original ideal. Cancel the unit m twice. The derivative ideal containment criterion gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivation_algebraMap_mem_map_derivIdeal: Since the differential module is finitely presented, clear a common denominator of the restricted derivation to obtain a derivation of S with values in S. The cleared derivative of a is then the image of a derivative of an element of J, so it lies in the extended derivative ideal. The denominator acts by a unit in the localization, and canceling it proves membership of the original derivative.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_derivIdeal: The extension of the original derivative ideal is contained in the derivative ideal of the extension by extending derivations. Finite presentation of the differential module gives the reverse containment by clearing denominators. Therefore the two ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_derivIdeal_away: Localization away from g is localization at the multiplicative set of its powers. Apply the equality for a general localization to that set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_derivIdeal_le: The extension of J is contained in its derivative ideal. Each original derivation extends to the localization and agrees there on the images of elements of S. Thus the image of every derivative generator for J is a derivative of an element of the extended ideal. This proves containment for all the generators of the extended derivative ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_natCast_of_le_of_not_succ_le: The upper condition excludes infinity. For the resulting ordinary natural number, being at least n and strictly below n + 1 forces equality with n.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eulerDerivation_apply: The Euler derivation is the sum of the coordinate derivations with the given coefficients. Apply the finite-sum evaluation formula over the full index set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eulerDerivation_apply_generator: On the chosen generator the duality hypothesis makes every summand vanish except the one at the matching index. That term is the generator itself multiplied by one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eulerDerivation_apply_mem_span: In the Euler sum each term has a coordinate generator as a factor and therefore belongs to the coordinate ideal. The sum belongs to the ideal as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eulerDerivation_sub_natCast_mul_mem_pow_: Apply the Euler congruence for the r-th power of the coordinate ideal to the given element f.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eulerDerivation_sub_self_mem_sq: Let J be the coordinate ideal. On each generator, the Euler derivation gives the generator itself. The difference between the Euler value and the input is additive. For a multiple ca of an element of J, this difference is c times the difference for a plus a times the Euler value of c, by the Leibniz rule. The latter term lies in J² because every Euler value lies in J. Induction on expressions in the ideal span gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_eulerDerivation_sub_natCast_mul_m: Let J be the coordinate ideal and induct on r. At zero every Euler value lies in J. At the successor, use sums of products ab with a in the r-th power and b in J. Write E for the Euler derivation. By the Leibniz rule, E(ab) − (r + 1)ab equals a(E(b) − b) + b(E(a) − ra). The first difference lies in J² and the second lies in the (r + 1)-st power by induction. Both products lie in the (r + 2)-nd power, and additivity gives the claim for all sums.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_derivIdealIterate_of_isUnit_n: Induct on j. At zero the iterate is I and the order is r. For a successor within the bound j + 1 ≤ r, the preceding iterate has order r − j, which is positive. Applying the one-step decrease gives order r − j − 1, the required order at the successor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_derivIdeal_of_isUnit_natCast: Order r means I lies in the r-th power of the maximal ideal and fails to lie in the next power. The general derivative estimate puts the derivative ideal in the (r − 1)-st power. The Euler argument with r a unit shows that the derivative ideal cannot lie in the r-th power, because the parameters generate the maximal ideal. These two facts give order exactly r − 1.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_pow_succ_of_deriv_mem_pow: Each term in the Euler value of f is a generator times a derivative lying in the r-th power. Thus the Euler value lies in the next power. By the Euler congruence it differs from r times f by another element of that next power. Subtract to put r times f in the next power, then multiply by the inverse of r to obtain f there.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_derivIdeal_le_pow: If the entire derivative ideal lay in the r-th power, then each dual derivation of every element of I would take values in that power. Since the elements of I already lie in that power and r is a unit, the Euler criterion puts every one of them in the next power. This contradicts the failure of that containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sum_smul_derivation_apply: Evaluation at a commutes with finite sums of derivations because their addition is pointwise. Evaluating a scalar multiple multiplies the value by the same ring element, giving the stated sum.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_sectionsAlgebra: The algebra structure is defined by the given ring homomorphism from k to the section ring. Its structure homomorphism is therefore that same map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_add: Induct on r. At zero the outer iterate is the identity. At each successor apply the derivative ideal sheaf operation to both sides of the induction equality, which gives the new equality by the recursion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_ideal: At zero both sides are the original section ideal. At a successor the sheaf operation on the previous iterate takes its affine section ideal to the ring-level derivative ideal. By induction the input is the previous ring-level iterate, so its derivative ideal is the next ring-level iterate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_one: One iteration applies the derivative ideal sheaf operation to the zero-th iterate, which is I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_succ: The successor iterate is defined by applying the derivative ideal sheaf operation to the preceding iterate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_zero: The zero-th iterate is the original ideal sheaf by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheaf_ideal: The derivative ideal sheaf assigns to each affine open the derivative ideal of its original ideal in the section ring, using the k-algebra structure induced by the structural morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheaf_map_ideal_basicOpen: Restriction of sections from an affine open to the basic open is localization at f and respects the scalar maps from k. The ideal on the basic open is the extension of the original section ideal. The differential module of the original section ring is finitely presented, so the derivative ideal commutes with this localization. This identifies the extended derivative ideal with the derivative ideal assigned to the basic open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheaf_mono: An inclusion of ideal sheaves yields inclusions of the section ideals on all affine opens. The ring-level derivative ideal is monotone, so it preserves each inclusion. These inclusions give monotonicity of the sheaf operation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheaf_mul_le: On an affine open, multiplication of ideal sheaves gives the product of their section ideals. Apply the product bound for the derivative ideal of that ring product. The two terms on the right are the section ideals of the two product sheaves, each of which lies in the section ideal of their sum. This proves the claim on every affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheaf_pow_succ_le: On each affine open the power and products of ideal sheaves are the corresponding operations on the section ideals. Applying the derivative ideal bound for a successor power to those ideals gives the asserted containment there, and hence globally.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.finitePresentation_kaehlerDifferential_s: The section ring is of finite type over k, so its differential module is generated by the differentials of finitely many algebra generators. The section ring is Noetherian. Over such a ring a finite module is finitely presented, giving the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.finiteType_sections: Since the morphism is locally of finite type, its ring map from the affine base to the sections on U is of finite type. The global sections of the affine base identify with k. Composing with this identification preserves finite type, and the given algebra structure uses exactly the resulting scalar map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherianRing_sections: The section ring is a finitely generated algebra over the Noetherian ring k. The Hilbert basis theorem therefore makes the section ring Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isScalarTower_sections: The scalar maps from k are the pullbacks of global sections of the base. The structure map between the two section rings is restriction. Restriction sends the scalar section on U to the same scalar section on the basic open, showing that the two routes from k agree. This is the scalar tower condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_derivIdealSheaf: On every affine open the derivative ideal of the section ideal contains the section ideal itself. These containments give the inclusion of ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_derivIdealSheafIterate: At zero the iterate equals I. Each new derivative ideal sheaf contains the previous one, so induction gives containment of I in every iterate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_preimage_top: The inverse image of the whole base is the whole source, which contains U.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsAlgebraMap_comp_restrict: Pullback of global sections to an open, followed by restriction to a smaller open, equals direct pullback to the smaller open. Composing this equality with the identification of k with the base global sections gives the stated compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsAlgebraMap_eq: The structure map on sections first identifies k with the global sections of its spectrum. It then pulls these sections back to U along the structural morphism. This is the defining composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsAlgebraMap_restrict_apply: Evaluate the compatibility of the two structure maps with restriction at the scalar a.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_comap_fieldBaseCh: At zero both sides are the pulled-back input. At a successor apply the one-step field base-change formula to the previous iterate, using induction to identify that previous input after pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheaf_comap_fieldBaseChange: In the field pullback square, compatible affine charts give equality of the section ideals around every point. The local equality criterion gives equality of the derivative ideal sheaves globally.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_derivIdealSheaf_comap_: Choose an étale chart on X around the image of y and lift it to a compatible affine chart on Y by field base change. The pullback on section rings is a k-algebra map because the scheme square commutes and the scalar map on the new chart factors through L. It sends every old coordinate to the matching new coordinate. The affine ideals of both pulled-back sheaves are extensions along this section map. Apply the ring-level field-extension formula for derivative ideals on compatible coordinates to identify them on the chosen neighborhood of y.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_mem_of_map_mem: On the basic open the restriction map is localization at g. Write the image of s as a fraction with numerator in the given ideal and denominator a power of g. The cross-multiplied equality holds in the source after multiplication by one further power of g. The product of these powers times s is therefore in the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_eq_of_locally_eq: Apply the local-to-affine containment result in both directions. The section ideals agree on every affine open, giving equality of the sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_of_le: Restriction of either ideal sheaf to the smaller affine amounts to extending its section ideal along the restriction map. Equal ideals on the larger affine have equal extensions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_le_of_locally_eq: Take s in the section ideal of I on U. Around each point of U choose an affine with equal section ideals and then a basic open of U inside it. The two ideal values remain equal on this smaller affine. Thus the restriction of s belongs to the localization of the section ideal of J on U. Clearing denominators shows a power of each defining section times s lies in that ideal. These defining sections generate the unit ideal because they cover U. They lie in the radical of the ideal of multipliers taking s into J, so that ideal contains one, giving s in J.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxContactIdeal_comap_fieldBaseChange: The maximal contact ideal is the specified iterate of the derivative ideal sheaf. Rewrite both maximal contact ideals by that description and apply field base change for the iterate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_fieldBaseChange: At threshold zero both sides are the whole scheme. At a positive threshold m, the order locus is the support of the (m − 1)-st derivative ideal iterate on either scheme. Field base change commutes with this iterate, and the support of the pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support. This gives the equality of loci.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_fieldBaseChange: The equality of order loci identifies the two membership conditions for every natural threshold at the chosen point. Thus the two extended orders have exactly the same finite lower bounds, giving equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsAlgebraMap_comp_specMap: The global section map of the spectrum morphism corresponds to φ under the identifications of global sections with the fields. Pullback on sections along the composite therefore sends a scalar to L through φ and then pulls its scalar section back to W along q.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.span_eq_top_of_isAffineOpen_of_forall_me: Suppose the span is proper and choose a maximal ideal containing it. Its point in the affine open lies in some basic open of a member of s. That member must lie outside the maximal ideal, contrary to containment of the span. Thus the span is the unit ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.algebraMap_stalkAlgebra: The algebra structure on the stalk is given by the specified homomorphism from k. Its structure map is therefore that homomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_eq_top_of_orderAt: The support formula at threshold m + 1 identifies the support of the m-th iterate with the empty order locus from the hypothesis. An ideal sheaf with empty support has unit ideal on every affine open, and hence equals the unit ideal sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_top_or_exists_eq_natCast: An extended natural number is either infinity or a finite natural number. In the finite case its ordinary natural value represents it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isAffineOpen_mem: Choose a member of the affine open cover containing the point. Its image in the scheme is an affine open neighborhood.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.finite_kaehlerDifferential_of_isLocaliza: The differential module of the localization is the scalar extension of the original differential module. A finite generating family maps to a finite generating family after scalar extension, so the localized module is finite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.finite_kaehlerDifferential_stalk: Take an affine neighborhood of x, whose finite-type section algebra has finitely generated differentials. The stalk is its localization at the point prime, and the scalar maps commute with that localization. The localization formula preserves finite generation of the differential module.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_of_charZero: Choose a transcendence basis for the extension. The purely transcendental part is formally smooth, and the algebraic extension above it is separable in characteristic zero, as in the transcendence-basis result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_of_isAlgebraic: The injective map from the domain into L sends each nonzero element to a unit, so it extends to the fraction field. That field is formally smooth over k because it is a localization of the formally smooth domain. An algebraic relation over the domain remains a nonzero polynomial relation over the fraction field, so L is algebraic over that field. In characteristic zero it is separable, hence formally étale over the fraction field. Composition gives formal smoothness over k.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_of_isTranscendenceBasis: The subalgebra generated by the basis is a polynomial k-algebra because the basis is algebraically independent. It is a formally smooth domain, embeds in L, and L is algebraic over it by the spanning property of the transcendence basis. Apply the fraction-field and separability argument to this subalgebra.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_of_ringEquiv: The compatible ring isomorphism is an isomorphism of k-algebras. The identity k-algebra is formally smooth over itself, and formal smoothness transfers along this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_residueField: The residue field with the given scalar map is a field extension of k. Over a characteristic-zero base every field extension is formally smooth, by the transcendence-basis argument.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_sections: Smoothness gives a smooth map from the global sections of the affine base to the section ring of the affine open. This map is formally smooth. The base global sections are isomorphic to k by the affine identification, so formal smoothness over k follows by composition using the specified scalar map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_stalk: Choose an affine neighborhood of x. Its section ring is formally smooth over k, and the germ map identifies the stalk with its localization at the point prime. Localization is formally smooth over the original ring. Composing gives the result over k, since the scalar maps are compatible with the germ.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.free_kaehlerDifferential_of_formallySmoo: The finite differential module is finitely presented over the Noetherian ring. Formal smoothness makes it projective, hence flat. A finitely presented flat module over a local ring is free.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.free_kaehlerDifferential_stalk: The stalk ring is local and Noetherian, formally smooth over k, and has finite differential module. The freeness criterion for this situation applies to its differentials.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.germ_sectionsAlgebraMap_apply: Evaluate the equality between the scalar map followed by the germ and the stalk scalar map at a.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_eq_top_of_support_eq_empty: At each point of an affine open U the stalk ideal is the unit ideal because the point is outside the support. Therefore the ideal on U has a section whose germ is a unit at that point. The basic opens of such sections cover U, so the sections generate the unit ideal in the affine section ring. All those sections already belong to the ideal of J on U.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_orderAtLeastLocus: For threshold zero the locus is the whole scheme. For positive threshold it is the support of the specified derivative ideal sheaf iterate, which is closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherianRing_sections_of_smooth: The section map from the affine base is smooth and hence finitely presented. Its source is isomorphic to the field k, which is Noetherian. A finite-variable polynomial ring over it is Noetherian, and the section ring is a quotient of such a ring. Thus the section ring is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherianRing_stalk: Every affine section ring is Noetherian by smoothness over the field. The stalk is a localization of an affine section ring, so it too is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isScalarTower_stalk: The stalk scalar map agrees with the scalar map on U followed by the germ. With the given identifications of the structure maps, this is the scalar tower condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_natCast_stalk: The positive integer has nonzero image in the characteristic-zero field k and is therefore a unit there. Its image in the stalk remains a unit under the scalar homomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_orderAt_derivIdealSheafIterate: The given order bound puts the stalk ideal in the (n + r)-th power of the maximal ideal. Taking the r-th derivative iterate lowers the guaranteed exponent by at most r, so the resulting stalk ideal lies in the n-th power. Translate this back into an order bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_derivIdealSheafIterate: The general lower bound gives the inclusion from the original locus to the locus of the iterate. For the reverse, at a point with infinite original order the threshold is automatic. If its finite order n is below r, the n-th iterate has order zero and all later iterates have order zero because the ideals increase. This contradicts the positive threshold m − r. If n is at least r, the r-th iterate has order n − r. The assumed threshold m − r then gives n at least m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_orderAtLeastLoc: If m is less than r, the target threshold is zero and every point satisfies it. Otherwise apply the previous order lower bound at each point of the original locus with n = m − r.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_derivIdealSheafIterate_eq_sub: The stalk is Noetherian and formally smooth over k with a finite free differential module. Its residue field is also formally smooth over k. These facts give local parameters generating the maximal ideal and derivations dual to them. Each positive natural scalar is invertible in the stalk. The ring-level order decrease formula therefore makes the j-th derivative iterate have order r − j for j at most r. Use compatibility of iteration with taking the stalk to obtain the sheaf order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsAlgebraMap_comp_germ: The scalar section on U is the restriction of the corresponding global scalar section. Restriction from the whole scheme to U followed by the germ at x is the global germ map. Therefore the scalar maps agree after taking germs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_derivIdealSheaf: Choose an affine neighborhood of x. The stalk is the localization of its section ring at the prime of x, and the scalar structures agree through the germ map. The differential module of the section ring is finitely presented, so taking the derivative ideal commutes with localization. The two stalk ideals are the extensions of their affine section ideals. The localization formula therefore gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_derivIdealSheafIterate: At iteration zero the equality is immediate. At each successor the stalk of the derivative ideal sheaf is the derivative ideal of the preceding stalk. Applying induction identifies this preceding stalk with the preceding ring-level iterate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_derivIdealSheafIterate_eq_orderA: Use the equality of order loci with r = m − 1. Since m is positive, the corresponding threshold for the iterate is one. The locus of order at least one is exactly the support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheafIterate_comap: At zero both sides are the pullback of I. At each successor, apply the induction equality for the preceding iterate and then use the one-step result that the derivative ideal sheaf commutes with smooth pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.derivIdealSheaf_comap: At every point of Y the local smooth charts give an affine neighborhood where the two section ideals agree. Equality of ideal sheaves is local, so these affine equalities give the claimed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_derivIdealSheaf_comap_: Choose an étale chart around the image of y in X. Smoothness of h gives affine neighborhoods W of that image and V of y where h admits an étale chart over relative affine space over W. Shrink W inside the original chart and restrict it. The section ring of W is formally étale over the polynomial ring in its original coordinates. The section ring of V is formally étale over the polynomial ring over the sections of W in the relative coordinates. Composing gives formal étaleness over the polynomial ring over k in both sets of coordinates, where the original coordinates map to the corresponding first set. On V, pullback of each ideal sheaf extends its ideal on W along the section map. The ring-level equality for compatible old and new coordinates identifies the derivative ideal of the extended ideal with the extension of its original derivative ideal. This is the required equality on V.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_pow_mul_mem_of_mem_map: Represent the image of x as a fraction with numerator in N and denominator a power of f. Equality in the localization implies equality after multiplying the cross-multiplied expressions by a further power of f. The resulting product of powers times x belongs to N.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_eq_of_locally_eq: The local equalities give local containments in both directions. Apply the result that local affine containments imply containment on each affine open. The two ideals thus agree on every affine open, which gives equality of the ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_ideal_le_congr: Identify the affine opens by the given equality. The two section rings and their ideal values then coincide, and the stated inclusion transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_ideal_le_of_locally_le: Fix an element x of the ideal of the first sheaf on U. At every point of U choose an affine neighborhood where the local containment holds, then shrink to a common neighborhood principal in both affines. Ideal extension along the restriction preserves that local containment. Thus on the principal open in U the image of x lies in the localized ideal of the second sheaf. Clearing a power of the defining section puts a multiple of x in the second ideal on U. The defining sections of these principal opens generate the unit ideal because the opens cover U. The powers that kill the class of x modulo the second ideal also generate the unit ideal, so that class is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsAlgebraMap_appLE_apply: Evaluate the compatibility of scalar maps with pullback at a.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sectionsAlgebraMap_comp_appLE: Sending a scalar first to W via p and then to V via h pulls the same base global section back along the composite morphism. Functoriality of pullback and restriction identifies this with the structure map for the composite on V.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coord_mul_partialDeriv_map_eq_map_add_su: In the formula summing over all center coordinates, separate the summand at s. It is present because s belongs to the center index set. The remaining sum is over that set with s removed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coord_mul_partialDeriv_map_eq_map_sum: The weighted exceptional partial after pullback and the pullback of the sum of the weighted center partials are both derivations. Compare them on source coordinates. For the exceptional coordinate, either side gives its image. For another center coordinate, the exceptional partial differentiates the exceptional factor, and multiplying it back gives the entire image. Outside the center both derivations vanish. The coordinate values determine the derivations.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.finset_sum_smul_derivation_apply: Evaluation at x distributes over finite sums of derivations and takes a scalar multiple to the same multiple of the value. Apply these two facts term by term.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_derivIdealIterate_le_span_pow_mul: At iteration zero this is the assumed containment. If the next index is at most m, the exceptional exponent at the previous step is positive. Apply the one-step chart estimate with the two preceding iterates as inputs. It takes one more derivative step on both sides and decreases the guaranteed exceptional exponent by one, giving the induction step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_derivIdeal_le_span_pow_mul: Write m = e + 1 and denote the exceptional coordinate by b. For every element of J its pullback is b to the m-th power times an element g of J₁. Its image already lies in the stated ideal since the derivative ideal contains J₁. For derivatives in other center directions the chart formula gives b to the e-th power times a derivative of g. In a direction outside the center it leaves one additional factor of b. The exceptional direction gives b to the e-th power times a sum of multiples of g and its chart derivatives. In each case the remaining factor belongs to the derivative ideal of J₁. The coordinate partials generate all derivations, so the same containment holds for every derivative generator and extends to the whole ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_partialDeriv_eq_pow_mul_of_mem: Differentiate the factorization of φ(f) in direction i. This direction kills the exceptional factor, so it produces the exceptional power times the derivative of g. The chart derivative formula also identifies the same derivative with one exceptional factor times the image of the source derivative. Cancel that factor because it is a nonzerodivisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_partialDeriv_eq_pow_mul_of_notMem: The chart partial in a direction outside the center commutes with the pullback of source functions. It also kills the exceptional coordinate, so applying it to the factorization of φ(f) leaves the full exceptional power multiplying the derivative of g.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_partialDeriv_self_eq_pow_mul: Let b be the exceptional coordinate. Differentiate φ(f) = b to the (e + 1)-st power times g in direction s. The derivative is that power times the partial of g plus (e + 1) times the preceding power times g. Multiply by b and compare with the weighted chart formula, separating the source s term from the other center terms. Each other center term contributes the full power of b times the corresponding new weighted partial of g, by the derivative formula for a nonexceptional center direction. Subtract this sum and cancel one common nonzerodivisor b. Factoring the remaining e-th power yields the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_mem_span_singleton_mul: The element a belongs to the principal ideal it generates, and g belongs to I. Their product belongs to the ideal product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDeriv_map_of_mem: Both sides as functions of f are k-derivations into the chart ring with scalars acting through φ. On the center coordinates different from s, the chart substitutes the product of the new coordinate with the exceptional coordinate. The i-th derivative of this product is the exceptional coordinate when the index is i and zero otherwise. It kills the exceptional coordinate itself and every coordinate outside the center. These are the values of the scaled source partial on all coordinates, which determine the derivation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.partialDeriv_map_of_notMem: Compare the two sides as derivations into the chart ring. A partial in a direction outside the center kills both factors of each transformed center coordinate, since neither has its index. It also kills the unchanged exceptional coordinate. On each coordinate outside the center the map leaves the coordinate unchanged, so the values are the same as in the source. Agreement on coordinates yields equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.add_idealOrder_le_idealOrder_mul: For any finite m and n bounded by the orders of I and J, the two ideals lie in the corresponding powers of the maximal ideal. Their product therefore lies in the power with exponent m + n. Hence every such sum is bounded by the order of the product. The extended-natural addition criterion gives the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.enat_add_le_of_forall_natCast_add_le: If either a or b is infinite, take the finite bound on that argument arbitrarily large and take zero on the other. The hypothesis then makes c infinite, giving the inequality. If both are finite, take their actual values as m and n and apply the hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_idealOrder_eq_coe: A nonzero ideal of a Noetherian local ring has order different from infinity by the Krull intersection argument. Every finite extended natural number is represented by an ordinary natural number.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_bot: The zero ideal is contained in every power of the maximal ideal. The criterion for infinite order therefore applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_eq_top_iff: An extended natural number is infinite exactly when it is at least every natural number. Apply the finite-exponent criterion to each such lower bound to get the equivalent ideal containments.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_eq_zero_iff: An extended natural number is zero exactly when it is less than one. By the order-one criterion, failure of order at least one is equivalent to failure of containment in the maximal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_le_idealOrder_map: Take any finite exponent bounded by the order of I. Extend the containment of I in that power of the source maximal ideal. The image of this power lies in the corresponding power of the target maximal ideal, so the same exponent is bounded by the order of the extended ideal. Comparing all finite lower bounds gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_le_of_le: If a power of the maximal ideal contains J, it also contains I because I is contained in J. The set of exponents defining the order of J is therefore contained in the set defining the order of I. Taking suprema gives the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_ne_top_of_ne_bot: If the order were infinite, the ideal would lie in every power of the maximal ideal. Their intersection is zero by the Krull intersection theorem for Noetherian local rings. This would make the ideal zero, contrary to the hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_sup: The sum of the ideals is contained in a given power of the maximal ideal exactly when both summands are contained in that power. Thus an ordinary exponent is at most the order of the sum precisely when it is at most both individual orders. These finite lower bounds determine the extended order, so it is the minimum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_top: The unit ideal is not contained in the proper maximal ideal, so the order-zero criterion gives order zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_idealOrder_iff: If I is contained in the n-th power of the maximal ideal, then n occurs in the set defining its order and hence is at most the supremum. Conversely, if that containment fails, n is positive because the zeroth power is the unit ideal. The powers are decreasing, so every exponent for which containment holds is less than n. Their supremum is at most n − 1, contradicting the assumed lower bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_maximalIdeal_pow_le_pow: Extension of ideals commutes with ideal products. For exponent zero the inequality is automatic because the target is the unit ideal. At a successor use the product formula, the previous inequality for the lower power, and the assumed containment for the image of the maximal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_idealOrder_le_idealOrder_pow: For exponent zero the lower bound is zero. For a positive exponent, if I has infinite order then its power is contained in I and also has infinite order. If the order of I is finite, say n, then I lies in the n-th power of the maximal ideal. Taking c-th powers yields containment in the power with exponent cn, which gives the bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_le_idealOrder_iff: Apply the finite-exponent criterion at one. The first power of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_le_idealOrder_iff_ne_top: Order at least one is equivalent to containment in the maximal ideal. Every proper ideal of a local ring lies in the maximal ideal, and any ideal contained there is proper. This gives the equivalence.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.add_orderAt_le_orderAt_mul: The product of the sheaves has the product of their ideals in the stalk. Apply the lower bound for the order of a product in that local ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.germ_mem_maximalIdeal_iff_not_mem_basicO: Membership in the basic open means that the germ of f is a unit. In the local ring the nonunits are exactly the maximal ideal, giving the equivalence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.germ_mem_stalkIdeal: The germ of a section of the ideal belongs to its extension along the germ map. That extension is one of the ideals in the supremum defining the stalk ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hom_hom_apply_of_comp_eq: The underlying ring homomorphism of the composite acts by applying f and then g. Evaluate its equality with k at x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealOrder_map_of_inverse: The ring isomorphism carries the maximal ideal onto the target maximal ideal, so the order of an ideal cannot decrease under extension. Apply the same inequality to the inverse map and the extended ideal. The inverse carries that ideal back to J, giving the opposite inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_one_eq_top: The multiplicative identity assigns the unit ideal to every affine open. This is the greatest ideal sheaf.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inter_orderAtLeastLocus_subset_orderAtLe: At a point of the intersection the orders of the factors are at least m and m′. Their sum is at least m + m′ and is bounded above by the order of the product. Thus the product satisfies the summed threshold.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_orderAt_iff: Apply the finite-exponent characterization of ideal order in the local ring at x. The ideal in that characterization is the stalk ideal of I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_algebraMap_eq_maximalIdeal: The extension of J lies in the maximal ideal since J lies in p. Every prime of the localization containing this extension contracts to a prime between J and p, so the contraction is p. The prime correspondence then makes that prime the maximal ideal. The radical of the extended J, as the intersection of the primes containing it, is therefore the maximal ideal. Localization preserves radical ideals, so the extended J is already radical and equals it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_germ_ideal_affineBasicOpen: The section ideal on the basic open is the extension of the ideal on U along restriction. Extension of ideals composes, and restriction followed by the germ at x is the original germ. Hence the two extended ideals coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_germ_ideal_congr: Equal affine opens have the same section ideal and the same germ map at x, independently of the witnesses that x belongs to the open. Extending the ideal therefore yields the same stalk ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_germ_ideal_eq: Choose a neighborhood of x in the intersection that is a basic open in each of the two affine opens. Restricting to this common basic open preserves the germ image of each ideal. The two images there are equal because they use the same open and germ map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_germ_le_stalkIdeal: The chosen germ image is a term in the supremum defining the stalk ideal, so it lies below that supremum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_maximalIdeal_of_inverse: The mutually inverse ring maps preserve and reflect units. They therefore carry the nonunits of the first local ring onto the nonunits of the second. Those sets are the respective maximal ideals, giving the equality of the extended ideal and the target maximal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maximalIdeal_ne_bot_of_not_isField: If the maximal ideal of a local ring is zero, every nonzero element is a unit and the ring is a field. The hypothesis excludes this.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maximalIdeal_not_le_sq: If the maximal ideal were contained in its square, then it would equal its square. It is finitely generated since the ring is Noetherian, and the maximal ideal is the Jacobson radical of the local ring. Nakayama’s lemma would make it zero, contrary to the hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_of_vanishingIdeal_le: The prime contains the vanishing ideal of W, so it belongs to the zero locus of that ideal. This zero locus is the closure of W, which equals W by closedness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_orderAtLeastLocus_iff: The locus is defined by the stated lower bound on the order at the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_orderAtLeastLocus_iff_stalkIdeal_le_: Membership in the locus is the lower bound m on the order. The finite-exponent criterion translates this into containment of the stalk ideal in the m-th maximal-ideal power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_orderAtLeastLocus_one_iff: Membership means order at least one, which is precisely the support criterion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_iff_forall_germ_mem_maximalI: On U the support is the common zero locus of its section ideal. Thus x is in the support exactly when it lies in none of the basic opens of sections of the ideal. For each such section this is equivalent to its germ belonging to the maximal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_iff_stalkIdeal_le_maximalIde: Compute the stalk ideal on any affine neighborhood of x. It is generated by the germs of sections of the ideal. Containment in the maximal ideal is therefore equivalent to all of those germs lying in it, which is the support criterion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_iff_stalkIdeal_ne_top: By the support criterion the stalk ideal must be contained in the maximal ideal. In a local ring this is equivalent to being proper, since every proper ideal is contained in the maximal ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mul_orderAt_le_orderAt_pow: The stalk ideal of the power sheaf is the same power of its stalk ideal. Apply the lower bound for the order of an ideal power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.one_le_orderAt_iff_mem_support: Order at least one is equivalent to containment of the stalk ideal in the maximal ideal. This containment is precisely the condition that x belongs to the support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_one: At each point, membership in the locus of order at least one is equivalent to membership in the support. The two sets therefore coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_of_le: If a point has order at least m′ and m is at most m′, transitivity gives order at least m.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_of_le_ideal: The order of the smaller sheaf ideal is at least the order of the larger one. Hence every point satisfying the threshold for J also satisfies it for I.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_orderAtLeastLoc: At a point in the given locus, multiplying the order bound by c gives a bound of c times m. The order of the c-th power is at least c times the original order, so the point belongs to the required locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_top_eq_empty: The unit ideal sheaf has order zero at every point, which is smaller than the positive threshold m. Thus its locus at that threshold is empty.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_zero: Every order is an extended natural number and hence is at least zero. Every point therefore belongs to this locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_bot: The stalk of the zero ideal sheaf is zero, and the zero ideal lies in all powers of the maximal ideal. Its order is infinite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_of_isIso: A scheme isomorphism is an open immersion. Apply invariance of the order under pullback by an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_comap_of_isOpenImmersion: Choose an affine neighborhood of y and its image under the open immersion. The section rings are isomorphic, and the pulled-back sheaf ideal on the source open is the extension of the ideal on its image. The section isomorphism commutes with the germ maps and the induced stalk isomorphism, so the pulled-back stalk ideal is the image of the original one along that stalk isomorphism. An isomorphism of local rings preserves the ideal order, giving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_idealOrder: By definition the order at x is the ideal order of the stalk ideal at x.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_of_stalkIdeal_eq: Order at x is computed solely from the stalk ideal, which is the same for I and J by assumption.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_one_iff: An extended natural number is one exactly when it is at least one and strictly below two. By the finite-exponent criterion these conditions say the stalk ideal lies in the maximal ideal and does not lie in its square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_one_of_stalkIdeal_eq_maximalI: The local ring at x is Noetherian by localization of a Noetherian affine section ring. Its nonzero maximal ideal is not contained in its square by Nakayama’s lemma. The stalk ideal equals this maximal ideal, so the criterion for order one applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_top_iff: The zero stalk ideal has infinite order. A nonzero stalk ideal on a locally Noetherian scheme has finite order, giving the converse.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_eq_zero_iff_not_mem_support: Order zero means that the stalk ideal is not contained in the maximal ideal. The support criterion identifies this with being outside the support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_le_of_le: Stalk ideals preserve inclusions. Taking the order reverses an ideal inclusion because the smaller ideal lies in every power containing the larger one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_ne_top_of_stalkIdeal_ne_bot: The local ring at x is the localization of the Noetherian section ring of an affine neighborhood, so it is Noetherian. A nonzero ideal in a Noetherian local ring has finite order by the Krull intersection theorem. Apply this to the nonzero stalk ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_sup: Taking stalk ideals takes the sum sheaf to the sum of the two stalk ideals. The order of a sum of ideals is the minimum of their orders.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_top: The stalk of the unit ideal sheaf is the unit ideal. Its ideal order is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_vanishingIdeal_eq_one: At the generic point of the maximal irreducible subset, the stalk of the vanishing ideal equals the local maximal ideal. The latter is nonzero by hypothesis, so its order is one by the locally Noetherian criterion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAt_vanishingIdeal_eq_one_of_not_isF: The nonfield local ring has nonzero maximal ideal. Apply the order-one result for the stalk of the vanishing ideal at the generic point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_bot: Every section ideal of the zero sheaf is zero. Extension along each germ map sends it to zero, and the supremum of these zeros is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_eq_map_germ: The stalk ideal is the supremum of the germ images over all affine neighborhoods. Every one of those images equals the image from the chosen neighborhood U, and U itself is among the terms. Their supremum is therefore that image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_mono: On every affine neighborhood the first section ideal is contained in the second. Extension along the germ map preserves containment, as does taking suprema over the neighborhoods.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_mul: Compute all three stalk ideals using the same affine neighborhood of x. On that open the product sheaf gives the product of the section ideals. Extension along the germ map preserves products, giving the claimed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_pow: For exponent zero both sides are unit ideals. At a successor apply the stalk identity for products to the preceding power and use induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_sup: The local sum estimate gives one inclusion. For the other, each sheaf is contained in the sum sheaf, so monotonicity puts each of their stalk ideals in the stalk ideal of the sum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_sup_le: On each affine neighborhood the sum sheaf gives the sum of the section ideals. Extension along the germ map preserves their sum. Each extended summand lies in its own stalk ideal, so the extended sum lies in the sum of the two stalk ideals. Take the supremum over neighborhoods.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_top: Choose an affine neighborhood of x. The unit section belongs to the unit ideal there, so its germ is one in the stalk ideal. An ideal containing one is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_vanishingIdeal_eq_maximalIdea: Choose an affine open around ξ and let p be its prime there. The stalk ideal is the localization at p of the radical ideal of the inverse image of Z in this affine spectrum. This ideal lies in p. If a prime q containing the ideal lies below p, its point belongs to Z and specializes to ξ. Its closure in X is an irreducible closed subset of Z containing the closure of ξ, which is T. By maximality it equals T, so ξ also specializes to that point. The affine open embedding reflects specialization, so the two primes contain each other and are equal. This proves that p is minimal over the radical ideal, whose localization is consequently the maximal ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.closure_genericPoint: A scheme has a generic point for every irreducible closed subset. The component is irreducible and closed, so the closure of its chosen generic point is the entire component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.disjoint: Suppose the two components share a point. Choose an affine étale chart around it where the support is defined by one coordinate. Both generic points lie in the chart because both specialize to the common point. Their primes are minimal over the coordinate ideal. Indeed a smaller prime containing the coordinate would give a point of the support whose irreducible closure contains the corresponding component, and maximality gives equality. At the common point, the contraction of the ideal generated by the coordinate germ recovers either of these minimal primes by the contraction formula. Thus the two primes and their generic points agree. Their closures are the components, contradicting distinctness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_affineOpen_etaleChart_coordIdeal: At the given point choose a chart in which the support is defined by a coordinate. There are finitely many components of the support and each is closed. Since distinct components are disjoint, the union of the other components is closed and misses the point. Shrink the chart to an affine neighborhood avoiding this union. Every support point in it belongs to the given component. On this neighborhood and on each smaller affine open, the coordinate ideal is radical and has the same vanishing set as the component, so its section ideal equals the component’s vanishing ideal. Extending the equality along each germ map gives the stalk equalities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_fromSpec_mem_and_primeIdealOf_eq: The prime maps into the affine open because that open is the image of its section-ring spectrum. The point’s associated prime maps to the same point. The spectrum map is an open embedding, so injectivity identifies the associated prime with the given prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isIrreducibleComponentOfSupport: Consider the irreducible subsets of the support ordered by inclusion. A nonempty chain has its union as an upper bound. The union is nonempty and stays in the support. If two opens meet it, the chain contains one member containing points from both intersections. Irreducibility of that member gives a point in both opens and hence establishes irreducibility of the union. Apply Zorn’s lemma starting from the singleton of the given point to obtain a maximal irreducible subset containing it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.finite_isIrreducibleComponentOfSupport: The support with its subspace topology is Noetherian, so it has finitely many irreducible components. An ambient irreducible component of the support gives an irreducible subset of that subspace by taking its preimage under the inclusion. A larger irreducible subset in the subspace would have an irreducible image in the support containing the ambient component. Maximality rules out strict enlargement. The assignment is injective because taking the image recovers the ambient subset, giving finiteness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.genericPoint_mem: A point belongs to its own closure. The closure of the generic point equals the component, giving the membership.
