Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_open_cover: Each point of the pulled-back support maps into the original support. Use the inverse image of its original neighborhood, which contains that point. The open restriction of the map gives the local order certificate by hypothesis. Its structural map, pulled-back ideals and memory agree with the required restrictions because the maps through the two open inclusions have equal composites. Apply the localization constructor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_orderCertificat: Apply simultaneous induction to the order and principalization certificates. The elementary constructors remain valid under pullback of supports, ideals and memory. For a principalization certificate built from an order certificate, pull back the factorization and use the induction hypothesis for that order certificate. For both localization cases take inverse images of the specified neighborhoods. For an order certificate built by descent, use the smooth-divisor restriction result and the induction hypotheses for the descended principalization certificates. This supplies the restriction for the given order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_smoothDivisor_c:
For each point of the pulled-back support, choose the inverse image of the original neighborhood of its image. Pull the smooth divisor back to this open. Stability gives smoothness and the support containments pull back. Transport any present auxiliary ideal along the induced map of hypersurfaces, and keep absent values absent.

For an absent ideal the required support preimage is open by the pulled-back openness result. For a present ideal the hypersurface map preserves nonvanishing on components. It also transports the local equality away from memory and, by the all-opens hypothesis on the original hypersurface, the descended principalization certificate. Thus the new data satisfy the descent conditions and give the order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_support_subset: The inverse image of the support lies in the inverse image of memory. The support of the pulled-back ideal is that inverse image, so the memory constructor gives an order certificate on every open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapOrderCertificate_of_two_le: The marking does not change under restriction. Its lower bound still applies, so the large-marking case gives the required order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_mul_: Pullback preserves the ideal product and sends the support of the first factor to its inverse image, which lies in the pulled-back memory. The marking inequality stays the same. A point in the pulled-back target support maps to a point where the second factor has the required order. The order inequality for pullback gives at least that order at the source point. The order certificate for the second factor pulls back by hypothesis. These data assemble the principalization certificate on the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_open: For each point in the pulled-back target support, its image lies in the original support. Choose the given original neighborhood of that image and take its inverse image. The restricted map to the original neighborhood is an open immersion, so the local hypothesis supplies a principalization certificate there. The commuting square of open inclusions identifies its structural map, ideals and memory with the restrictions of the new ambient data. The localization constructor assembles these certificates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_prin: Induct simultaneously on principalization and order certificates, requiring each to restrict along every open immersion. The memory and large-marking cases follow by support containment and the same marking. The factorization case uses the pulled-back product and the induction hypothesis on its order certificate. The localization cases follow by taking inverse images of the chosen covering opens. The descent case follows by pulling back the smooth divisors, optional ideals and descended certificates using the open-immersion stability assumptions. These cases establish the required restriction property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_supp: For any open immersion, the pulled-back target support is the inverse image of the original support. It is contained in the inverse image of memory by the given containment. The memory case therefore gives a principalization certificate on the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapPrincipalizationCertificate_of_two_: The marking is retained on any open and is at least two. The large-marking constructor supplies a principalization certificate for the pulled-back data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapSubscheme_comp: The map of closed subschemes is induced by the given ambient morphism and the pulled-back ideal. The defining compatibility of that map is that its composite with the original inclusion equals the pulled-back inclusion followed by the ambient morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapSubscheme_comp_assoc: Compose the compatibility of the induced subscheme map with the remaining morphism. Associativity gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_comap_eq_comap_morphismRes: The composite through the new subscheme and open into the original ambient scheme agrees with the route through the original subscheme. A point outside the inverse image of memory therefore maps to a point outside the original memory. Choose the neighborhood of that point on which the two original ideals agree. Its inverse image contains the given point. Pull the equality of ideals back along the restricted subscheme map and use the commuting inclusions to identify the result with the asserted local equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpen_preimage_support_comap_morphismRe: The support on the new open is the inverse image of the relevant support on the old open, by compatibility of ideal pullback with the restriction square. The subscheme map commutes with the two inclusions. Thus the further inverse image on the new subscheme is the inverse image of the given open on the old subscheme. It is open by continuity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_comap_morphismRestrict: Restrict the open immersion to the inverse image of the chosen target open. This is again an open immersion, so the smooth divisor pulls back to a smooth divisor by the stability assumption. The open restriction square identifies its composite structural map with the one in the statement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_comap_comapSubscheme: The restricted ambient map is an open immersion, so the induced map of closed subschemes is an open immersion by the stated stability assumption. Componentwise nonvanishing pulls back along it by that same assumption.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_congr: Replace each of the structure map, input ideal, memory and target ideal by its equal value. This gives the required order certificate directly.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_base_comp: A point maps into the given set under the composite exactly when its image under the first map is in the inverse image under the second. This is the nested inverse-image formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_base_preimage_base_of_comp_eq: Each nested inverse image is the inverse image under its composite. Equal composites have the same inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_comapSubsche: The restricted map of hypersurfaces is an open immersion by the stability assumption. Apply the hypothesis giving certificates on all opens of the original hypersurface to that map. The commuting open and subscheme inclusions identify its structural map, inverse image of memory and pullback of the target ideal with the prescribed data. The input ideal is already the required pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_congr: Use the equalities of the structure maps, input ideals, memory sets and target ideals to identify all certificate parameters. The given certificate then has the required data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_morphismRestrict_subset: The open restriction square identifies pulling back the restricted ambient ideal with restricting the pulled-back ideal. Both supports on the new open are therefore inverse images under the restricted map. Pulling back the original containment gives the result.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.comap_iso_hom_comp: The descent case of order certificates has the established invariance under ambient isomorphisms. Apply the certificate transport theorem with that descent result and the given isomorphism to pull back the structural map, ideal, memory, and target ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.comap_iso_of_eq_iso_hom: The order certificate pulls back under the isomorphism by the established descent invariance and the certificate transport theorem. Substitute the stated equality to write its structural map as the specified new map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationCertificate.comap_iso_of: Transport the principalization certificate along the ambient isomorphism using invariance of the order-certificate descent case. The given equality identifies the new structural map with the transported one, yielding the claimed certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_support_comap_iso: Support is the locus where the order is at least one. This locus pulls back along an isomorphism, so the support of the pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapSubschemeIso_hom_comp: The isomorphism was chosen to factor the pulled-back subscheme's inclusion followed by the ambient isomorphism through the original subscheme inclusion. Its forward map therefore satisfies the displayed identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_preimageOpens_ι_comap_iso: Each iterated pullback is the pullback along a composite. The composite through the inverse image inclusion and the ambient isomorphism agrees with the composite through the restricted isomorphism and original open inclusion. Hence the ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_subschemeι_comap_iso: Pullback along a composite equals successive pullback. Compatibility of the subscheme isomorphism with the two closed immersions identifies the two composite maps, giving the stated equality of ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_none_of_map_comap_eq_none: Pullback in an optional ideal changes its value only when an ideal is present. A present ideal yields a present pulled-back ideal. Hence an absent result forces the original optional ideal to be absent.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_eq_some_of_map_comap_eq_some: If the pulled-back optional ideal is present, the original one must also be present. Its original ideal pulls back to the given value because equality of present values identifies their underlying ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_comap_eq_comap_preimageOpe: The identity of the inverse images of memory shows that the image of the given point on the original subscheme lies outside the old memory. Choose the open around that point on which the two original ideals agree. Take its inverse image under the subscheme isomorphism. It contains the given point, and functoriality of ideal pullback along the compatible open and subscheme maps transports the equality to it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_subscheme_comap_comm: The kernel containments allow the forward and inverse ambient maps, restricted to the two closed subschemes, to factor through the opposite closed immersions. Their composites become the respective inclusions because the two ambient maps are inverse. Each inclusion is a monomorphism, so the composites are identities. The forward factorization is the required compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_mem_irreducibleComponents_of_homeo: The image of the component is irreducible by continuity. If an irreducible set contains this image, its inverse image under the homeomorphism is irreducible and contains the original component. Maximality makes that inverse image equal to the original component, so the containing set is the original image. Thus the image is a component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpen_preimage_support_comap_preimageOp: First carry the support of the ideal on the original open back through the open isomorphism. Compatibility of the closed immersions with the induced subscheme isomorphism then identifies the desired inverse image with the inverse image of the given open set along this subscheme isomorphism. It is open by continuity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_comap_iso: The effective Cartier property of the ideal is preserved by transport through an isomorphism. Its closed subscheme is identified with the original smooth divisor over the field. Thus the pulled-back ideal again defines a smooth divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_comap_preimageOpensIso: Pull the smooth divisor back along the isomorphism of the inverse image open with the original open. Compatibility of this isomorphism with open inclusions identifies its structural morphism with the prescribed composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isoInvariantOrderCertificateDescend:
At a point of the pulled-back target support, take the inverse image of the original neighborhood and transport its smooth hypersurface along the open isomorphism. The pullback identities preserve both support containments. For each optional hypersurface ideal, transport a present value along the induced subscheme isomorphism and keep an absent value absent.

When the ideal is absent, the original openness condition transfers by the subscheme isomorphism. When it is present, the original ideal supplies the pulled-back ideal, and nonvanishing on components transfers under the isomorphism. The equality of local ideals away from memory also transfers, because the inverse images of the old and new memory agree under the same identification. Finally the hypothesis for the descended principalization certificates applies to the induced subscheme isomorphism. These transported data meet every condition of the descent constructor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comap_subschemeι_le_ker_subschemeι_c: The two inclusions have kernels equal to their defining ideals. Pulling the pulled-back ideal back along the inverse isomorphism recovers the original ideal. The image–pullback adjunction for that inverse map therefore puts the pulled-back ideal inside the kernel of the composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_subschemeι_le_ker_comap_subschemeι_c: The defining ideal is the kernel of the original subscheme inclusion. The kernel of the composite from the pulled-back subscheme is the image of the pulled-back ideal along the forward map. The image–pullback adjunction contains the original ideal in that image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_comap_iso: If a component of the new scheme were contained in the pulled-back support, its image would be a component of the original scheme, since the ambient isomorphism is a homeomorphism. The image would lie in the original support by the formula for pulled-back supports. This contradicts original nonvanishing on components.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimageOpens_ι_comp_hom: The isomorphism from the inverse image open to the original open is the restriction of the ambient isomorphism. After composing with the original open inclusion it gives the restriction of the ambient map to the inverse image open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_base_comp: A point maps into the set under the composite exactly when its image under the first map belongs to the inverse image under the second. This is the asserted equality of inverse images.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_comap_subschemeι_preimageOpens_: Compose the maps used for the nested inverse images. The compatibility of the subscheme and open isomorphisms says that these composites into the original ambient scheme are equal. Their inverse images of the memory set therefore agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_comap_preima: Apply the hypothesis about principalization certificates to the isomorphism from the pulled-back subscheme to the original one. The inclusion identities identify its structural map with the specified composite. The same identities identify the inverse images of the memory set and the pullback of the target ideal. Substituting gives the required certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subschemeι_comp_preimageOpens_ι_comp_hom: First use compatibility of the open inclusions with the ambient isomorphism. Then use compatibility of the subscheme isomorphism with its closed immersions. Associating these maps gives equality of the two routes to the original ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_iso_subset_of_subset: Both supports are inverse images of their original supports under the same isomorphism. Inverse images preserve the given containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_comap_preimageOpens_subset: Restricting the pulled-back ambient ideal to the inverse image open agrees with pulling its original restriction back by the restricted isomorphism. Pullback along that isomorphism preserves the support containment, giving the claim.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.divisorFamily_apply: The family at the chosen boundary index is obtained by applying the divisor rule to the input. Each strictly smaller request is answered by the supplied assignment, which is exactly the displayed rule.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inputLevelData_isMaxOrderReduction: Induct on the level. At zero there are no natural dimension indices strictly below zero, so the specification holds vacuously. Given the specification for the input at level n, the rule hypotheses give the divisor reduction specifications and their boundary invariance through dimension n. These yield the new order reduction specification. Applying the maximal-order rule gives the maximal-order specification through dimension n for the output. This output is the next input, and being at most n is equivalent to being strictly below n plus one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inputLevelData_reductions_eq_of_dim_lt: Induct on the given dimension bound. Both levels under comparison are positive, so compute their values by applying the next-level construction to the preceding inputs. At dimension bound zero there can be no strictly smaller auxiliary dimension. The next-level comparisons therefore give equality of both reductions. At a successor bound, every strictly smaller auxiliary input has dimension index at most the preceding bound. The preceding levels are still above that bound and are in the given order. Thus induction gives equality of their maximal-order reductions on each auxiliary input. The next-level comparisons use exactly these equalities to show that both current reductions agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inputLevelData_succ: The recursion defines the successor input by applying the next-level construction to the preceding input, which is exactly the preceding output.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inputLevelData_zero: The recursion begins at level zero with the trivial order reduction data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxOrderReduction_outputLevelData: The order reduction of the output level satisfies its specification through the current dimension. The maximal-order rule uses this order reduction, so its specification hypothesis gives the required maximal-order reduction property at that level.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderReduction_outputLevelData: The input level's maximal-order and order reductions satisfy the specification below the current dimension. Thus the rule hypotheses give the boundary divisor reductions and their boundary invariance through the current dimension. Applying the order rule specification to these procedures gives the claimed order reduction property of the output.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.maxOrderFamily_apply: The maximal-order family applies the maximal-order rule to the input and answers each auxiliary request by the supplied order assignment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextLevel_maxOrderReduction: The next level first constructs its new order reduction from the divisor family of the previous maximal-order reduction. It then applies the maximal-order rule with this new order reduction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextLevel_maxOrderReduction_congr: The maximal-order rule consults the new order reduction only on inputs of at most the original dimension index. For each such input the hypothesis gives agreement of the previous maximal-order reductions on all strictly smaller indices. The next-level order reduction comparison thus gives equal replies to every request. Hence the maximal-order rule has the same output.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextLevel_orderReduction: The next level obtains its order reduction by first forming the divisor family with the previous maximal-order reduction and then applying the order rule to that family.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextLevel_orderReduction_congr: For a request from the order rule, the auxiliary marked ideal has dimension index at most that of the original input. Its divisor rule uses the previous maximal-order reduction only on strictly smaller inputs. All those inputs are strictly smaller than the original input, so the two previous reductions agree there by hypothesis. The auxiliary divisor procedures are therefore equal at every request. Applying the same order rule gives equal outputs.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderFamily_apply: The order family applies the order rule to the given input. Its auxiliary procedure uses the supplied divisor assignment at the requested boundary index, on each permitted input.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_eq_nextLevel: The output at a level is obtained by applying the next-level construction to that level's input data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_maxOrderReduction_eq: The maximal-order reduction of the output is constructed by applying the maximal-order rule to the order reduction at the same output level.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_maxOrderReduction_eq_at_: Take the smaller level to be the dimension index of the marked ideal itself. The ideal satisfies this bound by equality, so the comparison with any larger level applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_maxOrderReduction_eq_of_: The two outputs are the inputs at their respective successor levels. The dimension index of the marked ideal is at most the smaller bound, and both successor levels are strictly above that bound. The stabilization theorem for input levels gives equality of their maximal-order reductions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.outputLevelData_orderReduction_eq_orderF: The order reduction of the output level is the order rule applied to its divisor family. At every boundary index that family uses the maximal-order reduction from the input level.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.IsAdmissible.top: Admissibility gives a locally finite-type and quasi-compact structural map to the base field. The finite-dimension result for schemes with those properties applies to the marked ideal's ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_preimage_val_eq: The two closed sets have equal intersections with the open. The intersection with the larger irreducible set is nonempty because the smaller set meets it. This intersection is dense in the larger set and is contained in the smaller closed set. Thus the larger set lies in the smaller one, giving equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_le_natCast_of_lt_top: An element below top in this ordered set is either bottom or an embedded natural number. In the first case zero bounds it, and in the second the corresponding natural number bounds it by equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.natCast_withBot_lt_top: The embedded natural number is below top and distinct from it, so it is strictly below top.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.natCast_withBot_ne_top: A natural number is finite in the extended natural numbers. Adjoining a bottom element preserves the distinction between that finite number and the top element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_lt_top_of_finiteType: A finite-type algebra over the field is a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables. A surjection does not increase Krull dimension, since it identifies prime ideals of the quotient with prime ideals containing the kernel. The polynomial ring has finite dimension by the preceding result, so the quotient does as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_mvPolynomial_lt_top: Induct on the number of variables. With no variables the polynomial ring is the coefficient field and has dimension zero. With one more variable it is a univariate polynomial ring over the preceding multivariate polynomial ring. The polynomial-ring dimension bound is twice the preceding dimension plus one. By induction the preceding dimension is below top, so this bound is still below top.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.subset_closure_inter_of_isPreirreducible: Take a point of the preirreducible set and any open neighborhood of it. That neighborhood meets the set, and so does the given open by hypothesis. Preirreducibility gives a point of the set in both opens. Thus every such neighborhood meets the intersection with the given open, proving the closure assertion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_affineOpen_lt_top: Local finite type of the structural map gives a finite-type map from the sections on the field spectrum to the sections on the affine open. The former ring identifies with the field, so the affine open's coordinate ring is a finite-type algebra over that field. The affine open is homeomorphic to the spectrum of this coordinate ring, whose dimension is finite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_natCast_of_isOpen: Apply the open-cover chain bound with the embedded natural number as the common bound for the dimensions of the open sets.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_iUnion_eq_univ: Take any finite strict chain of irreducible closed subsets. A point of its smallest member lies in some covering open, and this same point lies in every member. Intersect the chain with that open. Each intersection is nonempty, irreducible and closed in the open. The inclusions remain strict because equality of consecutive intersections would, by density in the irreducible sets, identify the two original closed subsets. Thus there is a chain of the same length in that covering open, whose dimension is bounded by the given bound. Taking the supremum over all original chains gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_lt_top_of_finiteType: The field spectrum is quasi-compact, and the inverse image of its whole space is quasi-compact by the given property of the structural map. Hence the affine opens admit a finite subcover of the scheme. Every member has finite dimension by local finite type and the affine-open result. The finite-cover dimension bound then gives finite dimension of the whole scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_lt_top_of_finite_isO: Choose a natural upper bound for the dimension of each covering open. Their finite supremum is still a natural number and bounds every open's dimension. By the chain bound for open covers it bounds the dimension of the whole space. It lies strictly below top, as required.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_lt_top_of_homeomorph: A homeomorphism identifies the posets of irreducible closed sets and preserves the lengths of their strict chains. The two topological Krull dimensions are therefore equal, so finiteness transfers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_primeSpectrum_lt_top: Topological Krull dimension of a prime spectrum equals the ring's Krull dimension. Apply the finite-type algebra bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_spec_lt_top: The underlying space of the affine scheme is the prime spectrum of its coordinate ring. The dimension bound for spectra of finite-type algebras therefore applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.two_mul_add_one_lt_top: Since the element is distinct from top, it is bottom or an embedded natural number. In the bottom case multiplying by the nonzero element two and adding one still gives bottom. In the finite case the result is the embedded natural number given by twice the number plus one. Both are strictly below top.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.two_mul_natCast_add_one: For embedded finite numbers, multiplication and addition agree with multiplication and addition of natural numbers before embedding. This gives the equality for twice the given number plus one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.two_ne_zero_withBotENat: Two and zero are distinct natural numbers. Both embeddings into the extended naturals and then into the order with a bottom element are injective, so their images remain distinct.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.specMapOfFieldHom_eq: The map of field spectra is defined by taking the spectrum morphism induced by the given field homomorphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.comap_iso: The simultaneous induction proves transport of the order certificate along any isomorphism under the stated descent assumption. Apply it to this isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.comap_iso_of_eq: Use the order certificate transport theorem for the isomorphism, then identify its composite structural map with the new one by the given equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationCertificate.comap_iso: The simultaneous transport theorem applies to the given principalization certificate. Evaluate it at the specified scheme and isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationCertificate.comap_iso_of: Pull the certificate back along the isomorphism by the transport theorem. The equality of structure maps lets that certificate be viewed over the stated new structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_support_comap_iso_hom: A point belongs to the support of the pulled-back ideal exactly when its image belongs to the original support. This identifies the support with the inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_preimageOpensIso_hom: Both iterated pullbacks are pullbacks along composites. The identity for the restricted isomorphism and its inclusions makes those composites equal, so the ideal sheaves agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_resLE_of_iso: Restricting the ambient isomorphism to the inverse image of an open is the base change of that isomorphism to the open. Base changes of isomorphisms are isomorphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso: Induct simultaneously on order and principalization certificates with the assertion that each transports under every isomorphism. The memory and marking cases use the underlying pulled-back support and the same marking. The principalization factorization case transmits the factorization and the smaller order certificate. The localization cases transport through isomorphic opens. For a descent step, the assumed invariance applies using the transported principalization certificates supplied by induction. This proves transport for the order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso_of_opens_cove: Every point of the new target support maps to one of the original support points. Use the inverse image of its specified open neighborhood. The local order certificate transports through the restriction of the ambient isomorphism. Its structure map, ideals and memory match those of the new open because the inclusions commute with the isomorphism. The localization constructor assembles the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso_of_smoothDivi: The assumed invariance of the descent step applies to the given local smooth divisors, support conditions and auxiliary ideals. It takes the original descended principalization certificates together with their transported versions supplied by the hypothesis. Its conclusion is precisely the order certificate after the ambient isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso_of_support_su: Under the isomorphism the support becomes the inverse image of the original support. It remains inside the inverse image of memory, so the order certificate follows from the memory case.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_comap_iso_of_two_le: The marking stays at least two under pullback. The large-marking constructor therefore supplies the transported order certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_congr: Use the four equalities to identify the parameters of the two certificates. The original order certificate has the required parameters after substitution.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimageOpensIso_hom: The isomorphism of the inverse image open with the given open is constructed from the restricted ambient map, which is therefore its forward map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimageOpensIso_hom_comp_ι: The isomorphism between the opens is the restriction of the ambient isomorphism. Composing it with the original open inclusion agrees with following the inverse image inclusion by the ambient map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimageOpensIso_hom_comp_ι_comp: Postcompose the equality for the restricted isomorphism and open inclusions with the structural map. Associativity gives the stated identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_comp_base: A point lies in the successive inverse images exactly when its image under the composite lies in the set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_preimageOpensIso_hom: Each nested inverse image is the inverse image along the corresponding composite into the original scheme. Those composites agree by compatibility of the open isomorphism with inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_comap_iso: Use simultaneous induction on principalization and order certificates, asking for transport along every isomorphism. Support containments, markings and products are preserved, which gives the memory, large-marking and factorization cases using the relevant induction hypotheses. Charts in the two localization cases transport by inverse image and the restricted isomorphism. The descent case follows from the assumed invariance for smooth divisors applied to the original principalization certificates on the hypersurfaces and their transported versions. These cases prove the required transport.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_comap_iso_of: For a point of the new support, its image lies in the original support. Take the inverse image of the chosen original neighborhood. The local hypothesis transports its principalization certificate along the restricted isomorphism. The open inclusion compatibility identifies the transported structure map, ideals and memory with the desired local data. These local certificates give the new global certificate by localization.

The ideal factorization persists under pullback. The support of the first factor is the inverse image of its old support and remains in the pulled-back memory. Order loci are preserved under the isomorphism, so the pulled-back target support satisfies the order bound for the second factor. Together with the same marking inequality and the transported order certificate from the hypothesis, these give the transported principalization certificate.

The pulled-back target support is the inverse image of the original support. It lies in the inverse image of memory by the given containment, which yields a principalization certificate by the memory case.
The isomorphism transport retains the marking. Since that marking is at least two, use the large-marking principalization constructor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_congr: Substitute the equal structure map, input ideal, memory set and target ideal. The given certificate is then a certificate for the specified data.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_irreducibleClosedsImageVal: The irreducible closed set in the larger space is constructed as the image of the given set under the inclusion of the closed subspace. Its underlying set is this image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_irreducibleClosedsMapOfHomeomorph: The transported irreducible closed set is defined by taking the image under the homeomorphism. Its underlying subset is that image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_mem_irreducibleComponents_superse: Extend the given irreducible set to a maximal preirreducible subset. It is nonempty because it contains the original set, hence irreducible. Its closure is preirreducible and contains it, so maximality makes it closed. The same maximality makes it an irreducible component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.irreducibleClosedsImageVal_subset: Every point in the image of the closed subspace inclusion is a point of that subspace, so the image of the specified set is contained in the subspace.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_lt_of_homeomorph_isClosed: The closed subset has strictly smaller topological Krull dimension because it is nonempty and contains no ambient irreducible component. The given homeomorphism transfers its dimension to the scheme in the statement. Since the greater dimension is finite, passing to successor indices preserves the strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_lt_of_topologicalKrullDim_l: The dimension index is given by the successor conversion of topological Krull dimension. The monotonicity result for that conversion preserves the strict inequality because the greater dimension is below top.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonempty_irreducibleCloseds: The closure of the singleton of the given point is closed and irreducible, since singletons are irreducible and closure preserves irreducibility. It is nonempty because it contains the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictMono_irreducibleClosedsImageVal: Taking images preserves inclusions. Since the subspace inclusion is injective, equality of images would imply equality of the original sets. Strict inclusions therefore remain strict.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictMono_irreducibleClosedsMapOfHomeom: Images under the homeomorphism preserve inclusions, and injectivity makes equality of images imply equality of the original sets. Hence the image operation preserves strict inclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_length: Topological Krull dimension is defined as the supremum of the lengths of finite strict chains of irreducible closed sets. This gives the displayed expression.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_homeomorph: The homeomorphism sends chains to chains of the same length, giving one dimension inequality. Its inverse gives the reverse inequality, so the dimensions agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_homeomorph: The homeomorphism sends irreducible closed sets to irreducible closed sets and preserves strict inclusions. Every finite strict chain in the first space therefore has an image chain of the same length in the second. Taking suprema gives the dimension inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_lt_of_isClosed_of_no:
Take a finite strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of the closed subspace. Its images are irreducible and closed in the ambient space and remain a strict chain because the inclusion is injective. The last image lies in some ambient irreducible component. No component is contained in the subspace, so this containment is strict. Appending the component produces an ambient chain one step longer.

The subspace has a point, whose closure gives a chain of length zero. The extended chain shows the ambient dimension is at least one. Since the ambient dimension is finite, write it as a positive natural number. Every chain in the subspace has length at most one less than that number by the extension argument. Their supremum is therefore strictly smaller than the ambient dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBotSuccToNat_lt_withBotSuccToNat: The upper value is below top and has a smaller value, so it is an embedded finite natural number. Its successor index is positive. If the lower value is bottom, its index is zero. Otherwise it too is finite and its natural value is strictly smaller, so adding one to both values preserves strict inequality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.dim_baseChange: Admissibility makes the original structure map smooth. Extending the field preserves the ambient topological Krull dimension by the comparison for smooth schemes. Applying the common successor conversion gives equality of the marked ideals' dimension indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_bot_of_formallyUnramified_of_comap_le:
Localize the target domain at the images of elements outside the kernel prime of the base. These images are nonzero, so the localization remains a domain and the localization map is injective. The base map to the localization kills the kernel prime and inverts every nonzero class modulo that prime. It therefore factors through the fraction field of the quotient base. The localized domain is essentially of finite type and formally unramified over that field by the corresponding composition and restriction properties. It is consequently a field.

The prime in the statement avoids the inverted elements because its contraction is contained in the kernel prime. It therefore extends to a proper prime in the localization. If it contained a nonzero element, that element would remain nonzero by injectivity and become a unit in the field. This would put one in the extended prime, a contradiction. Thus the original prime is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_le_of_comap_eq: Quotient the target by the smaller prime. The resulting domain is still essentially of finite type and formally unramified over the base. The kernel of the new base map is the contraction of the smaller prime. The image of the larger prime is prime in the quotient, and its contraction is contained in the kernel prime by the given equality of contractions. The domain result makes this image prime zero. Hence the larger prime lies in the smaller one and they are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etaleChart_dim_le_topologicalKrullDim: Choose a closed point of the nonempty affine chart. At that point the local ring is Noetherian, and the local dimension theorem for an étale chart identifies its dimension with the number of coordinates. That local ring agrees with the ambient local ring at the same point. The dimension of any ambient local ring is at most the topological dimension of the scheme, giving the bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isField_of_formallyUnramified: Pass from the domain to its fraction field. Localization is formally unramified and essentially of finite type, and both properties are preserved by composition over the base field. For this field extension formal unramifiedness gives separability, hence algebraicity. Every element of the domain is then integral over the base field because the domain embeds in its fraction field. A domain integral over a field is a field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyNoetherian_of_smooth_over_field: Sections on each affine open of a smooth scheme over a field are a finite-type algebra over that field and hence Noetherian. This is the local Noetherian condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherianRing_stalk_of_opens: The stalk map of an open inclusion is a ring isomorphism. It transfers Noetherianity of the ambient local ring to the local ring on the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_eq_of_topologicalKrullDim_e: The dimension index is the same successor conversion of topological Krull dimension for both schemes. Applying that conversion to the given equality gives equal indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_le_of_etale: The étale dimension inequality bounds the source by the target. Since the target dimension is finite, the conversion to successor indices preserves the weak inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_le_of_essFiniteType_formall: Every finite strict chain of target primes contracts to a strict chain of the same length by the contraction result. Taking the supremum of chain lengths gives the dimension bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_le_of_isLocalization_etale: The given étale ring map is finite type and formally unramified. Composing with localization of the target gives a map from the original source ring to the localized target that is essentially of finite type and formally unramified. The commutative diagram factors this map through the localized source. These two properties pass to that factor over the localized source by the localization and composition results. The dimension bound for essentially finite-type formally unramified maps now applies to the given local rings.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_of_etaleChart_of_i: The local ring of the chart domain is Noetherian because it is isomorphic to the ambient local ring. An étale morphism to affine space bounds the dimension of that local ring by the number of coordinates. Transfer the bound to the ambient local ring through the open-inclusion isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_le_of_etale_of_isNoet: Choose an affine neighborhood of the target point and an affine neighborhood of the source point within its inverse image. The latter can be taken to be a basic open of an initial affine neighborhood. On sections the induced map is étale. The local rings are localizations of those section rings at the relevant primes, and the germ maps commute with the map on stalks. Apply the dimension inequality for localizations of an étale map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringKrullDim_stalk_opens: The inclusion of an open subscheme induces an isomorphism of the local rings at corresponding points. Isomorphic rings have the same Krull dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictMono_comap_of_formallyUnramified: Contraction preserves inclusion of primes. For a strict inclusion, equal contractions would force the two primes to be equal by the preceding prime comparison theorem. Thus contraction preserves strict inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_base_pullback_fst_specMapOfFi: A field spectrum is a single point, so the map of field spectra is surjective. The projection in question is its base change, and surjectivity is preserved by base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_le_of_etale: An étale morphism is locally of finite type, so its source is locally Noetherian because its target is. At each source point the dimension of the local ring is at most the dimension of the target local ring by the étale stalk bound. The latter is at most the topological dimension of the target. Bounding every source local ring in this way bounds the source's topological dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_pullback_specMapOfFi: The projection of the field base change is surjective by stability of surjectivity under base change. The dimension comparison for a smooth scheme with such a projection therefore gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.topologicalKrullDim_pullback_spec_map_of:
The original and extended schemes are smooth over their fields, hence locally Noetherian. For a point of the extended scheme, choose an affine étale chart around its image and pull this chart back to the extended scheme. The extended local dimension is at most the chart's number of coordinates, which is at most the original scheme's dimension by the bound for nonempty affine charts. This bounds the extended scheme's dimension from above.

For the reverse direction, choose an affine étale chart at any point of the original scheme and use surjectivity to choose a point above it. The original local dimension is at most the number of chart coordinates. The extended chart has that same number and is nonempty and affine, so this number is at most the extended scheme's dimension. The bounds on all original local rings give the reverse inequality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSequence_center: The ambient center at a stage is defined by taking the image of the original center ideal through its stage embedding.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSequence_isoObjZero: Since the initial ambient is the given ambient itself, the construction uses its identity isomorphism at stage zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSequence_length: The ambient blowup sequence is assigned the same number of active steps as the original sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupSequence_schemeAt_zero: The recursive ambient sequence starts with the given ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_imageIdealSheaf_of_isClosedImmersi: The image ideal sheaf is the image of the original ideal along the closed immersion. Pulling this image back along the closed immersion recovers the original ideal by the ideal image formula for closed immersions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbientBlowupSequence_succ_: The two maps at consecutive stages are the recursive embeddings, with the ambient transition given by the successor construction. Its compatibility with the original transition is the successor commutative square already established.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoAmbientBlowupSequence_zero: The initial embedding is defined as the original sequence's stage-zero isomorphism followed by the given ambient immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddingIntoBlowupImageIdealSheaf_comp_: The chosen immersion identifies the source blowup with the strict transform in the ambient blowup over the preceding embedded scheme. Its projection to the old ambient is therefore the source transition followed by the old embedding.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_closedImmersion_blowup_imageIdeal: At a valid stage the transition is a blowup of the specified center. The ambient is Noetherian and hence locally Noetherian. Apply the result on embedding a blowup into the ambient blowup of the image ideal, using the given closed immersion and center condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_closedImmersion_blowup_of_isBlowu: Push the center ideal forward through the closed immersion. Its pullback is the original center ideal. If an irreducible component of the embedded scheme mapped entirely into the pushed-forward center support, the support pullback identity would put it inside the original center support, contrary to the hypothesis. The strict-transform blowup theorem therefore identifies the ambient strict transform of the embedded scheme as a blowup along the original center. The given source is also such a blowup, so their universal properties give mutually inverse maps over the embedded scheme. Compose this isomorphism with the inclusion of the ambient strict transform. This is a closed immersion compatible with both blowup projections. Its kernel is the strict-transform ideal because the first map is an isomorphism and the second is the inclusion defined by that ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_ambientBlowupMor: The transition map of the recursive ambient sequence is the successor ambient map at the chosen stage. At every valid index this map is a blowup along the image of the current center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_succAmbientEmbed: At an active step the construction uses the canonical projection from the blowup of the image of the center ideal. This projection is a blowup along that image ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_embeddingIntoAmbientBl: Every stage of the recursive ambient construction supplies a closed immersion. At zero it is the original immersion composed with the initial isomorphism, at an actual successor it is the strict-transform immersion, and beyond the active stages the construction uses the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_embeddingIntoBlowupIma: The chosen next-stage embedding is the one supplied by the ambient blowup comparison, which is a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_isoObjZero_hom_comp: The stage-zero isomorphism is a closed immersion, and the original embedding is a closed immersion by hypothesis. The property is preserved by composition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_ambientBlowupSequence_schem: The initial ambient is Noetherian, and each actual subsequent ambient arises by blowing up the preceding Noetherian ambient along the image center. The preservation assumption gives Noetherianity throughout the stated range.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_blowup_of_isNoetherian: The canonical projection is a blowup along the given ideal. The assumed Noetherian preservation for blowups applies because its target is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPushforwardBlowupSeq_ambientBlowupSequ: The two sequences have equal length. Take the recursive closed immersion at every stage. At zero it agrees with the original immersion through the initial isomorphisms. The successor squares commute by the stage compatibility. Each ambient center is the image of the original center, and the defining ideal of each successor embedding is the corresponding strict transform. These are the required pushforward comparison data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoAmbientBlowupSequence_s: At this actual step, the next stage is embedded as the strict transform of the previous stage in the ambient blowup. The successor kernel formula therefore identifies its ideal with the strict transform along the ambient map and center of that step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_embeddingIntoBlowupImageIdealSheaf: The chosen new embedding has image the ambient strict transform of the preceding embedded scheme. Its defining kernel is the strict transform of the preceding embedding ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_succAmbientEmbedding_eq_strictTransf: At a valid step the new embedding is the chosen strict-transform embedding, and the ambient map is the canonical blowup of the image center. The kernel calculation for that embedding gives the stated strict transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_support_subset_support_comap: The support of a pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support. In particular, the indicated inverse image is contained in it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.succAmbientEmbedding_comp_blowupMorphism: At an active step the compatibility follows from the chosen embedding into the ambient blowup. After the active range, the new embedding is the identity and the new ambient map is the source transition followed by the old embedding. The same equality then follows from the identity law.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.boundary_length: At zero the pullback of the original list has its original length. At each successor, taking strict transforms preserves the length and appending the exceptional ideal increases it by one. Induction gives the original length plus the number of steps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.boundary_succ: The successor boundary first takes the strict transforms of the ordered preceding list and then appends the exceptional ideal of the transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.boundary_zero: The boundary recursion starts by pulling back every member of the original ordered boundary along the stage-zero isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.controlledTransform_s: For the successor pull back the preceding transform along the transition and take its residual ideal with respect to the exceptional ideal raised to the marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.controlledTransform_z: The recursion begins with the original ideal pulled back along the stage-zero isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.eq_of_pow_exceptional: At the valid stage the map is a blowup, whose exceptional ideal is locally generated by non-zero-divisors. The cancellation theorem for powers of such ideals gives equality of the two factors.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.pow_exceptionalIdeal_: The successor transform is the selected residual ideal. The given divisibility supplies a factorization, so multiplying that selected ideal by the exceptional power recovers the pulled-back preceding transform.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.BlowupSequenceData.toMarkedBlowupSequenc: The marked sequence retains the original transition map at the given stage.
The marked data use the boundary list produced by the boundary recursion at the given stage.
The center of the marked sequence is the original center at the specified stage.
The ideal assignment of the marked data is defined to be the recursively computed controlled transform.
The marked construction keeps the length of the underlying blowup sequence.
The projection of the marked sequence data is assigned to be the projection to the base of the underlying blowup data.
The marked construction uses the same scheme at every stage as the original sequence data.
The construction adds marking, ideals, boundary and compatibility data to the given blowup sequence. Its underlying blowup sequence data are the original data.
Passing from marked data to the sequence retains the underlying ordinary blowup data. Applying the ordinary sequence construction to those data therefore gives the original sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_and_boundary_eq: At each valid step any two residual factors satisfying the marked transition equation have equal products with the same exceptional power. This power can be cancelled by the blowup cancellation theorem. Thus the uniqueness hypothesis of the simultaneous ideal and boundary comparison holds.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.controlledTransform_and_boundary_eq_of_c: Induct on the stage. The initial ideal and boundary from the recursions coincide with the marked data's initial pullbacks. At a successor, the recorded next ideal is a residual factor for the pulled-back previous ideal by the marked transition equation. The recursively chosen ideal satisfies the same equation, because that factorization exists and the preceding ideals agree by induction. The assumed cancellation identifies the two residual factors. The boundary recursions agree because both take the same strict transforms of the equal old lists and append the same exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor: At every point cancel the common locally principal factor in the stalk by the non-zero-divisor argument. Equal stalk ideals give equal ideal sheaves.
The power of the common factor is still locally generated by non-zero-divisors. Apply the cancellation theorem to that power.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_span_singleton_mul_eq_mul: The cancellation argument gives containment of the first ideal in the second. Apply it to the reversed product equality to obtain the reverse containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_of_stalkIdeal_eq: On any affine open, the localizations of its two section ideals at a maximal ideal are the corresponding stalk ideals. These are equal by hypothesis. Ideals in a ring are determined by their localizations at all maximal ideals, so the section ideals on every affine open are equal. They determine the ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_excep: The exceptional ideal is the center ideal pulled back to the blowup. For a blowup this pullback is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor, giving the asserted property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isLocallyGeneratedByNonZeroDivisor_pow: On an affine neighborhood where the ideal is generated by a non-zero-divisor, its power is generated by the same power of that element. Powers of non-zero-divisors are non-zero-divisors, giving the required local generators.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMarked_toBlowupSequenceData: At every active step take the recorded successor ideal as the divisibility witness, using equality of the recorded preceding ideal with its recursive controlled transform. The same equality transfers the center's order condition. The projections to the base agree with those of the marked sequence, so the center's smoothness carries over. The recursive and recorded boundaries agree as well, so the same center has the required strict normal crossing condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_span_singleton_mul_eq_mul: Take an element of the first ideal. Its product with the given generator belongs to the product of the principal ideal and the first ideal, hence also to the product with the second ideal by equality. It is therefore the generator times an element of the second ideal. Cancel the generator using that it is a non-zero-divisor. The initial element lies in the second ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_boundary: The marked sequence data retain the sequence's boundary list at each stage. Its comparison with the boundary recursion yields the required equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofMarkedSequence_controlledTransform: The data associated to a marked sequence retain its stage ideals. Apply the comparison with the recursive controlled transform to those data at the specified valid stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_eq_toBlowupSequenceData: Both projections at zero are the chosen initial isomorphism. For a successor both compose the same transition map with the preceding projection. Induction therefore gives equality at every index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_eq_of_mul_eq_mul: Near the given point the common factor is generated by a non-zero-divisor on an affine open. Its germ remains a non-zero-divisor because the stalk is a localization there. Taking stalks of the equality of products gives equality of the products of the stalk ideals with the principal ideal of this germ. Cancel the principal ideal to conclude.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupSequenceData_boundary_eq_boundar: The simultaneous comparison gives equality of the recursive boundary and the original marked boundary at this stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupSequenceData_controlledTransform: The simultaneous comparison of the recursive and recorded data gives equality of the two ideals at the specified valid stage.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dimensionNonincreasingAlongBlowups: Induct on the stage of the marked sequence. At zero the scheme is isomorphic to the original ambient, so their dimension indices agree. At a successor the preceding marked ideal is admissible and its scheme is locally of finite type and quasi-compact over the field. The center has strict normal crossings with the boundary and the transition is its blowup. The blowup dimension inequality therefore bounds the successor dimension index by the preceding one. Compose with the induction bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_eq_krullDimSucc_of_iso: A scheme isomorphism induces a homeomorphism of the underlying spaces. Their topological Krull dimensions agree, so applying the successor conversion gives equal dimension indices.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_eq_filterNeTop: Both list filters keep an entry exactly when its ideal differs from the unit ideal. They therefore produce the same sublist.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.validOfSameNontrivialBoundary: Replacing the boundary retains the field, scheme, structure map, ideal and marking. The old and new lists agree after deleting unit ideals. The strict normal crossing criterion under this agreement therefore transfers the one admissibility condition involving the boundary. All other conditions are inherited.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_eq: The new boundary is defined by taking the strict transform of each entry of the old list in order and then appending the exceptional ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_succ_eq_map_strictTransform_app: The transition rule in the sequence takes the strict transforms of the entries of the current boundary and appends the exceptional ideal of the step. Apply that rule at the given valid index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_eq:39: The exceptional ideal of a blowup is the pullback of the center ideal along the blowup map. This is the exceptional ideal of the given step.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_eq:94: At this stage the exceptional ideal is the center ideal pulled back by the transition map of its blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_center: The sequence's center condition gives strict normal crossings with the current boundary at every valid index. Apply it at the specified stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastBoundary_eq: The last boundary is the boundary at the final index, which is the length of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastIdeal_eq: The last ideal is defined by evaluating the stage ideals at the length of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_center_subschemeι: The sequence includes smoothness of each actual center over the field. The composite in that condition is exactly the center inclusion followed by this stage's structure morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_def: The structural map at this stage is the projection to the original scheme followed by that scheme's morphism to the field spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_eq: The structure morphism of the blown-up scheme is defined by following its blowup map with the original structure morphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPositionAt_comap_i: Choose an étale coordinate chart for the boundary at the image point. Pull its open back along the isomorphism and compose the restricted isomorphism of opens with the chart. The composite is étale and respects the new structure map. Keep the same assignment of coordinates to the boundary entries. Distinct assigned coordinates remain distinct, since pullback preserves the list's positions. An entry described by the unit ideal remains the unit ideal. An entry described by one coordinate ideal pulls back to that coordinate ideal under the composite chart, by functoriality of ideal pullback. This is the required local normal crossing presentation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_boundary: Induct on the stage. At zero, the boundary is pulled back from the original one along the isomorphism at stage zero, so it has strict normal crossing position. At a successor the underlying space is Noetherian by hypothesis. The preceding boundary has strict normal crossings by induction, and the current center satisfies the normal crossing condition with it. The blowup boundary theorem gives strict normal crossing position for the strict transforms with the exceptional divisor appended. This is exactly the successor boundary with its successor structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_boundary_: Every actual stage of the sequence is Noetherian because the starting scheme is Noetherian, so its underlying space is Noetherian. These bounds supply the Noetherian hypotheses of the boundary induction theorem.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comp_iso_: The local chart transport gives strict normal crossing coordinates at every point of the new scheme. For any boundary entry these charts give either the unit ideal or the ideal of a single coordinate near each point. The local coordinate criterion makes each entry a smooth divisor. Along with the pointwise presentation, this gives strict normal crossing position globally.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt: The underlying sequence of blowups begins on a Noetherian scheme. The theorem on Noetherianity along blowup sequences applies to every stage up to its length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_structureMorphism: Induct on the stage within the sequence. At zero the structure map is the original smooth map preceded by an isomorphism. For the successor, the preceding stage is smooth over the field by induction. Its center has strict normal crossings with the boundary, so the theorem for blowup of such a center gives smoothness of the successor over the field. The successor formula identifies its map with that composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_succ: The projection of the successor stage to the base is its transition map followed by the preceding projection. Compose this identity with the original structure map to obtain the successor formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.structureMorphism_zero: The projection of stage zero to the base is its chosen isomorphism with the original scheme. Following this with the original structure morphism gives the formula.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.centersContainNoComponent_ofMarkedSequen: At a valid stage the transformed ideal is nonzero on components by the preceding induction. Every center point lies in its locus of order at least the marking. Since the marking is at least one, this locus lies in the support of the ideal. A whole component in the center would therefore lie in that support, which is impossible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_support_comap_eq_preimage: The support of the pulled-back ideal sheaf is the inverse image of its original support. Taking underlying sets gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.effectiveCartierSupportContainsNoCompone: A divisor ideal locally generated by a non-zero-divisor avoids the generic point of each irreducible component. Equivalently, its support contains no irreducible component. Apply this effective Cartier divisor property to the given ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_irreducibleComponent_subset_of_se: Intersect the source component with the inverse image of the given open. It is a nonempty open in that irreducible component. Its image is irreducible, so choose a target irreducible component containing it. This target component meets the open, and their intersection is irreducible. Its inverse image in the source is the continuous image of that intersection under the section, because the section is inverse to the map over the open. Thus this inverse image is irreducible and contains the open part of the source component. Its closure then contains the entire source component by density. Maximality makes that closure equal to the source component. Consequently the target component's open part maps back into the source component and lies in the given closed target set. Its density in the target component puts the whole target component in that closed set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_section_off_center: The blowup is an isomorphism over the complement of the center. Take the map on points of its inverse there and include its values in the blowup scheme. This map is continuous. The two inverse identities for the restriction give a section on that open and show that its image contains every blowup point lying above the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPreirreducible_inter_of_isOpen: Take two opens meeting the intersection. Intersect each open with the given open. The two resulting opens meet the original preirreducible set, so they meet it in common. This point also belongs to the original intersection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPreirreducible_preimage_val: Two opens in the subspace come from opens in the larger space. If they both meet the preimage of the given set, their ambient opens meet that set. Preirreducibility yields a common point in the given set, which lies in the subspace by containment. This proves preirreducibility in the subspace.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_comap_iso_hom: The support pulls back under the isomorphism, and the corresponding homeomorphism sends each irreducible component to an irreducible component. The isomorphism invariance of componentwise nonvanishing gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_ideal_of_isAdmissibl: Induct on the stage. The initial ideal is pulled back from the admissible marked ideal along the stage-zero isomorphism, preserving nonvanishing on components. For the successor, the controlled-transform identity multiplies the new ideal by the exceptional ideal to the power of the marking to obtain the pulled-back preceding ideal. The exceptional ideal is the pulled-back center ideal. The nonvanishing result for this identity applies to the blowup and induction hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_of_pow_mul_eq_comap: Suppose an irreducible component of the blowup were in the support of the transformed ideal. The given formula makes the pulled-back original ideal a product with this transform, whose stalk ideals are contained in those of the transform. Thus the component lies in the pullback of the original support. The exceptional ideal is effective Cartier, so its support does not contain the component. Choose a point of the component off that support. Its image is off the original center, where the blowup has an inverse section covering the entire inverse image. The component comparison for a map with such a section produces a component of the original scheme contained in the original support, contradicting componentwise nonvanishing.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EtaleChart.ofIso_coordIdeal: A chart coordinate ideal is the corresponding coordinate ideal of affine space pulled back along the chart map. The transported chart map first uses the restricted isomorphism and then the original chart. Functoriality of pullback gives the original chart ideal pulled back along that restricted isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapIsoInvariance: The order locus comparison supplies transport of the cosupport. The chart argument supplies transport of the center's crossing condition with the boundary, and the pullback of the closed subscheme gives smoothness of the transported center. The kernel description of strict transform gives its compatibility with the isomorphism. These four statements are the required invariance properties.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.etale_resLE_comp_map_of_iso: The restricted ambient isomorphism is étale, as is the original chart map. Their composite is étale.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isIso_subschemeι_eq_comp_of_eq_ke: Replace the ideal by the kernel of the closed immersion. Its canonical subscheme inclusion and the given closed immersion then have the same kernel. The lifting property factors each inclusion through the other. Their two composites become the original inclusions after composition, so monomorphism of both inclusions makes the factors inverse. This gives the isomorphism and the required compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_comap_iso: A point of the pulled-back center support maps to the original center support, so choose normal crossing coordinates for the center and boundary there. Transfer the chart to the inverse image open using the restricted ambient isomorphism. Keep the same coordinate indices for the center and list entries. Unit boundary ideals are preserved by pullback, and each original equation expressed by a coordinate ideal becomes the same equation for the transported chart. This applies both to boundary entries and to the center, giving the required normal crossing condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_resLE_iso_hom: The inverse scheme map takes the original open into the inverse image open because the two maps are inverse. Restrict it to give the candidate inverse to the restricted forward map. After composing with the respective open inclusions the two composites are identities by ambient compatibility. Since the open inclusions are monomorphisms, the restricted maps are inverse.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_hom_base_inv_base_apply: The inverse followed by the forward isomorphism is the identity of the target. Apply the induced maps to the specified target point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_inv_base_hom_base_apply: The forward isomorphism followed by its inverse is the identity, so their maps on points have the stated composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofIso_map_comp_affineSpaceFinToSpec: The original chart has structure map given by the open inclusion followed by the original structural map. Precompose with the restricted isomorphism, then use its compatibility with the two open inclusions. This gives the structure map of the inverse image open.
