Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_comap_iso_hom_eq_preim: The order inequality for pullback compares the original order at the image point with the pulled-back order. Apply it also to the inverse isomorphism. The inverse sends the image point back and pulls the ideal back to the original ideal, giving the reverse order inequality. Thus the two orders agree, and the loci of order at least the given marking correspond by inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_comap: Restriction of an ideal to an open is pullback along the open inclusion. The two composites from the new open to the original ambient agree because the open restriction square commutes. Pulling back the ideal along these composites gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_comap_iso: Pull back the closed center inclusion along the ambient isomorphism. The second projection of the pullback is an isomorphism to the old center, while the first is a closed immersion with the pulled-back defining ideal. The closed subscheme of that ideal is isomorphic to this pullback over the new ambient. Thus its structure map is the old center's smooth structure map preceded by the composite isomorphism of centers, and is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_comp_iso_hom: Pulling back the center and divisor ideals along the composite is the same as first pulling them back along the isomorphism and then along the given map. The constructions of the strict-transform open and the subscheme immersion use exactly these two pullbacks. The corresponding immersions therefore have the same kernel, which is their strict transform ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_iteratedComap: Induct on the stage up to the given bound. The initial divisor is smooth by hypothesis. At a successor, both ambient structural maps are smooth and the transition is a blowup whose center is disjoint from the preceding divisor. The smooth-divisor pullback theorem for a blowup away from the divisor applies. The recursion of the ideal and the formula for the successor structure map give the desired result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isSmoothDivisor_strictTransform_of_disjo: At each stage the transformed ideal factors as the prescribed smooth divisor times the iterated pullback of the initial divisor, with disjoint supports. The iterated pullback is a smooth divisor by the disjoint-center induction. The product of these two smooth divisors with disjoint supports is a smooth divisor, yielding the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedComap_succ: The successor in the recursion pulls the preceding ideal back along the transition from the new stage, giving the displayed formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iteratedComap_zero: Before any transition, the iterated pullback is defined to be the original divisor ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_eq_mul_iteratedComap: Induct on the stage, with the given product and disjointness as the initial case. At the next blowup the pulled-back divisor factor is disjoint from the center at the preceding stage. The strict transform of its product with the other ideal is therefore the strict transform of the other factor times the pullback of the divisor factor. This is the asserted new product by the two transform rules. The support of the strict transform of the other factor lies in its old support's inverse image, while the pulled-back divisor support is exactly its old support's inverse image. The old disjointness gives new disjointness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_strictTransform_subset_preimage: The strict-transform support is the closure of the inverse image of the original support away from the center. That set is contained in the full inverse image of the support, which is closed. Its closure is therefore contained there as well.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.krullDimSucc_eq_: The dimension index of the marked ideal is defined to be the dimension index of its ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.mk_eq_mk: The two marked ideals already have the same field, ambient and marking. Substituting the equal structure maps, ideals and boundaries makes every component agree, so the data are equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedSequenceOfBlowups.toMarkedSequence: The conversion retains the underlying sequence and the ideal at every stage. Evaluating the same ideals at the same final index gives equal last ideals.
The conversion to an ideal blowup sequence adds the properties of the ideal transforms but retains the same underlying sequence of schemes and blowup maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationAssignment.toSequenceOfB: Identify the two marked ideals using the given equality. The assignment is then applied to the same input on both sides, so the underlying blowup sequences are equal under that identification.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptyMarkedSequenceOfBlowups_length: The empty marked sequence uses the empty ordinary sequence as its underlying sequence, so its length is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.emptySequenceOfBlowups_length: The empty sequence is defined with length zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalDivisor_eq: The exceptional ideal of the stage is the center ideal pulled back along that stage's blowup transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isResolution_iff: The sequence is a resolution precisely when the final ideal's locus of order at least the marking is empty. This is its defining resolution condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_eq_withBotSuccToNat_topolog: The dimension index is defined by applying the successor conversion to the topological Krull dimension of the underlying space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.krullDimSucc_le_krullDimSucc_of_topologi: If the first dimension is bottom, its successor index is zero. Otherwise both dimensions are non-bottom because the first is at most the second. The upper dimension is below top, so both are embedded finite natural numbers. Their natural-number values have the same order, and adding one to both preserves the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastBoundary_eq: The last boundary is the boundary list at the final index, which is the length of the underlying sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastIdeal_eq: The last ideal is the ideal at the index given by the sequence's length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedSequenceOfBlowups_boundary_zero: The initial boundary is the pullback of the input list along the stage-zero isomorphism. Since the projection at zero is that same isomorphism, the displayed formula follows.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedSequenceOfBlowups_exceptionalIdeal: Apply the controlled-transform identity at the given valid stage. The marking is one, so the first power of the exceptional ideal is the ideal itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedSequenceOfBlowups_ideal_vanishesAl: The center support is in the locus where the stage ideal has order at least one. This locus is the ideal's support. The reduced-center condition turns that containment of supports into containment of the stage ideal in the center ideal, which means it vanishes along the center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedSequenceOfBlowups_ideal_zero: The stage-zero ideal is pulled back along its chosen isomorphism to the base. This isomorphism is the projection at stage zero, giving the claimed formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToSpec_eq: The projection from the stage to the field is defined by composing its projection to the base with the original structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBotSuccToNat_bot: The successor conversion assigns zero to the bottom element.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBotSuccToNat_coe: On an extended natural number viewed in the larger ordered set, the conversion takes its natural-number value and adds one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsAdmissible.transformAt: The field and positive marking are those of the original admissible input. The stage is smooth over the field and its boundary has strict normal crossings by the stage induction. Smoothness gives local finite type. The stage is Noetherian, so inverse images of quasi-compact opens are compact and its structural morphism is quasi-compact. The transformed ideal is nonzero on components by the controlled-transform induction. These give every admissibility condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_comap_iso: A pulled-back boundary entry is a pulled-back smooth divisor because the original list has strict normal crossing position. At each point start with an étale chart at its image and transport the chart through the isomorphism of inverse image opens. The boundary indices and their distinct assigned coordinates are unchanged. Pullback preserves unit ideals, and each coordinate ideal pulls back to the same coordinate ideal of the transported chart. These are the required local normal crossing presentations.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_projectio: Take the boundary conclusion of the simultaneous induction on stage smoothness and strict normal crossings at the specified valid stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt: The original scheme is Noetherian by admissibility, and the initial stage is isomorphic to it. Induct along the sequence. At each actual step the transition is a blowup of the preceding Noetherian scheme, hence its source is Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToSpec_succ: The successor projection to the base is the transition map followed by the preceding projection. Compose with the base field map and associate the arrows to obtain the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToSpec_zero: The stage-zero projection to the original ambient is its chosen isomorphism. Composing with the original structural map gives the stage-zero structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_and_inStrictNormalCrossingPositio: Induct on the stage. Initially the scheme is identified with the original one, transferring smoothness and the strict normal crossing condition of the initial boundary. At a successor the preceding ambient is smooth and its boundary has strict normal crossings by induction. The center is in strict normal crossing position with that boundary and the transition is its blowup. The smooth blowup theorem gives a smooth successor structure map. Since the successor is Noetherian, the boundary blowup theorem gives strict normal crossing position for the strict transforms of the old boundary with the exceptional ideal appended. The stage formulas identify these with the desired structure morphism and boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_projectionToSpec: The simultaneous induction on ambient smoothness and the boundary condition supplies smoothness at every stage in the allowed range. Take its smoothness conclusion at this stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_baseField: The transformed marked ideal retains the original base field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_boundary: The transform takes the boundary list from the specified stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_dim: The transform's dimension index depends only on its ambient scheme, which is the scheme at the specified stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_dim_le: Dimension nonincrease along blowups bounds the dimension index of the specified stage by the original one. The transform uses exactly that stage as its ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_ideal: The ideal of the transformed datum is the ideal assigned to that stage in the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_mult: Transforming the marked ideal retains its marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_scheme: The transform uses the ambient scheme of the specified blowup stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transformAt_structureMorphism: The structure map of the transform is the map from the specified stage to the field spectrum.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_id: The exceptional ideal is the center ideal pulled back along the morphism. With the identity morphism this pullback equals the center ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exceptionalIdeal_pow_mul_singleBlowupRes: At the only active index, zero, the exceptional ideal is the center pulled back to the blowup, and the preceding ideal is the original ideal. The successor ideal is chosen as a residual factor. The assumed divisibility ensures that multiplying this factor by the exceptional power gives the pulled-back original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasStrictNormalCrossingsWith_singleBlowu: The only index in range is zero. The initial projection is the identity and pulling back the original boundary along it leaves the list unchanged. Thus the crossing condition is exactly the original hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_singleBlowupMap: The only index below one is zero. At that index the map is the canonical blowup projection of the given ideal, which has the required blowup property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_comap_id_list_idealSheafData: Pullback along the identity fixes every ideal. Applying it in order to every entry therefore returns the original list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_blowupMorphism_zero: The transition at zero is defined to be the canonical map from the blowup of the given center to the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_boundary_one: At the positive stage the boundary consists of the strict transforms of the original list followed by the exceptional ideal of the blowup.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_center_zero: The center assignment uses the given ideal at the initial stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_ideal_one: The ideal at the positive stage is defined by taking a residual factor of the pulled-back original ideal with respect to the indicated power of the pulled-back center ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_length: The sequence data are defined with one active transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_projectionToBase_one: The projection at the first positive stage is defined as the blowup projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_schemeAt_succ: The scheme assignment uses the blowup scheme at every positive index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ofSingleBlowup_schemeAt_zero: The scheme at index zero is defined to be the given original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_mul_residualByPow: The hypothesis supplies a residual ideal whose product with the given power is the original ideal. The residual construction chooses one such ideal, so it satisfies that identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.singleBlowupBoundary_succ: There is only one active transition. The initial boundary is the original list, since its defining pullback is along the identity. The boundary on the blowup is defined by taking its strict transforms and appending the exceptional ideal, giving the successor identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.singleBlowupCenter_support_subset_orderA: The bound on the index forces it to be zero. There the center is the given ideal and the stage ideal is the original ideal pulled back along the identity. The asserted support containment is therefore the given order condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.singleBlowupProj_succ: At index zero the transition is the blowup projection and the preceding projection is the identity on the original scheme. At any later index the transition is the identity on the blowup and the preceding projection is the blowup projection. Both composites give the stated successor projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_singleBlowupCenter_of_smooth: The only active center is at index zero, and its stage projection is the identity. Its composite field map is the given smooth center map.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.irreducibleComponentsDisjointOfSmooth: Every local ring of the smooth scheme over the field is a domain. If two irreducible components met at a point, the local ring there being a domain would force the two components to be equal. Thus distinct components are disjoint.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.MarkedIdealWithBoundary.IsAdmissible.isN: The field spectrum is Noetherian. Admissibility makes the structure morphism locally of finite type and quasi-compact, so the source is Noetherian by the finite-type theorem over a Noetherian base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ideal_le_ideal_succ: The controlled-transform identity expresses the pulled-back ideal as the product of an exceptional factor and the successor ideal. An ideal product is contained in each factor, so the pulled-back ideal is contained in the successor ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_succ_apply: The successor projection is the transition to the preceding stage followed by its projection to the base. Evaluating the composite on the given point yields the displayed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_zero: The projection at stage zero is the zero-stage transition followed by the chosen initial isomorphism. The transition from zero to itself is the identity because the sequence is a functor. Thus the projection is the chosen isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ideal_succ_subset_preimage: The pulled-back old ideal is contained in the successor ideal. Support reverses inclusion of ideals, so the successor support lies in the support of the pulled-back old ideal. The latter is the inverse image of the old support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsBoundaryDivisorReduction.isPullbackBlo: The smooth pullback clause allows a boundary with the same nontrivial part and a matching designated entry. Taking the actual pulled-back boundary makes both comparisons reflexive. The assumptions on both marked ideals then give the stated sequence pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsBoundaryDivisorReduction.isStrictPullb: Apply the strict field extension clause with the actual boundary of the extended datum. Its nontrivial boundary and designated entry agree with themselves, and the specified hypotheses give all the other requirements.

Use the strict smooth pullback clause for the given surjection. The actual pulled-back boundary agrees with itself after removing unit ideals and has the same designated entry. This gives the strict pullback comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxOrderReduction.isPullbackBlowupSequ: In the field base-change clause use the actual boundary of the extended datum, so its nontrivial boundary agrees by equality. Apply the clause using the given admissibility and dimension hypotheses.

Apply the smooth pullback clause of maximal-order reduction, taking the new boundary list to be the actual pulled-back boundary. Its nontrivial part equals itself, and the remaining admissibility and dimension assumptions are given.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxOrderReduction.isStrictPullbackBlow: Apply the strict field base-change clause to the actual extended datum. Its boundary itself gives the comparison list and meets the requested agreement after removing unit ideals.

Use the strict smooth pullback clause with the given smooth surjection. Choose the pulled-back boundary itself as the comparison boundary, so the required agreement after deleting unit ideals is reflexive. The clause gives the strict comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsMaxOrderReduction.mono: Any dimension covered by the new predicate is covered by the original one. Apply this implication to the original input and, in each comparison involving another input, to the other input as well. All the original specification clauses then apply to the restricted predicate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.append: Filter both concatenations. Filtering distributes over concatenation, and each pair of filtered parts agrees by hypothesis. Hence the filtered concatenations agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.map: After mapping each list, discard all unit ideals. The filter identity allows the original unit ideals to be discarded before mapping as well. The original filtered lists agree by hypothesis, so applying the same map and final filter gives equal lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.refl: Deleting the unit ideals from the same list on both sides gives equal lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.symm: The condition is equality of the filtered lists. Reversing that equality gives symmetry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SameNontrivialBoundary.trans: The first filtered list equals the second and the second equals the third. Composing these equalities gives the stated relation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_baseField: The definition of field base change sets the new base to the extension field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_boundary: The base-changed boundary pulls each ideal in the old list back along the projection to the old ambient scheme, preserving the order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_ideal: The new ideal is pulled back along the first projection from the fiber product to the old ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_mult: Field extension retains the original marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_scheme: The ambient scheme over the new field is the fiber product of the old scheme with the new field spectrum over the old field spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_structureMorphism: The structural morphism of the base-changed ambient is the second projection of the fiber product, to the new field spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isMaxOrderReduction_of_forall_not: Each part of the maximal-order specification assumes that the dimension predicate holds at the input's index. The assumption rules this out at every index, so each part holds vacuously.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOrderBoundedByMult_iff: The order bound is the requirement that at every point the order of the ideal is at most the marking. The two sides give the same condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.kerSubschemeIso_hom_comp: The source of a closed immersion is isomorphic to its scheme-theoretic image, defined by the kernel ideal. The original map factors through that image. Composing the inverse of the factorization with the original map therefore recovers the image inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.kerSubschemeIso_inv_comp: The inverse isomorphism identifies the source with its kernel subscheme. Following it by the kernel subscheme's inclusion gives the original immersion by the image factorization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_boundaryLocus_iff: The boundary locus is the union of the supports of the boundary ideals at the stage. A point belongs to that union precisely when at least one boundary ideal has it in its support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_otherBoundaryLocus_iff: The locus is a union over the valid boundary positions other than the excluded one. Membership in the union is equivalent to finding such a position whose boundary support contains the point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_append: Filtering out the unit ideals from a concatenation keeps the surviving entries from the first list followed by those from the second. This is the concatenation of the two filtered lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialPart_map_nontrivialPart: A unit ideal that is deleted before applying the map would still be a unit ideal after mapping, and would be deleted by the final filter. Every other entry gives the same mapped value whether it is first filtered or immediately mapped. The final filter keeps that value exactly when it differs from the unit ideal. Induction down the list gives equality with order preserved.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_baseField: Pulling the marked ideal back along a morphism of schemes over the field retains its base field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_boundary: Each boundary ideal is pulled back along the given morphism in its original position. This gives the boundary list of the new datum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_ideal: The ideal component of the pulled-back datum is the original ideal sheaf pulled back along the given morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_mult: The pullback changes the ideal and boundary by pullback and keeps the original marking.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_scheme: The pullback datum takes the supplied source scheme as its new ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlong_structureMorphism: The new marked ideal uses the structural morphism to the field specified for the source scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sameNontrivialBoundary_iff: The condition is defined by deleting all unit ideals from the two lists and comparing the resulting ordered lists.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_baseField: Changing the boundary alone leaves the base field unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_boundary: The boundary replacement assigns the supplied list as its boundary component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_dim: The dimension index depends only on the ambient scheme, which is retained in the boundary replacement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_ideal: The underlying marked ideal sheaf is copied as part of boundary replacement.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_mult: The marking is copied unchanged when the boundary is replaced.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_scheme: Changing the boundary retains the ambient scheme, on which the new list is defined.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_self: Replacing the boundary with its original list gives exactly the original data.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withBoundary_structureMorphism: The boundary replacement retains the structural morphism of the same ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_baseField: Replacing the ambient scheme, ideal and boundary keeps the base field of the existing marked datum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_boundary: The replacement uses the supplied boundary list on the new ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_ideal: The replacement explicitly sets the ideal sheaf to the supplied ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_mult: The replacement datum retains the marking of the old ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_scheme: The replacement datum takes the supplied scheme as its ambient.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withSchemeIdealBoundary_structureMorphis: The new scheme is equipped with the structural morphism supplied in the replacement data.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.OrderCertificate.of_two_le: The large-marking case of an order certificate applies as soon as the marking is at least two. The hypothesis gives this bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.PrincipalizationCertificate.of_two_le: A marking of at least two satisfies the large-marking case in the definition of a principalization certificate. That case supplies the required certificate directly.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_orderCertificate_of_subset:
Induct simultaneously on order and principalization certificates. Memory witnesses remain valid by transitivity of containment, and large markings use the same witnesses regardless of memory. In a principalization step that passes to an order certificate, enlarge the recorded containment and apply induction to that order certificate. For either localization case, the old and new memory sets remain nested after taking inverse images in each open.

In a descent step, a point outside the new memory also lies outside the old one, so keep the same local ideal conditions. On every chosen hypersurface the two pulled-back memory sets are nested, so induction gives the descended order certificates for the new memory. All defining cases are preserved, yielding the order certificate with enlarged memory.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_principalizationCertificate_of_su:
Use simultaneous induction on the principalization and order certificates. In the memory cases, compose the old containment with the enlargement of the memory set. Large-marking certificates have no memory condition. In the passage from principalization to order reduction, enlarge the required containment and apply induction to its order certificate. Localization uses that inverse images preserve containments, so the induction hypothesis applies on every chosen open.

For descent to a hypersurface, keep the opens, hypersurfaces and ideals. Any point outside the enlarged memory was outside the old memory, so the required local condition remains valid. The inverse image of the old memory under the hypersurface inclusion into the original scheme is contained in the inverse image of the new memory. Apply induction to each descended order certificate with those inverse images. This covers every constructor and gives the enlarged principalization certificate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderCertificate_mono_of_subset: Use the order certificate induction result with the enlarged memory set and its given containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationCertificate_mono_of_subs: Apply the simultaneous induction result for principalization certificates to the given certificate and the stated enlargement of its memory set.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasReducedCenters_markedBlowupSeq: At any actual stage, the marked sequence gives a center smooth over the field. Its structure map is the center inclusion followed by the stage's projection to the field. Apply the smooth-center ideal criterion to this center and the given ideal whose support contains it. The resulting ideal containment is precisely the required reduced-center condition at this stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isFunctorialPrincipalization_principaliz: The conversion to a principalization sequence preserves both the underlying blowups and the final ideal. Pushforward along the given closed immersions therefore follows from the assumed pushforward comparison for the marked sequences. Field base change and smooth pullback follow from the corresponding marked-sequence comparisons, including their strict forms for field extensions and smooth surjections. Finally the marked sequence resolves the order-one ideal, so its final ideal and hence the principalization's final ideal are the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_baseChange_isPullback: The original and field-extended data both define admissible marked triples of order one. Use the maximum of their dimension indices as a common bound, which leaves both outputs unchanged by coherence. The maximal-order specification at that bound provides compatibility with field base change. Its comparison is the stated pullback along the projection to the original scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_baseChange_isStrictPullb: Form the two admissible order-one inputs over the original and extended fields. Both sequences can be computed at the maximum of their dimension indices by coherence of the reduction levels. At this common level the maximal-order reduction has the strict field base-change property, which gives the strict comparison of the two sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_lastIdeal_eq_top: At the ambient dimension index, the maximal-order specification resolves the admissible marked triple. Resolution at marking one means that the final ideal has empty locus of order at least one. That locus is the support of the final ideal. An ideal sheaf with empty support is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_smoothPullback_isPullbac: Form the admissible marked triples of order one on the original and new schemes, pulling back the ideal and boundary for the latter. Take the maximum of the two dimension indices. Coherence of the reduction levels lets both marked blowup sequences be computed at this one bound. At that bound the maximal-order rule satisfies its specification by dimension reduction. Apply its smooth pullback property to the two admissible triples to obtain the comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_smoothPullback_isStrictP: Use a common dimension bound equal to the maximum of the two dimension indices. The two admissible inputs of marking one give the same outputs at that bound as at their original levels by coherence. At the common level the maximal-order reduction specification gives strict pullback along a smooth surjection. Apply it to the given map and pulled-back input.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedBlowupSeq_toSequenceOfBlowups_eq_o: The marked triple has the dimension index of its ambient scheme. Coherence of the successive reduction levels says that maximal-order reduction at any larger bound agrees with its value at that index. Apply the operation that forgets the markings to this equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_baseField: The marked triple uses the supplied field as its base field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_boundary: The construction uses the supplied ordered list as the boundary of the marked triple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_dim: The dimension index of a marked triple is computed from its ambient scheme. Here that scheme is the original one, so their dimension indices agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_ideal: The ideal of the marked triple is the ideal supplied to its construction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_isAdmissible: The field has characteristic zero and the structural map is smooth, locally of finite type and quasi-compact by hypothesis. The ideal is nonzero on components and the boundary has strict normal crossings by the remaining hypotheses. The marking equals one and is therefore positive. Thus every admissibility condition is satisfied.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_mult: The marked triple is defined with marking one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_pullbackAlong: Pullback replaces the ambient scheme and structure map by the specified ones, pulls back the ideal, and pulls back each boundary ideal in order. The field and the marking one are retained. These are precisely the data of the marked triple on the new scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_scheme: The marked triple is formed on the supplied ambient scheme, so its scheme is that input.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.markedTripleOrderOne_structureMorphism: Construction of the marked triple retains the supplied structural morphism to the field spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalization_lastIdeal: The conversion from the marked sequence of order one to an ideal blowup sequence retains its ideals, including the final ideal. Hence the two final ideals agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalization_toSequenceOfBlowups: The output of principalization is obtained by viewing the marked sequence of order one as an ideal blowup sequence using the reduced centers. This conversion retains the underlying sequence of blowups, so forgetting the additional data on either side gives the same sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sequence_eq_maxOrderReduction: The marked blowup sequence is defined by applying maximal-order reduction at the dimension index of the ambient scheme to its marked triple of order one.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.radical_ker_le_ker_of_isReduced: If a power of an element belongs to the kernel, the same power of its image is zero. In a reduced target this forces the image itself to be zero. Thus the element belongs to the kernel.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothSubschemeIdealIsRadical:
The smooth closed subscheme has local rings that are domains, so it is reduced and its rings of sections on opens are reduced. On each affine ambient open the defining ideal is the kernel of the restriction to the subscheme. The reduced-target kernel criterion makes each such ideal radical, so the defining ideal sheaf is radical.

The support of the smooth center is contained in the support of the given ideal. The order relation between supports and vanishing ideals then places the given ideal inside the vanishing ideal of the center's support. This vanishing ideal is the radical of the defining ideal, which equals the defining ideal by the preceding argument.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.blowupMorphism_eq_transitionMap: A successor transition is defined using the order arrow from its stage to the next natural number in the opposite indexing category.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_blowupMorphism: For every index strictly below the length, the data of the sequence identify the successor transition as the blowup along the center ideal of that index. Apply this property at the given index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastStructMap_eq_projectionToBase: The last structural map is defined as the projection to the base at the index equal to the length of the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_def: The projection to the base is defined by taking the transition to stage zero and then applying the chosen isomorphism from stage zero to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_succ: Factor the transition from the successor stage to stage zero through its preceding stage. Composing with the initial isomorphism gives the successor transition followed by the preceding projection to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_zero: At stage zero the transition to zero is the identity. Composing it with the chosen initial isomorphism gives that isomorphism itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_fst: The pulled-back transition is the map furnished by the pullback universal property. Its first prescribed projection is the first projection from the later pullback, with an identity on the new base. Removing that identity gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_snd: The pullback universal property prescribes the second projection of the lifted map as projection from the later pullback followed by the original transition on the tower.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_def: The tower is indexed by the opposite of the ordered set of stages. The transition from the later stage to the earlier stage is, by definition, the image under the tower functor of the opposite of the indicated order arrow.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_self: The order arrow from a stage to itself is the identity, and its opposite is also the identity. The tower functor preserves identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_trans: The composite of the order arrows from the first stage to the intermediate stage and from there to the last stage is the order arrow for the transitive inequality. Take opposites, which reverse the order of composition, and apply functoriality of the tower.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.length_eq: Equal lengths are the first condition in the definition of a strict pullback of blowup sequences.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.of_length_zero: The sequence lengths agree because both are zero. The only stage to compare is stage zero. Use its isomorphism to the source base, apply the given base morphism, and then use the inverse initial isomorphism on the target side. The required equality at stage zero follows by cancellation. There are no successive squares or centers to compare.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.isomorphic_refl: The lengths are equal. Choose the identity isomorphism at every stage. These preserve the initial structural map, commute with all successor transitions, and pull every center back to itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_comp: The image ideal is the direct image operation on ideal sheaves that takes the scheme-theoretic image of the corresponding closed subscheme. This operation is functorial in the morphism. Applying it to the composite gives the image of the intermediate image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.imageIdealSheaf_eq_ker: By definition the image ideal is the kernel of the map of schemes from the given closed subscheme to the target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eq_imageIdealSheaf: Both ideals are defined as the kernel ideal sheaf of the closed subscheme inclusion followed by the morphism to the target.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em._root_.FunctorialResolution.Blowup.IsLoc: Take the generic point of the component and an affine neighborhood where the ideal is generated by a non-zero-divisor. If the whole component were contained in the support, its generic point’s prime ideal would contain that generator. This prime is minimal. Indeed, a smaller prime would give a point specializing to the generic point, and the closure of that point would be irreducible and contain the component. Maximality would identify those closures, forcing equality of the two primes. A non-zero-divisor belongs to no minimal prime, giving the contradiction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_closure_singleton_iff_fromSpec: Membership in the closure of a singleton is the specialization relation from that singleton’s point. The canonical map from the affine spectrum is an open embedding and therefore preserves and reflects specialization. The closure condition is consequently equivalent on both sides.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_primeIdealOf_of_mem_support: On the affine open, support membership means the point lies in the zero locus of the section ideal. In particular, the point is outside the basic open of the given section. The corresponding prime ideal therefore contains that section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_primeIdealOf_of_notMem_basicOpen: In the spectrum of the affine open, the inverse image of the basic open is the basic open of the same section. If the corresponding prime did not contain the section, it would lie in this basic open, and its image would be the original point in the given basic open. This contradicts the hypothesis.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_restrict_comp: The restriction of the composite to the target open factors as the restriction of the first morphism to the inverse image open followed by the restriction of the second morphism. Both factors are isomorphisms, so their composite is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_restrict_lastStructMap_of_centersL: The last structural map is the projection at the final stage. Apply the stagewise isomorphism result there to the given disjoint open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_restrict_lastStructMap_smoothLocus: The smooth locus is disjoint from its complement. All centers lie over that complement by hypothesis, so the last structural map restricts to an isomorphism over the smooth locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_restrict_projectionToBase_of_cente: Induct on the stage. Initially projection to the base is the given isomorphism, whose restriction remains an isomorphism. At a successor, the center misses the inverse image of the chosen open because all center points project into the prescribed disjoint set. Hence the restricted center ideal is the unit ideal and the restricted blowup is an isomorphism. Compose this with the preceding restricted projection, which is an isomorphism by induction.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedPrincipalizationAmbientIsNoether: Construct the affine-space principalization data using the specified embedding, empty boundary, and smooth ambient structure. The ambient-stage Noetherianity result applies to these data at every stage within the sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_ambientLevel: The base ambient scheme is finite-dimensional affine space over a field. Its polynomial coordinate ring is Noetherian, hence so is its spectrum. The initial ambient stage is isomorphic to that scheme. Each successor is a blowup of a Noetherian previous stage and is Noetherian by induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_of_isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf: A blowup over the Noetherian target is proper, hence quasi-compact and locally of finite type. These two properties over a Noetherian base give a Noetherian source.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_of_iso: The inverse isomorphism is quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Apply the Noetherianity result to it with the given Noetherian scheme as target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType: A morphism locally of finite type over a Noetherian scheme has a locally Noetherian source. Its quasi-compactness makes the source quasi-compact because the target is quasi-compact. These two properties make the source Noetherian.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isNoetherian_schemeAt: Induct on the stage within the length of the sequence. Stage zero is isomorphic to the Noetherian base. At each successor the transition is a blowup of the previous Noetherian stage, so its source is Noetherian as well.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_top_of_lt_nextNontrivialIndex: If the earlier index had a nonunit center, it would be an admissible result for the search. Minimality would then bound the search result by that index, contradicting the strict inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_top_of_lt_nontrivialIndex_zero: The first search starts at zero, and the given index precedes its least admissible result. Therefore its center is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_eq_top_of_nontrivialIndex_lt: The next search starts just after the preceding retained index. The index in question lies within that search range and before the result. If its center were nonunit the search would have stopped there or earlier, so its center is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_nextNontrivialIndex_ne_top_or_len: The index selected by the search meets its defining stopping condition. Its center is nonunit or the index is at least the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_nontrivialIndex_ne_top: The indexed search result has a nonunit center or reaches the original length. Since this is a position strictly within the shortened sequence, the retained value is below the original length. Thus the center is nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.center_nontrivialIndex_ne_top_or_length_: Both the initial retained index and every successor retained index are results of the same search. In each case the result satisfies the stopping condition of having a nonunit center or reaching the sequence length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_le_center_ne_top_or_length_le: Choose the larger of the starting index and the sequence length. It is at least the starting index and satisfies the stopping condition because it is at least the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_length_le_nontrivialIndex: Use the sequence length as the enumeration index. The retained index function has value at least its argument, so the result is at least the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_towerWithoutIsoB: The shortened transition factors through the stage immediately after the original retained blowup. The map back from the next retained stage to that intermediate stage is an isomorphism, since all intervening centers are unit ideals. The other factor is the original blowup along the retained center. Precomposing a blowup with an isomorphism of its source leaves it a blowup along the same ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_transitionMap_nontrivialIndex_succ: Between the stage immediately after the retained blowup and the next retained stage, all omitted centers are unit ideals. The next retained stage is at most the original length. The transition across this interval is therefore an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_transitionMap_nontrivialIndex_zero: The first retained index is at most the original length, and all centers before it are unit ideals. The transition across that initial interval is therefore an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_transitionMap_of_center_eq_top: Induct on the upper endpoint starting at the lower endpoint. The initial transition is the identity. At a successor the transition factors as the last single blowup followed by the shorter transition. The last center is the unit ideal by hypothesis, so its blowup is an isomorphism. The shorter transition is an isomorphism by induction, and their composite is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_transitionMap_refl: The transition from a stage to itself is the tower functor’s image of an identity arrow and is therefore an identity morphism. Every identity morphism is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_nextNontrivialIndex: The search specification includes the condition that the returned index is at least the starting index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_nontrivialIndex: The first value is a natural number and hence at least zero. Each successive value is at least one larger than the preceding value. Induction therefore bounds the enumeration index by its value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.length_le_nontrivialIndex_lengthWithoutI: The shortened length is the first enumeration index whose retained value reaches or exceeds the original length. Its retained value therefore satisfies that lower bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextNontrivialIndex_le: The candidate lies at or above the starting index and meets the stopping condition. The search chooses the least such candidate, giving the claimed bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextNontrivialIndex_le_length: The sequence length is at least the starting index by hypothesis and automatically satisfies the end-of-sequence condition. Minimality bounds the search result by the length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextNontrivialIndex_spec: The search returns the least index at or above the starting index with a nonunit center or at or beyond the end. By the defining property of a least witness, the returned index satisfies both conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_le_length: For the initial value, the original length is an admissible bound for the search. At a successor within the shortened length, the preceding value is strictly below the original length. The new search therefore starts at or below that length and cannot pass it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_le_length_of_forall_lt: At index zero the search starts at zero and can always stop at the original length. At a successor, the preceding retained value is strictly below the length by hypothesis, so restarting at its successor is still at or below the length. In either case the length is an admissible endpoint, bounding the search result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_lengthWithoutIsoBlowups: At the shortened length the retained value is at least the original length. Every earlier value is strictly below that length by minimality. The search that produces the value at the shortened length therefore starts at or below the original length and cannot pass it. The two bounds give equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_lt_length: A value at an enumeration index strictly before the shortened length cannot already reach the original length, since that would contradict minimality of the shortened length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_lt_succ: The next retained index is at least the starting index of its search, which is the preceding retained index plus one. Thus it is strictly greater than the preceding index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_monotone: Strict increase implies weak increase for unequal indices, and equal indices have equal values.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_strictMono: Successive values strictly increase. Chaining these one-step inequalities across any finite interval gives strict monotonicity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_succ: The recursive step resumes the search at one more than the preceding retained index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_zero: The enumeration begins by searching for the next nontrivial index starting at zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.objNontrivialIndexZeroIso_hom: The forward map first takes the initial run of omitted blowups back to stage zero and then applies the original initial isomorphism. That composite is the projection to the base at the first retained index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projectionToBase_eq_eqToHom_comp: Replace the equal indices by a single index. The indicated transport morphism then becomes the identity, whose composite with the projection is that projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.succ_le_nontrivialIndex_succ: For natural numbers, strict inequality between two consecutive retained indices means that one plus the earlier index is at most the later index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_blowupMorphism: Apply the formula for shortened transitions to the order arrow from a stage to its successor, which defines the shortened blowup morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_center: The center of the shortened sequence is defined by evaluating the original center at the corresponding retained index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_center_ne_top: Every center of the shortened sequence is the original center at its retained index. For a position within the shortened length, the search result lies before the original end and has a nonunit center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_centersLieOver: A point on a shortened center is a point on the original center at the corresponding retained index. The shortened projection to the base equals the original projection from that stage. Its image lies in the prescribed set by the original center condition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_isoObjZero: The shortened sequence uses the previously constructed isomorphism from the first retained stage to the original base as its stage-zero isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_lastObj: The last retained index is exactly the original length. Evaluating the original tower at these equal indices identifies the two last objects.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_lastStructMap: The final shortened structural map is the original projection from the final retained stage. That retained index equals the original length, so transport along the induced equality of last objects identifies the projection with the original final structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_length: The shortened sequence is defined with length equal to the first enumeration index whose retained value reaches the original length.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_projectionToBase_eq_no: The shortened projection is the original transition to the first retained stage followed by the shortened initial isomorphism. This isomorphism’s forward map is the original projection from the first retained stage. The transition compatibility for projections identifies the composite with the original projection from the given retained stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_schemeAt: The shortened tower is the original tower evaluated at the retained indices. Its scheme at the given index is therefore the original scheme at the corresponding retained index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.withoutIsoBlowups_transitionMap: The shortened tower is obtained by precomposing the original tower with the map of ordered indexing categories given by the monotone retained-index function. The resulting transition is the original transition for the inequality between the retained indices.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isIso_strictTransformOpens_of_isI: The ambient isomorphism induces an isomorphism of the two pulled-back closed subschemes. The support of the pulled-back center is the inverse image of the original center support, and taking complements commutes with inverse image. Because the subscheme isomorphism commutes with the inclusions, it identifies the two opens used for strict transform. Restrict the isomorphism and its inverse to those opens. They are still inverse after composing with the open inclusions, and the restricted forward map commutes with the strict-transform immersions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isIso_subscheme_comap_of_isIso: Pullback of the ideal along the composite is successive pullback along the two maps. Base-changing the closed subscheme along the isomorphism identifies its pulled-back subscheme with the original one and gives an isomorphism commuting with the closed inclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lengthWithoutIsoBlowups_congr_of_center_: The two retained index functions agree because the sequences have the same length and the same trivial center positions. Shortened length comparison in both directions then gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lengthWithoutIsoBlowups_le_of_nontrivial: If the first shortened length exceeded the second, its retained index at the second shortened length would still be below the common original length. At the same position the second retained index is at least the original length, by the stopping criterion. This contradicts equality of their retained index functions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextNontrivialIndex_congr_of_center_eq_t: Apply the comparison inequality in both directions. Reversing the roles of the sequences preserves equal length and exchanges the two sides of the equivalence for unit centers. The two inequalities give equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nextNontrivialIndex_le_of_center_eq_top_: The first admissible index at or above the starting index in the second sequence is also admissible in the first. If it is within the common length, its center is nontrivial in both sequences by hypothesis. If it is at or beyond the length, it meets the stopping condition in both. Minimality in the first sequence gives the inequality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivialIndex_congr_of_center_eq_top_i: The first retained indices agree because both searches start at zero. If the current retained indices agree, the next searches start at the same successor index and again have equal results. Induction gives pointwise equality of the index functions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.preimage_inv_eq: Replace the source open by the forward inverse image of the target open. Taking the inverse isomorphism’s inverse image amounts to taking the inverse image along the composite of the inverse and forward maps. That composite is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_isIso_comp: The isomorphism between the two strict-transform opens commutes with their maps into the original source. Thus precomposing the original strict-transform immersion with that isomorphism leaves its kernel unchanged and gives the same kernel as the new immersion followed by the ambient isomorphism. Pulling this kernel back along the ambient isomorphism gives the kernel of the new immersion. These kernels are the strict-transform ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_top_eq_comap: The unit center ideal has empty support, so its pullback also has empty support. The open used to define the strict transform is therefore the entire pulled-back subscheme, and its open inclusion is an isomorphism. Taking the kernel of the composite immersion gives the kernel of the pulled-back closed immersion itself, which is the pulled-back ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.base_apply_congr: Equal morphisms have equal maps on points. Apply these maps to the specified point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_saturationOpens: The saturation open is defined by pulling back the complement of the first ideal’s support to the closed subscheme defined by the second ideal. On points it is exactly this inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_comp_morphismRestrict_eq_saturati: Map the restricted closed subscheme into the restriction of the original closed subscheme by the closed-immersion factorization. On the restricted saturation open, its points avoid the pulled-back first support, so their images in the ambient scheme avoid the original support. The map therefore factors through the original saturation open. Its ambient image also lies in the given ambient open by construction. Factor again through the inverse image of that open in the original saturation source. Composing the resulting map with the restricted original immersion agrees with the new immersion, as can be checked after the ambient open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_comp_saturationι_eq_morphismRestr: The inverse image of the ambient open in the original saturation source maps into the restriction of the original closed subscheme. Compose with the factorization into the subscheme defined by the restricted second ideal. The ambient image of every point avoids the first support, and hence the image in the ambient open avoids its inverse image. The composite therefore factors through the restricted saturation open. After composing with the ambient open inclusion both maps to the ambient scheme equal the original saturation immersion on the restricted source, yielding the desired compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_factorizations_subscheme_restrict: Restricting the closed immersion to the ambient open pulls its kernel ideal back along the open inclusion. The closed subscheme of the pulled-back ideal has this same kernel. Each closed immersion thus factors through the other, giving both maps and their compatibility with the inclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isOpen_mem_forall_subset_isCompac: Choose an affine open containing the point, using the affine open cover of the scheme. All subsets of this affine open are quasi-compact by local Noetherianity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_comap_hom_id: A ring element belongs to the inverse image of the ideal under the identity exactly when the element itself belongs to the ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_preimage_ι_le: The image of the inverse image under an open inclusion is the intersection of the given open with the range of the inclusion. That intersection is contained in the given open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompact_of_subset_affineOpen: The affine open of a locally Noetherian scheme has a Noetherian coordinate ring and hence a Noetherian underlying space. Every subset in that space is quasi-compact. The subset in the ambient scheme is its continuous image under the inclusion, so is quasi-compact too.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompact_of_subset_isCompact: Cover the larger quasi-compact set by finitely many affine open neighborhoods, each of which has quasi-compact subsets. The smaller set is the finite union of its intersections with these neighborhoods. Each intersection is quasi-compact, so the union is quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_app_subschemeι: On an affine open the kernel ideal sheaf of the closed immersion is computed by the kernel of its section map. The closed immersion has kernel ideal sheaf equal to the ideal defining its subscheme, which gives the section ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comap_ι: Check the equality on an affine open of the restricted target. Restriction of the original kernel is computed by the section map on the corresponding ambient open. The section map of the restricted morphism is that map transported to the identified inverse-image open. Transport of the ring along the equality of opens preserves the kernel, giving the chartwise equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_comp_map_eqToHom: Identify the two equal opens. The transport of section rings then becomes the identity, and composing with it leaves the kernel unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_ker_of_factorizations: Each morphism factors through the other. The kernel containment for a composite applies to the first factorization and gives one inclusion, and the second factorization gives the opposite inclusion. Hence the kernels agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_le_ker_comp: On every affine target open the section map of the composite factors through the section map of the second morphism. A section killed by that first section map has zero image under the composite section map. This gives containment of the kernel ideal sheaves.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_basicOpen_eq_zero_iff: On an affine chart the section ring of the basic open is the localization of the chart ring at the powers of the defining section. An element maps to zero in this localization exactly when some power of that section annihilates it. In one direction this is the equality criterion for localization. In the other, the power becomes a unit, so its vanishing product forces the localized element to vanish.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eq_zero_congr: The two restrictions have the same target open. After identifying these equal opens, the restrictions are the same and give equivalent vanishing conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_saturationOpens: A point belongs to the saturation open exactly when it belongs to the inverse image of the complement of the first ideal’s support. Equivalently its image under the closed immersion avoids that support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_saturation_ideal_iff: On the affine chart, the saturation immersion restricts the closed subscheme of the second ideal to the basic open of the image of the generator of the first ideal. Thus a section belongs to the saturation ideal exactly when its image in the closed-subscheme section ring vanishes after localization at that generator. This happens exactly when some power of the image of the generator annihilates that image. Since the kernel of the closed-subscheme section map is the second ideal, the last condition says that the same power times the original section belongs to the second ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_strictTransform_ideal_iff: The strict transform is the saturation of the total transform by the pulled-back center. On the affine chart this center ideal is principal, so the affine saturation criterion says that a section belongs to the strict-transform ideal exactly when a power of the generator times the section lies in the total-transform ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_of_eq: Replace the first morphism by the equal second morphism. Its quasi-compactness is the given hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_saturationι_congr: Replace both ideals by their equal counterparts. The saturation immersion thereby becomes the one assumed quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_saturationι_of_isLocallyNoe: The saturation immersion is an embedding. The image of the inverse image of a quasi-compact open is its intersection with the saturation range. As a subset of the original quasi-compact open in a locally Noetherian scheme, the intersection is quasi-compact. The embedding reflects that property back to the inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_saturationι_of_noetherianSp: The saturation immersion is an embedding into a Noetherian space, so its source is Noetherian with the induced topology. In particular, the inverse image of each quasi-compact open is quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_saturationι_restrictIdeal: Take a quasi-compact open in the restricted ambient scheme. Its image in the original ambient scheme is open and quasi-compact, so its inverse image by the original saturation immersion is quasi-compact. The image of this inverse image is its intersection with the original saturation range. Pulling the intersection back along the open embedding preserves quasi-compactness and identifies it with the chosen open intersected with the new saturation range, since the restricted supports are inverse images. The restricted saturation immersion is an embedding and hence reflects quasi-compactness of that intersection back to the required inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_strictTransformι_comp_ι: The original strict-transform immersion is the saturation immersion for the two pulled-back ideals and is quasi-compact. Restriction to the open preserves quasi-compactness of this saturation immersion. The restricted ideals are exactly the ideals pulled back along the composite with the open inclusion, so the restricted immersion is the required strict-transform immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.quasiCompact_strictTransformι_of_noether: The strict-transform immersion is the saturation immersion for the total transform away from the pulled-back center. The ambient space is Noetherian, so the quasi-compactness result for saturation immersions applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_saturationι: Every point in the source maps to the support of the second ideal because it lies in its closed subscheme. The saturation open also ensures that it maps outside the support of the first ideal. Conversely, any point in that difference lifts to the closed subscheme of the second ideal, and the lift lies in the saturation open. This proves equality of the two point sets.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_saturation: Restrict the kernel of the saturation immersion to the ambient open to obtain the kernel of the restricted immersion. The immersion formed by saturating the restricted ideals has the same kernel, since the two immersions factor through each other over the open and both are quasi-compact. This second kernel is the saturation of the restricted ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.restrictIdeal_strictTransform: Express the strict-transform ideal as saturation of the two pulled-back ideals, then commute saturation with restriction to the open. Each restricted pulled-back ideal equals its original ideal pulled back along the open inclusion followed by the given morphism. Their saturation is the strict transform for that composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.saturation_eq_ker_saturationι: The saturation ideal is defined as the kernel ideal sheaf of the saturation immersion, so it cuts out the scheme-theoretic image of that immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.saturation_ideal_eq_of_eq_mul: If a section lies in the saturation, some power of the generator times it belongs to the product of the principal ideal and the given factor ideal, hence to the factor ideal. Repeatedly apply the cancellation hypothesis for membership in the factor ideal to remove that power. Conversely, if a section lies in the factor ideal, multiplying it once by the generator gives an element of the product. Taking exponent one shows membership in the saturation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.saturation_ideal_eq_of_isUnit: For a section in the saturation, some power of the unit generator times it lies in the second ideal. Multiplying by the inverse unit power shows the section itself lies in that ideal. Every section already in the second ideal satisfies the saturation criterion with exponent zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.saturation_ideal_eq_top_of_span_pow_le: The stated containment puts the indicated power of the generator in the second ideal. The affine membership criterion, applied to the section one with that exponent, puts one in the saturation. An ideal containing one is the unit ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.saturationι_eq_ι_comp_subschemeι: The saturation immersion first includes the saturation open into the closed subscheme of the second ideal and then includes that closed subscheme into the ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_comp_ι: Pullback along the given composite is pullback along the open inclusion followed by pullback along the map into the open. Pullback along the open inclusion is restriction of each ideal. The two pairs of ideals used for saturation therefore agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_eq_of_comap_eq: Compute each strict transform as the saturation of its two pulled-back ideals. The two pairs of pulled-back ideals agree by hypothesis, hence the resulting saturations agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_eq_saturation: The strict-transform ideal and the saturation of the pulled-back original ideal away from the pulled-back center are the kernels of the same immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_ideal_eq_comap_of_isUnit: The strict transform on the chart is the saturation of the pulled-back original ideal by the pulled-back center ideal. Since the center generator is a unit, multiplication by any power of it preserves ideal membership. Saturation therefore leaves the pulled-back original ideal unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformι_eq_saturationι: The strict-transform immersion uses the subscheme defined by the pulled-back original ideal and the open away from the support of the pulled-back center. These are exactly the data defining the saturation immersion for the two pulled-back ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_compl_inf_eq_basicOpen: On the affine chart the first ideal is generated by the given section. A point of the chart belongs to its support exactly when that section vanishes there. The complement inside the chart is therefore the basic open of that section.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.coe_strictTransformOpens: The open in the pulled-back closed subscheme consists exactly of the points whose images lie outside the support of the pulled-back center ideal. This is the inverse image defining the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_ker_subschemeι_comp: Pulling back the kernel of the composite along the open immersion recovers the kernel of the closed immersion. The latter is the ideal defining that closed subscheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_le_strictTransform: The pulled-back subscheme ideal is the kernel of its closed immersion. The strict-transform immersion is obtained by precomposing that immersion with an open inclusion. Every section vanishing on the whole subscheme still vanishes on its open part, yielding the containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isIso_subschemeι_preimage_comap: The restriction of the given closed immersion and the closed immersion defined by the pulled-back ideal have the same kernel. The equal kernels give a factorization of the first immersion through the second and make the resulting morphism an isomorphism. Its factorization equation is the asserted compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.image_preimage_ι_of_le: The image of the inverse image lies inside the original open. Conversely, any point of that open belongs to the larger open by hypothesis and so has a lift to the larger open whose image is the point itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_of_isIso_comp: The pullback of the center ideal along the new morphism is the pullback of the original Cartier ideal along the given isomorphism and thus is Cartier. For any morphism satisfying the blowup lifting condition, take its unique lift to the original blowup and compose with the inverse isomorphism. This gives a lift to the new source. Any other lift would compose with the forward isomorphism to give the original lift, proving uniqueness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompact_of_subset_isCompact: Cover the larger quasi-compact set by finitely many affine opens. Each of those opens is Noetherian because the scheme is locally Noetherian, so its intersection with the smaller set is quasi-compact. The smaller set is the finite union of those intersections and is quasi-compact.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompact_of_subset_noetherianSpace: Regard the given subset as a subset of the Noetherian subspace. Every subset of a Noetherian space is quasi-compact. Its image under the continuous inclusion is the original subset, hence is quasi-compact in the ambient space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isReduced_subscheme_strictTransform: The blowup is an isomorphism over the complement of the center. Under this isomorphism the open used in the strict transform identifies with the restriction of the original closed subscheme to that complement. It is therefore reduced because the original subscheme is reduced.
