The same induction uses equality of the order loci at the current stage to transfer the center inclusion from the second ideal to the first. It gives the required divisibility and center condition for the first ideal. In either case the smoothness and normal crossings of the centers are inherited from the same sequence. The stagewise equality of the order loci is the corresponding conclusion of the induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.locallyOfFiniteType_projectionToBase_com: The structural morphism at each stage is smooth by induction along the blowups with strict normal crossings. Every smooth morphism is locally of finite type.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_orderAtLeastLocus_prod_map_of_forall: At an empty list the sum threshold is zero, so every point belongs to the order locus. For a nonempty list, the order lower bounds for the first factor and for the product of the tail add to a lower bound for their product, since multiplication of stalk ideal powers adds exponents. Induction gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_eq_and_exceptionalIdea: Induct on the stage to preserve the two containments between the transforms and the tuned bound. At stage zero they follow by pullback along the initial isomorphism, with tuning commuting with this pullback. At the current stage the containments identify the two order loci. The center hypothesis puts its support in this common locus. The strict normal crossings power criterion then puts both ideals in the respective powers of the center ideal. The total transforms thus have the required exceptional factorizations, and uniqueness identifies their quotients with the next controlled transforms of the sequence. The one-step blowup comparison carries both containments to the next stage. This proves equality of the order loci at every stage. Applying the center criterion at each step also gives the two families of exceptional divisibilities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_eq_of_pow_le_of_le_tun: Order loci reverse inclusion of ideals. Thus the inclusions placing the intermediate ideal between the input power and the tuned ideal put its order locus between theirs at the multiplied threshold. The order locus of the input power equals the original locus. The tuned ideal’s locus contains the original locus by the derivative weight bound. Together these give both desired inclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_pow_mul_eq_orderAtLeas: On a smooth scheme over the field the order of the given positive ideal power is the power exponent times the original order, with infinity allowed. The order-locus formula for powers at a multiplied threshold therefore identifies the two loci, using commutativity of multiplication of the threshold and exponent.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_subset_orderAtLeastLoc: At a point of the original order locus, the derivative of each index has order at least the mark minus that index. Raising each derivative ideal to the chosen exponent multiplies its order lower bound by that exponent. Taking their product adds these lower bounds, giving the tuning weight. Each qualifying weight is at least the target threshold, so every contributing product has its stalk in the requisite maximal-ideal power. Their supremum does too.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_le_and_le_tunedSheaf_of_isBlowupAlon: Pull back the first containment and use the two exceptional-factor identities. The power of the first identity has exceptional exponent equal to the mark times the power exponent, which is the same exceptional exponent as in the second identity. Cancel that common power to get the lower containment. For the upper one, the first transformed ideal is the controlled transform by uniqueness of the exceptional factorization. Pull back the original upper bound and apply the tuned-sheaf blowup estimate. Its right side is the tuned sheaf of the controlled transform times the common exceptional power. Cancel this power again to get the desired upper containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pow_le_tunedSheaf: Use the exponent function supported at derivative index zero with value equal to the power exponent. Its weight is the mark times that exponent. Its product is the original ideal to the given power, since all other factors are unit ideals. It occurs in the supremum at the multiplied threshold.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prod_map_range_pow_ite_eq: The range contains zero because it has positive length. The zero index supplies the indicated power, and at every other index the exponent is zero, giving the unit ideal. The product is therefore the single nontrivial factor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_projectionToBase_comp_of_snc: At stage zero the structural morphism is the original smooth morphism composed with the given smooth identification. At a successor stage the structural morphism is the blowup followed by the preceding structural morphism. The center has strict normal crossings, so the blowup is smooth over the field when the preceding stage is. Induction gives smoothness at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.stalkIdeal_iSup_le_of_forall: Choose an affine open containing the point. Evaluation of the supremum on this open takes the supremum of the section ideals. Extension to the stalk also preserves suprema, so the stalk of the supremum is the supremum of the individual stalk ideals. Since each lies in the stated ideal, their supremum does as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sum_map_range_eq_sum_range: Both sums are zero for the empty range. Increasing the range by one adds the same last term to the list sum and to the finite-set sum. Induction gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedSheafProperties_of_succ_le_of_mul_l: Use the supplied monotonicity and product containment for their two fields. The other fields are the marking equivalences, the derivative and maximal-contact identities, invariance, the exact product and power rules, derivative balance, and the order-locus comparison established by the preceding results. These provide every stated property.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dvd_foldr_lcm: Induct through the list. If the chosen number is the first entry, it divides the least common multiple of that entry and the tail’s least common multiple. If it lies in the tail, it divides the tail’s least common multiple by induction, which in turn divides the full one. An empty list has no member to check.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dvd_lcmUpTo: The list defining this least common multiple contains all integers from one through the bound. The chosen integer lies in that list and therefore divides its least common multiple.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.foldr_lcm_consecutive_pos: The empty list gives one. For a positive-length list starting at a positive number, the tail starts at the next positive number and has positive least common multiple by induction. The least common multiple of these two positive numbers is positive.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isDerivBalanced_tunedSheaf_mul_lcmUpTo: Evaluate the derivative-balance inequality on an arbitrary affine open. Derivative iterates and powers evaluate to the corresponding constructions on section ideals, and the tuned sheaf evaluates to the tuned ring ideal. The chosen common multiple is positive and divisible by all required weights, so the ring-level derivative power bound supplies the desired inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lcmUpTo_pos: The number is defined as the least common multiple of a consecutive list starting at one. The positivity result for such a list applies, including the empty list.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.le_of_not_natCast_succ_le: Infinity is above the indicated successor, so the hypothesis makes the extended natural number finite. An ordinary natural number below that successor is at most its predecessor, which gives the bound.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.orderAtLeastLocus_tunedSheaf_eq_and_orde: The given maximal-contact identity equates the derivative iterate one below the tuned threshold with the original derivative iterate one below the mark. The support of either iterate is its corresponding order locus, proving equality of the loci. For the bound, the original ideal has order at most the mark at every point, so its iterate one below the mark has order below two. This follows from the order-locus identity for differentiation. If the tuned ideal had order at least one above its threshold, differentiation one below the threshold would leave order at least two. The maximal-contact identity would then put the original iterate at order at least two, a contradiction. Thus the tuned order is bounded by its threshold everywhere.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedSheaf_mul_eq_add: Evaluate the sheaves on an affine open. The section ideals are the corresponding tuned ring ideals, and evaluation preserves products. The least common multiple of one through the mark is positive and divisible by every weight in the range. The ring-level tuned product equality therefore gives equality on each affine open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedSheaf_pow_eq_mul: On every affine open, the section ideal of the power is the power of the tuned ring ideal. The chosen common multiple is positive and divisible by every weight from one through the mark. Apply the ring-level equality for positive powers to obtain the section ideal at the multiplied threshold. This gives the sheaf equality.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iSup_mul_iSup_le: On an affine open the section ideal of the product is the product of the section ideals, and each supremum is computed on section ideals. Multiplication of ideals distributes over the suprema. The resulting pairwise products all lie in the target section ideal by hypothesis, so their supremum does too.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ideal_iSup: The supremum of ideal sheaves is evaluated on each affine open by taking the supremum of the section ideals. Applying this description to the given family gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.listProd_map_pow_mul_listProd_map_pow: Pair the factors at each position in the two list products. Commutativity allows this grouping. The product of those two powers is the power with the sum of their exponents, giving the displayed list product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedSheaf_mul_le_add: Expand both tuned sheaves as suprema of products of derivative ideal powers. It suffices to bound each pair of product terms. Their product is the term obtained by adding the exponent functions. The weighted sum of the added exponents is the sum of their weights and is therefore at least the sum of the two thresholds. This term appears in the target supremum, giving the containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.tunedSheaf_succ_le: Each exponent function admitted at the successor threshold has weight at least the original threshold. Its product term therefore also occurs in the supremum at the original threshold. Taking the supremum proves the containment.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em._root_.FunctorialResolution.Blowup.IsLoc: The power of an ideal locally generated by a nonzerodivisor has the same property, with the corresponding power as local generator. Cancel this common power from the given containment using local cancellation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_prod_map_range: Pullback preserves the unit ideal, giving the empty-product case. Extending the range by one appends one factor. Pullback preserves its product with the previous factors, so induction gives the claimed formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_tunedSheaf_le_exceptionalIdeal_pow: Expand the tuned sheaf as the supremum over exponent functions meeting the threshold. Pullback distributes over the supremum and each product of derivative powers. The blowup derivative estimate bounds the pullback of the derivative at each index by the derivative of the controlled transform times the exceptional power with exponent equal to the mark minus that index. After raising to the chosen exponents and multiplying, the exceptional exponents add to the tuning weight. The weight is at least the threshold, so the resulting power is contained in the specified exceptional power. The other product is one of the terms defining the tuned sheaf upstairs. Taking the supremum gives the containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_tunedSheaf_of_smooth: The exponent functions admitted by the tuning threshold are the same upstairs and downstairs. Smooth pullback commutes with each derivative iterate and preserves powers and products. Hence each upstairs term is the pullback of the corresponding downstairs term. Pullback preserves the supremum of these terms, proving the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prod_map_pow_mul_pow_eq: For each index, the power of its product is the corresponding power of the exceptional factor times the power of the other factor. In the first factor the two exponents multiply. Commutativity groups all powers of the common ideal together, so their exponents add to the weighted sum. The other factors form the remaining product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prod_map_range_congr: The two functions agree at every index present in the range, so the lists of factors agree. Their products are therefore equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prod_map_range_le: Every index in the range satisfies the hypothesis, so each factor of the first product lies in the corresponding factor of the second. Monotonicity of multiplication gives containment of the products.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompatibleWithEtaleCovers_affineResolu: Obtain the local ambient embedding property for smooth pullbacks from smoothness of affine space and the graph-chart theorem. The étale-cover compatibility theorem with this property gives the result.

Apply the étale-cover comparison theorem for a presented selection to the embedded principalization rule and the affine-space selection. Embedding independence, smooth ambient functoriality, and properness of centers give the rule hypotheses. Local ambient embeddings for smooth pullbacks and the empty-boundary theorem provide the geometric hypotheses. The rule associated to this selection is precisely the affine principalization rule.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompatibleWithFieldBaseChange_affineRe: Use the field base-change theorem for a presented selection with the affine-space embedding choice. The embedded principalization rule is independent of the presented embedding and compatible with field base change, and the empty boundary on a smooth scheme has strict normal crossings. These hypotheses give field base-change compatibility for the selected affine rule, which agrees with the affine principalization rule.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isCompatibleWithOpenImmersions_affineRes: Smoothness of affine space gives local ambient embeddings for smooth pullbacks through the graph-chart construction. Insert this result into the open-immersion compatibility theorem for affine principalization.

Use the affine-space presentation selection for the embedded principalization rule. This rule is independent of the presented embedding, is compatible with smooth ambient maps, and has proper centers. The local ambient embedding assumption and the empty-boundary result for smooth schemes therefore give open-immersion compatibility of the associated affine rule. The selected embedding is the affine-space embedding, for which this associated rule agrees with the affine principalization rule.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullbackBlowupSequence_affineResolutio: Apply the smooth pullback comparison for presented selections to the embedded principalization rule and the affine-space selection at the stated relative dimension. Its rule hypotheses follow from embedding independence, smooth ambient functoriality and proper centers. The local ambient embedding theorem and the empty-boundary theorem give the geometric hypotheses. At both source and target the selected rule is the affine principalization rule, yielding the stated pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smoothPullbackHasLocalAmbientEmbedding_o: The graph-chart theorem supplies local graph charts for smooth pullbacks. The local ambient embedding construction applied to these charts uses smoothness of affine space and gives the asserted embeddings.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceIsoOfEquiv_hom: A reindexing map pulls target coordinates back to the source coordinates. The forward isomorphism therefore uses the inverse bijection to send target indices to source indices, as in its definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceIsoOfEquiv_hom_comp_over: Reindexing changes the coordinate labels and preserves the structure morphism. Composing the forward reindexing with the target projection therefore gives the source projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceIsoOfEquiv_hom_comp_toSpec: Apply compatibility of coordinate reindexing with the structural projection when the base is the field spectrum.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceIsoOfEquiv_inv: The inverse isomorphism goes in the opposite direction and is defined by reindexing along the original bijection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpace_reindex_comp_reindex_symm: The composite is over the base. Its pullback on each coordinate first applies the inverse bijection to the index and then applies the bijection, recovering that coordinate. The coordinate characterization of maps into affine space gives the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpace_reindex_symm_comp_reindex: The composite preserves the structural map to the base. On each coordinate, its pullback reindexes first by the bijection and then by its inverse, so the coordinate returns to itself. These data determine the identity map of the affine space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_toAffineSpaceOfAmbie: The inclusion by one zero coordinate has smooth coordinate codimension one. Transport this codimension through the target reindexing, which is over the field, and through the source isomorphism from the ambient scheme. This gives coordinate codimension one for the composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_toAffineSpaceOfAmbient: The map first identifies the ambient scheme with affine space, then includes it as the zero locus of the extra coordinate, and finally reindexes the coordinates by an isomorphism. The middle map is a closed immersion, and the two isomorphisms preserve this property under composition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toAffineSpaceOfAmbientIso_comp_toSpec: The last coordinate reindexing respects the projection to the field, as does the inclusion by a zero coordinate. The composite with the field projection therefore reduces to the structural map on the original affine space composed with the given ambient isomorphism. This is the ambient structural map by hypothesis.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceChartBaseChangeAmbientIso_hom: First identify the ambient of the base-changed datum with the base change of its original affine space. This identification preserves its structural projection. The affine-space base-change isomorphism also respects the projection to the extension field, so their composite has the required projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceEmbeddingDatum_baseChange_amb: The original datum takes affine space of the chosen dimension as its ambient scheme. Changing the field in the datum changes the ambient scheme by taking its fiber product over the original field, giving the stated base change of affine space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeAffineSpaceIso_hom_comp_toSpec: The chosen base-change isomorphism was selected with compatibility with the structural map to the extension field. Its composite with the target projection is therefore the second projection defining the base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_baseChangeAffineSpaceIso: The base change of the original affine space and the affine space with the same coordinates over the extended field both satisfy the pullback property for the original structural map and the map of fields. The unique isomorphism of those two pullbacks respects their second projections, so it is over the extension field.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceIsoSpecMvPolynomial_inv_appTo: The affine-space isomorphism with the polynomial spectrum gives the universal coordinate sections on that spectrum. Pulling the specified coordinate back along its inverse gives the section of the corresponding polynomial variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_hom_inv_apply: The two pullbacks compose to pullback along the identity on the other scheme, since the forward map and its inverse compose to that identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_inv_hom_apply: Pulling back along the isomorphism and then along its inverse is pullback along their identity composite. The section is therefore unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.globalSectionsToMvPolynomial_apply: Pull the affine-space section back to the polynomial spectrum along the inverse isomorphism. The identification of sections on a spectrum with its ring then gives the corresponding polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.leftInverse_globalSectionsToMvPolynomial: Starting with a polynomial, the two maps first identify it with a section on its spectrum, then successively pull back along the forward and inverse scheme isomorphisms. Those pullbacks cancel. Returning from sections on the spectrum to polynomials recovers the original polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_C: On the polynomial spectrum the structural map to the field spectrum is induced by the inclusion of constants. By naturality of the identification of a ring with sections on its spectrum, pulling back a field element along this map gives the section corresponding to the constant polynomial. Transfer this equality to affine space using the isomorphism over the field.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_X: The section of the polynomial variable on the spectrum is the pullback of the corresponding affine coordinate along the inverse isomorphism. The forward polynomial-to-section map pulls it back along the opposite isomorphism, recovering that coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_apply: The forward map of the equivalence is the polynomial-to-section map. It identifies the polynomial with a section on the spectrum and pulls back along the affine-space isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_basicOpe: The section associated to the polynomial is pulled back from the polynomial spectrum along the affine-space isomorphism. A basic open for a pulled-back section is the inverse image of the basic open for the original section.
The basic open of the section on the polynomial spectrum is exactly the prime-spectrum basic open of its corresponding polynomial. Substitute this in the inverse-image formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_symm_app: The inverse of the equivalence uses the section-to-polynomial map. It transfers the section to the spectrum along the inverse affine-space isomorphism and then identifies it with a polynomial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialEquivGlobalSections_symm_coo: The forward equivalence sends the specified polynomial variable to the coordinate section. Applying the inverse returns that variable.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToGlobalSections_apply: The map first regards the polynomial as a global section of its spectrum, then pulls it back along the affine-space isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.rightInverse_globalSectionsToMvPolynomia: Starting with a section, pull it back to the spectrum and regard it as a polynomial. The forward map reverses the identification of sections on the spectrum with polynomials, then pulls back along the inverse of the first pullback. The result is the original section.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.EmbeddingDatum.ofClosedImmersionAffineSp: The datum for a closed immersion into affine space takes that affine space itself as the ambient scheme, which gives the stated ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.id: Use the identity as the comparison at every stage. The lengths are equal, the base projections are preserved, and each comparison square over the identity is a pullback. Pullback of a center ideal along an identity fixes the ideal. These give a strict pullback of the sequence along the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceInl_comp_affineSpaceIndexedBy: The first-block inclusion appends zero coordinates using the original structural map over the field. Thus composing it with the product structural map returns the original structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceInrEmbedding_comp_affineSpace: The second-block inclusion puts zeros in the first block and is defined over the field. Its composite with the product structure map is the second block's structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_apply_eq: The global-section map of a composite pulls back first through its second morphism and then through its first morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.base_injective_of_isClosedImmersion: A closed immersion induces a closed embedding of underlying topological spaces, and an embedding is injective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_affineSpaceInl: Both maps have the given structural map. The composite pulls first-block coordinates back by the original map and pulls second-block coordinates back to zero. These are exactly the coordinates of the defining vector, so the maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_affineSpaceInrEmbedding: The two maps are over the same field map. The composite pulls first-block coordinates back to zero and second-block coordinates back through the original map. These are the entries of the second-block vector, which determine its affine-space map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inStrictNormalCrossingPosition_nil_affin: The affine-space structural map is smooth by hypothesis. The empty-boundary theorem for smooth schemes gives strict normal crossing position for its empty boundary.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_affineSpaceInl: The first-block inclusion is over the field. Each source coordinate is the pullback of the coordinate at the same index in the first block of the target. The criterion for closed immersion using coordinate lifts therefore applies.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_affineSpaceInrEmbeddin: The second-block inclusion preserves the structure map. Every coordinate of its source lifts to the corresponding second-block coordinate of the target. The coordinate-surjectivity criterion makes the map a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_of_coord_surjective: For each source coordinate choose a section of the target that pulls back to it. These sections define a morphism back into the source affine space over the base. Its composite after the given map fixes the structure map and every coordinate, so it is the identity. On global sections the given map therefore has a right inverse and is surjective. Between affine schemes this makes the original map a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_range_of_isClosedImmersion: The map of spaces underlying a closed immersion is a closed embedding. Its image is therefore closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isomorphic_of_isPullbackSequenceOfBlowup: The identity of the base is surjective. Because each target center is proper, the given comparison along the identity is strict by the surjectivity criterion. The target sequence is also its own strict pullback along the identity, so uniqueness of strict pullbacks gives the sequence isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_ker_comp: The larger ambient space is irreducible, so it suffices to show that the composite's support is proper. For the composite closed immersion this support is its image. If the image were all of the larger ambient space, injectivity of the second immersion would force the first to be surjective onto its ambient space. The larger ambient space is nonempty, so surjectivity of the composite also supplies a point of the first ambient space. Any irreducible component through this point would lie in the support of the first immersion's kernel by surjectivity, contradicting its componentwise nonvanishing.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nonzeroOnComponents_of_support_ne_univ: In an irreducible space the whole space is irreducible, so maximality makes every irreducible component the whole space. If the support contained a component it would equal the whole space, contrary to its properness.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_affineSpaceInl: The coordinate vector of the inclusion keeps every first-block coordinate and gives zero in the second block. Pullbacks of target coordinates are the entries of this vector.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_affineSpaceInl_inl: Apply the coordinate formula for the first-block inclusion to an index in the first block. It returns the corresponding source coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_affineSpaceInl_inr: The second-block entries of the coordinate vector are zero, so each coordinate in that block pulls back to zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_affineSpaceInrEmbedding: The defining coordinate vector for the second-block inclusion has zero first-block entries and the original coordinates in the second block. The pullback formula for maps defined by coordinate vectors gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_affineSpaceInrEmbedding_in: Apply the coordinate formula for the second-block inclusion at a first-block index, where the vector has value zero.
At a second-block index the coordinate formula for this inclusion returns the corresponding source coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_id: A coordinate is a global section, and its pullback along the identity is that same section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_affineSpaceIndexedByToSpec: The assumption on affine space gives smoothness of the structural map for every dimension. Apply it to the chosen field and dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_ker_eq_range_of_isClosedImmersio: The support of the kernel ideal sheaf is the closure of the morphism's image. The image of a closed immersion is already closed, so it equals that support.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceInl_comp_projLeft: The composite preserves the structural map and pulls each coordinate back to itself because first-block projection recovers the coordinates retained by the first-block inclusion. It is therefore the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceInl_comp_projLeft_assoc: The first-block inclusion followed by its projection is the identity. Following this by the given map returns the given map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceInl_comp_projRight: Both maps have the original structural map to the field. The projection to the second block reads only the zero coordinates appended by the first inclusion, so every coordinate pulls back to zero. This agrees with the map through the origin of the second block.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceInrEmbedding_comp_projLeft: The two maps preserve the field structure. The second-block inclusion sets all first-block coordinates to zero, so the first projection after it has the same coordinate pullbacks as the composite through the first-block origin.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceInrEmbedding_comp_projRight: The composite is over the field and recovers each second-block coordinate retained by the inclusion. By the coordinate characterization it is the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceInrEmbedding_comp_projRight_a: The second-block inclusion followed by its projection is the identity. Composing with the given map therefore gives that map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceOrigin_appTop_coord: The map on global sections sends each target coordinate to the corresponding entry of the defining vector of the origin. This entry is zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceOrigin_comp_toSpec: The origin is the affine-space map defined by zero coordinates over the identity of the field spectrum. Composing with the structure map recovers that identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceOrigin_comp_toSpec_assoc: The origin followed by the structure map is the identity on the field spectrum. Composing with the given map therefore returns the given map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_hom_appTop_inv_apply: The successive pullbacks are the pullback along the composite of the isomorphism and its inverse. That composite is the identity, which fixes every section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_id: Pullback of global sections is a contravariant functor. Its value on the identity scheme map is the identity ring map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_affineSpaceOrigin_of_pullbackCoord_eq: A morphism into affine space is determined by its structural map and the pullback of each coordinate. The given map has the identity as its structural map and sends all coordinates to zero, just as the origin does.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_affineSpaceInl: Use the whole target affine space as the chart domain, with the projection to the second block as the chart. It is smooth and over the field. The kernel of the first-block inclusion is the pullback along this projection of the origin ideal of the second block. That ideal is generated by all its coordinates, giving the stated codimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_affineSpaceInrEmbedd: Take the entire target as the chart and the smooth projection to the first block as its coordinate map over the field. The defining ideal of the inclusion is the pullback of the first-block origin ideal, which is generated by its full set of coordinates. This yields the required codimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_affineSpaceOrigin: The structural map after the origin is the identity, so pullback along the structural map is a right inverse to pullback along the origin on global sections. Thus the origin's section map is surjective. Both schemes are affine, so the origin is a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_affineSpaceInrEmbedding_projL: Place the square above the affine product square. The second projection of the inclusion is the identity and the structure map of the first-block origin after that origin is the identity. These identify the outer rectangle with the pullback of an identity. The inner square commutes by the first-projection formula for the second-block inclusion, so cancelling the product square proves the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_affineSpaceInl_eq_comap: The first-block inclusion is the pullback of the second-block origin along the second projection. To see this, use the affine product square and cancel it from the outer rectangle, which is a pullback because both the first projection of the inclusion and the field projection of the origin are identities. The second projection is smooth and hence flat, and the closed immersions in the square are quasi-compact. The flat pullback formula for kernels gives the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_affineSpaceInrEmbedding_eq_comap: The second-block inclusion is the base change of the first-block origin along the first projection. This projection is smooth and therefore flat, and the two closed immersions are quasi-compact. Apply the flat pullback formula to identify their kernel ideals.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_affineSpaceOrigin: On an affine scheme the kernel ideal sheaf of this quasi-compact map is determined by the kernel on global sections. This kernel is generated by all the coordinate sections, which is the global ideal of the full coordinate subspace ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_appTop_affineSpaceOrigin: Compose the origin's section map with the surjection from polynomials to affine-space sections. The composite sends every variable to zero and has nontrivial target, so its kernel is generated by the variables. By surjectivity, the original kernel is generated by their images in the section ring. Those images are precisely the affine coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_span_image_of_surjective: The kernel of the composite is the inverse image of the second map's kernel along the first map. Since the first map is surjective, mapping this inverse image forward recovers the second kernel. Mapping an ideal generated by a set gives the ideal generated by its images, yielding the asserted formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_span_range_X: Each variable maps to zero, so the ideal they generate lies in the kernel. Any polynomial differs from its constant term by an element of this ideal. If it lies in the kernel, its constant term also maps to zero. The restriction of the ring map to the coefficient field is injective because the target is nontrivial, so that constant term is zero. The polynomial then belongs to the variable ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToSections_X: Under the inverse affine-space isomorphism, the coordinate pulls back to the section of its corresponding polynomial variable. The polynomial-to-section map then pulls this section back along the forward isomorphism, recovering the original coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToSections_apply: The section associated to a polynomial is obtained by first taking its section on the polynomial spectrum and then pulling back along the affine-space isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mvPolynomialToSections_surjective: Given an affine-space section, pull it back along the inverse isomorphism to the polynomial spectrum. Take the polynomial corresponding to this section. Both steps are reversed by the polynomial-to-section map, so the chosen polynomial maps to the original section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.nontrivial_globalSections_spec: The global sections of the field spectrum identify with the field. Under this identification zero and one are distinct, so the section ring is nontrivial.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_affineSpaceOrigin: The defining vector of the origin is zero at every coordinate. Its pullback of the specified coordinate is therefore zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_comp_eq_hom_appTop_apply: Pulling the coordinate back along a composite pulls it back along the second map and then applies the first map's pullback on sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sub_C_constantCoeff_mem_span_X: Subtract the constant term. Every remaining monomial contains at least one variable and hence lies in the ideal generated by the variables. Equivalently, polynomial induction gives zero for a constant, preserves the assertion under addition, and gives a multiple of a generator for a polynomial multiplied by a variable.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eq_homOfSumCoords_of_comp_reindex: The equality of the first projections determines the structure map. Each coordinate index belongs to exactly one of the two blocks because the indexing map is a bijection. For each block the given equality of projections determines its coordinate pullbacks, which are the corresponding entries of the combined map. Thus the original map equals the combined one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.homOfSumCoords_appTop_coord_inl: The coordinate index comes from the first block. The inverse indexing bijection returns that first-block index, so the section in the defining vector is its pullback along the first map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.homOfSumCoords_appTop_coord_inr: The inverse indexing bijection places this coordinate in the second block. Its section in the defining vector is the pullback along the second map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.homOfSumCoords_comp_reindex_inl: Both maps to the first affine space have the same structure map by construction. The first-block projection picks out exactly the first map's coordinate sections. Therefore the two maps coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.homOfSumCoords_comp_reindex_inr: The shared structure map equals that of the second map by the compatibility assumption. The second-block projection picks out precisely the second map's coordinate sections. These identities give equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_prodMapOnPreimage: The inverse image open is the product of the first-block open and the second affine block over the field. This follows by pasting its open restriction square with the original product square. The target of the product map is also a product over the field. The two projection identities show that the comparison is the given map on the first factor and the identity on the second. Cancelling the target product square gives the stated pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_projLeft_projRight: Apply the pullback result for any partition of the coordinates into two blocks to this disjoint indexing of the two finite coordinate sets.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_reindex_of_sumEquiv: The projections to the two blocks preserve the structural maps. For any pair of morphisms agreeing over the base, combine their coordinate sections in the indexing order. The resulting affine-space morphism has the two given projections. Any other morphism with these projections has the same structure map and coordinate pullbacks, so it is equal to the combined map. This proves the pullback property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.morphismRestrict_projLeft_comp: Both maps to the new first block preserve the structural map because the map out of the open is over the field. Their pullback of a first-block coordinate is the pullback along that map and then along the restricted projection, by the defining vector of the product map. Thus the maps agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prodMapOnPreimage_comp_affineSpaceIndexe: The product map is constructed from its coordinate sections over the field, using the given inverse image open's structural map. Its composite with the target structural map is therefore the structural map of that open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.prodMapOnPreimage_comp_projRight: Both maps to the second affine block preserve the structural map. They pull back each coordinate to the restriction of the corresponding original second-block coordinate, by the definition of the product map. These equalities determine the morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projLeft_appTop_coord: The first projection pulls a coordinate on the first factor back to its corresponding coordinate in the first block of the product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projLeft_comp_affineSpaceIndexedByToSpec: Projection to the first block is a reindexing over the field. Following it by the first block's structural map returns the structural map of the product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projRight_appTop_coord: Pullback of a second-factor coordinate along the second projection is the corresponding coordinate in the second block of the product.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.projRight_comp_affineSpaceIndexedByToSpe: Projection to the second block is a reindexing over the field, so the structural map of the second block composed with this projection is the original structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_prodMapOnPreimage: The product pullback square identifies the product map with base change of the given smooth map along the projection to the new first block. Smoothness is preserved by base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_projLeft: The projection to the first affine space is the base change of the second affine space's structural map along the first structural map. The second structural map is smooth, so its base change is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_projRight: The projection to the second affine space is the base change of the first affine space's structural map along the second structural map. The first structural map is smooth, so its base change is smooth.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumUliftEquivUliftSum_inl: On an element in the first block, the bijection retains the same index in the first block of the combined index set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumUliftEquivUliftSum_inr: On an element in the second block, the bijection retains the same index in the second block of the combined index set.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumUliftEquivUliftSum_symm_inl: The inverse bijection recovers the first summand and the original first-block index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.sumUliftEquivUliftSum_symm_inr: The inverse bijection recovers the second summand and the original second-block index.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSpaceOrigin_comp_affineSpaceInl_af: The composite is over the field. After undoing the coordinate reindexing, a coordinate lies in one of the two blocks. In the first block it pulls back along the origin and is zero. In the second block it pulls back along the zero-coordinate inclusion and is already zero. A map over the field with all coordinates zero is the origin of the combined space.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_affineSpaceInl:
At each point choose an original smooth coordinate chart for the closed immersion and take its inverse image under the first projection of the enlarged affine space. The enlarged point belongs to this open since the projection undoes the zero-coordinate inclusion. The product of the original coordinate map and the unchanged added block is smooth and preserves the structural map to the field. Reindex its two blocks together.

The restriction of the original immersion is defined by the pullback of the original ideal. In the original chart, this restriction is also the pullback of the origin in the coordinate space. The restricted zero section is a pullback of the enlarged zero inclusion, and the product chart carries it to the corresponding zero section in the chart's target. Pasting these pullbacks identifies the restriction of the enlarged immersion with the pullback of the enlarged origin along the reindexed product chart. The origin ideal is generated by all coordinates, so the restricted defining ideal is the pullback of the coordinate ideal for the original number of equations plus the number of added coordinates.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_affineSpaceInl_affineSpaceIsoOfEqui: Adding the zero-coordinate block increases the smooth coordinate codimension by the size of the block. Reindexing the two blocks by an isomorphism over the field preserves that codimension, so the final composite has the stated value.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isPullback_of_ker_eq_comap: Identify each of the two closed immersions with the inclusion of the closed subscheme of its ideal. By hypothesis the second ideal is the pullback of the first, so the canonical map between these two closed subschemes gives a pullback square over the ambient map. Transport the square through the identifications to get the comparison of the original sources.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_subscheme_of_ker_eq: A closed immersion identifies its source with its scheme-theoretic image. This image is the closed subscheme of its kernel ideal sheaf, which is the specified ideal. The identification followed by the subscheme inclusion is the original immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_zeroSectionOverOpen: The zero-coordinate inclusion on the given open has image in the inverse image open, so it factors uniquely through its open immersion. Following the factor by the restricted projection gives the identity because composing with the original open inclusion gives that inclusion, and the inclusion is a monomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_zeroSectionOverOpen: The product map sends the zero section to the zero section after the given map. On the first block both composites give the given map since projection splits the zero section. On the second block both give the zero coordinates over the same field map. To show that the square is a pullback, paste it with the product map's pullback square over the first projection. The outer rectangle has identity horizontal maps because both zero sections split their projections. It is a pullback, so cancellation of the product square proves the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ker_eq_comap_ker_of_isPullback_closedImm: Identify the given pullback with the canonical pullback of the closed immersion. The ideal of the resulting closed subscheme is the pullback of the original defining ideal. The identification is an isomorphism on the source, which preserves the kernel ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_affineSpaceIsoOfEquiv_hom: The forward affine-space isomorphism uses the inverse bijection on coordinate indices, so the pulled-back coordinate is the original coordinate at that inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_comp_eq_appTop: A coordinate pulled back along the composite is pulled back first to the intermediate scheme and then to the source, by functoriality of sections.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.range_affineSpaceInl_subset_range_opensP: A point of the open maps by the zero-coordinate inclusion to a point whose first projection is its original image in the open. The new point is therefore in the inverse image open and lies in the range of its inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.uliftFinSumEquiv_inl: The indexing bijection places the first block at the beginning of the combined list. The index in this block retains its original position.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.uliftFinSumEquiv_inr: The indexing bijection places the second block after the whole first block. Its index in the combined list is therefore shifted by the length of the first block.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zeroSectionOverOpen_comp_restrict: The chosen zero section is a section of the restricted first projection, so their composite is the identity of the open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zeroSectionOverOpen_comp_restrict_assoc: The restricted projection after the zero section is the identity. Following that composite by the given map therefore gives the map itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zeroSectionOverOpen_comp_ι: The zero section over the open is the chosen factorization of the original zero-coordinate inclusion through the inverse image open. Its composite with that open inclusion is therefore the original inclusion restricted to the given open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.zeroSectionOverOpen_comp_ι_assoc: First compose the restricted zero section with the inverse image open inclusion, which gives the original zero-coordinate inclusion restricted to the open. Then compose both equal maps with the given morphism.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_basicOpenEmbedding_lastCoordinate: The immersion assigns the inverse of the pulled-back defining function to the last coordinate. Thus the product of that coordinate and the defining function pulls back to one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_comp_projLeft_coord: Pullback along a composite is successive pullback in reverse order. The first projection pulls the specified coordinate back to the corresponding first-block coordinate of the product, which is then pulled back along the given map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_globalSectionLift: The chosen lift is a preimage under the map on sections of the closed immersion. Applying that map returns the original section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appTop_surjective_of_isAffine: A closed immersion into an affine scheme is induced by a quotient of the ambient section ring, so its map on global sections is surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.basicOpenEmbedding_comp_affineSpaceIndex: The structure map of the product factors through the first projection. After this projection the constructed embedding is the original embedding on the basic open. The latter is over the given structural map, yielding the asserted composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.basicOpenToPullbackBasicOpen_comp_projLe: The chosen immersion was constructed with original coordinates in its first block. After the open inclusion and the first projection it is the original embedding restricted to the source basic open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_appTop_eq_of_isClosedImmersion: The map on global sections of the closed immersion is surjective because its target is affine. Thus the given section has a preimage in the ambient section ring.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_comp_ι_eq_replaceLastCoord: Membership in the pulled-back basic open depends only on the first projection, and coordinate replacement preserves that projection. The replacement map thus lands in the open. The open immersion universal property gives the factorization.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isClosedImmersion_basicOpen_pullb: Lift the function defining the source basic open to the ambient affine space. Its pullback along the first projection and then the padded embedding is the original function, since first projection undoes the padding. Thus the inverse image of the ambient pulled-back basic open is the source basic open. Apply the preceding closed immersion construction to this open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isClosedImmersion_pullbackBasicOp: First embed by adding a zero last coordinate, then restrict the closed immersion to the inverse image of the pulled-back basic open. On that open add the inverse of the pulled-back defining section to the last coordinate. This translation is an isomorphism, so the composite is still a closed immersion. Projection to the first block undoes the zero-coordinate inclusion and is unchanged by translation. The last coordinate starts at zero and becomes the inverse of the defining section. Its product with that section is one on the image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_replaceLastCoord: Use the affine-space coordinate construction over the structural map of the open. Take its first-block entries from the open inclusion and use the given section for the last entry. This gives the prescribed pullbacks and structural map. After projecting to the first block, the resulting map and the projected open inclusion agree over the field and on every first-block coordinate, so the projections agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.false_of_isUnit_map_zero: A ring map sends zero to zero. In a nontrivial ring zero is not a unit, contradicting the assumption.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_basicOpenEmbedding: The ambient defining section pulls back along the padded original embedding to the source defining section, so the domain is the inverse image of the required ambient open. The constructed immersion has the original first projection and satisfies the inverse-coordinate equation. The codimension result for that construction therefore gives the original codimension plus one. Reindexing the coordinate blocks by an isomorphism over the field preserves the codimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_comp_opens_ι: At a point of the closed immersion choose a smooth chart inside the open ambient subscheme. Its composite open inclusion into the larger ambient scheme identifies the chart with its open image. Transfer the smooth coordinate map through this isomorphism, preserving the structural map. The ideal of the larger closed immersion restricts on the ambient open to the original ideal. The transferred coordinates therefore pull back to the same restricted ideal and give the same codimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hasSmoothCoordCodim_comp_pullbackBasicOp:
Inside the pulled-back basic open, compare the given immersion with the original immersion padded by a zero and then translated by the inverse defining section. Their first projections coincide by hypothesis, hence their first coordinates and structure maps agree. The product relation determines the last coordinate of the given immersion as the inverse of the pulled-back defining section, which is exactly the last coordinate of the translated immersion. Equality of coordinates identifies the two maps, since the open inclusion is a monomorphism.

Adding a zero coordinate increases the original codimension by one. Restricting to the pulled-back basic open preserves that codimension, and the translation is an isomorphism over the field, so it preserves it as well. The codimension of the closed immersion into the whole ambient space is then the same as in the open by the preceding open-inclusion result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_basicOpenEmbedding: The map is a closed immersion into the pulled-back basic open followed by an open immersion, so it is a preimmersion. Its image is closed within that open. On its image the last coordinate times the lifted function equals one, so the image lies in the closed zero locus of their product minus one. Conversely, any point of that zero locus has the lifted function invertible in its local ring. Indeed the product minus one is a nonunit there, so the lifted function is a unit by the local-ring criterion. Thus the whole zero locus lies in the pulled-back basic open. A subset closed in that open and contained in this ambient closed locus is closed in the whole ambient space. A preimmersion with closed image is a closed immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosedImmersion_basicOpenToPullbackBas: The selected map was chosen from the construction of a closed immersion into the pulled-back basic open. It therefore has the required closed immersion property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isClosed_image_of_isInducing: Since the topology on the source is induced, its closed subset is the inverse image of a closed subset of the target. Its image is therefore the intersection of this closed subset with the range of the map. The given image lies in the second closed subset, and that subset lies in the range. Thus intersecting the first closed subset with the second gives exactly the image, proving it is closed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_shiftLastCoord_lastCoordinate_add_: Use subtraction of the inverse unit from the last coordinate as the inverse to addition of the inverse unit. Both transformations fix that inverse unit because it comes from the first projection. Either composite restores the last coordinate by cancellation and fixes the structural map and first block, so both composites are identities.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_shiftLastCoord_shiftLastCoordSecti: This section is the last coordinate plus the inverse unit, so the established inverse translation gives an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_appTop_ι_basicOpen: On the basic open the defining section pulls back to a section whose own basic open is the whole scheme. Its germ is therefore a unit at every point. A section is a unit if it is a unit in every stalk, so the restricted section is invertible.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_appTop_ι_pullbackAlongProjection: The open is the basic open of the section pulled back along the projection. Restricting that defining section to its basic open makes it a unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isUnit_map_of_not_isUnit_map_mul_sub_one: In a local ring either the product of the two images or one minus that product is a unit. The latter would make its negative a unit, contrary to the hypothesis. Hence the product is a unit, and so its second factor is a unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastCoordinate_appTop_comp_affineSpaceIn: The zero-coordinate inclusion pulls the last coordinate back to zero. Further pullback along the given map preserves zero.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastCoordinate_eq: The additional factor is an affine line. The last coordinate is defined as the coordinate of its unique index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.lastCoordinate_eq_coord: The affine-line index set has only one element. The specified index is therefore the defining index of the last coordinate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_pullbackBasicOpen_iff: The basic open of a pulled-back section is the inverse image of the original basic open. A point belongs to it exactly when its projection belongs to the original open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackAlongProjection_eq: This section is defined by pulling the given section back along the first projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackCoord_replaceLastCoord_inl: The replacement map keeps the original pullbacks of every first-block coordinate. The specified first-block coordinate has exactly the pullback given by the open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_appTop_lastCoordinate: The last entry of the defining coordinate vector is the specified section. The section map sends the last coordinate to that entry.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_appTop_pullbackAlongPro: The section comes from the first projection, and the replacement map has the same first projection as the open inclusion. Functoriality of pullback therefore gives equal values on this section.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_comp_affineSpaceIndexed: The chosen replacement map was constructed over the same structural map as the open inclusion. Composing with the affine-space structure map therefore gives that structural map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_comp_projLeft: The first projection is determined by its structural map and the first-block coordinates. The replacement map preserves all of these, so its first projection agrees with that of the open inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.replaceLastCoord_comp_projLeft_assoc: First compose the replacement map with the first projection. This gives the projected open inclusion. Composing this equality with the given map gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoordSection_eq: The section used for translation is defined as the restriction of the last coordinate plus the inverse of the distinguished unit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoord_appTop_unitOnPullbackBasi: Pullback fixes the underlying unit and preserves the product of the unit with its inverse. Thus the image of its inverse is again an inverse of the same unit, which is unique.

The unit is the restriction to the open of the section pulled back from the first projection. Pulling it back through the map into the open can be computed using coordinate replacement in the ambient space. That replacement fixes the projected section, so the unit's underlying section is fixed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoord_comp_shiftLastCoord: It suffices to compare the composite with the identity after the monomorphic open inclusion. Both replacements preserve the structure map and all first-block coordinates. The last coordinate of the composite pulls back to the second replacement section pulled back by the first map, which is the original last coordinate by hypothesis. These data determine the map into affine space, giving the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoord_comp_ι: The map into the open is chosen as the lift of the coordinate replacement through the open immersion. Its composite with that immersion is the replacement map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.shiftLastCoord_comp_ι_assoc: Compose the lift identity with the given morphism after the open inclusion. Associativity gives the displayed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.unitOnPullbackBasicOpen_val: The chosen unit is the one supplied by invertibility of the restricted section. Its underlying section is that restricted section.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_map_center_eq_center_of_isPullback: Use the overlap isomorphism to write the second overlap pullback on the first overlap object. Its compatibility with the overlap base maps allows pasting with the self-pullback square of the cover. The stage comparison square is a pullback, and the comparison maps agree on the overlap by hypothesis. Cancelling the stage square gives a self-pullback square for the stage comparison map. The center pulls back to the same ideal along the two projections of this square by the center compatibility. Flat ideal descent now shows that the pullback of its image along the stage comparison is exactly the original center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isPullback_blowup_proj_map_center: The original stage transition blows up the original center, which is the pullback of the image center by hypothesis. The canonical blowup of the image center pulls back along the flat comparison map to a blowup of that same original center. By the universal property, the two blowups are isomorphic over the stage. The comparison map furnished by this identification has the stated commuting equation and pullback square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_fst_of_isPullback: The first projection in the pullback is obtained by base change of the given flat morphism. Flatness is preserved by base change.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_iso_hom_comp: Precompose both projections with the given isomorphism of their source. This identifies the new square with the original pullback square, so it still satisfies the same universal property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_toBlowupOfMapCenter: The comparison map was chosen to exhibit the original blowup as the pullback of the image-center blowup along the stage comparison. The asserted pullback square is that property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_toBlowupOfMapCenter_projectio: Paste the pullback square comparing the blowups with the earlier pullback square comparing their bases. The resulting maps to the original and new bases are the successor projections, because each transition followed by the preceding projection equals the successor projection. Hence the pasted square is the asserted one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupOfMapCenter_cocycle: Compare the two overlap maps to the blowup of the descended center. Their composites with its projection coincide, since the overlap comparisons commute with the successor transitions and the preceding comparisons agree as maps to the descended stage. The descended center becomes locally generated by a non-zero-divisor on the blowup. It remains so after pulling back through the flat comparison to the local successor and then through the flat overlap projection. The uniqueness part of the blowup universal property therefore makes the two maps to the descended blowup equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.toBlowupOfMapCenter_comp_proj: The comparison was chosen with a commuting square over the original stage. Its composite with the descended blowup projection is the original blowup transition followed by the stage comparison.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_projectionToBase_eq_fst: At stage zero the base-changed initial isomorphism is the first pullback projection. At a successor, the projection to the new base factors through the previous stage. By induction the preceding projection is the first pullback projection, and the pullback transition preserves that projection. This gives the formula at every stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isStrictPullbackSequenceOfBlowups: Construct the descended sequence recursively from the given overlap data. It has the same length as the local sequence. At zero the descended object is the original base and the comparison is the local initial projection followed by the cover. At each successor the recursive blowup construction gives a pullback square with the local successor and identifies the local center with the pullback of the descended center. The tower uses exactly these successor maps. These facts are the required strict pullback comparison.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isStrictPullback_of_isomorphic_ba: The two sequences over the self-overlap have the same stage objects as the two pullbacks used in the descent datum. The sequence isomorphism identifies their centers and commutes with all successor maps. It also commutes with projections to the overlap base, since it commutes at stage zero and with the transitions. Those projections are the first pullback projections. Thus the isomorphisms and their equations give the descent datum, from which the descended blowup sequence exists.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeTowerObjZeroIso_hom: The initial isomorphism of the base-changed tower is the isomorphism given by the first projection from the pullback at stage zero. Its forward map is that projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeTower_map: The base-changed tower assigns the induced pullback transition to the opposite of the order arrow between the two stages. This is the stated map by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChangeTower_obj: The base-changed tower is defined at each stage by pulling the original projection to the base back along the given base map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_blowupMorphism: For the successor arrow the base-changed tower uses the induced pullback transition between the two consecutive stages.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_center: The new center is defined by pulling the original center back along the second projection to the original stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_isoObjZero_hom: The initial isomorphism is the first projection from the base-changed stage zero, which is a pullback of the original initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_length: The base-changed sequence is assigned the original length when it is constructed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.baseChange_schemeAt: The scheme at this stage is the corresponding object of the base-changed tower, which is the pullback of the original projection to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isBlowupAlongIdealSheaf_baseChangeTower_: The original successor map is the blowup of the original center. Its pulled-back successor square is a pullback, and the projection to the original earlier stage is flat as a base change of the given flat map. Flat base change of blowups gives the claim for the pulled-back center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_pullback_fst_projectionToBase_zero: The original projection at stage zero is an isomorphism. Construct an inverse to the first projection by lifting the identity on the new base and the new base map followed by the inverse initial projection. The pulled-back square commutes, so the lift exists. Its composite with the first projection is the identity, and the other composite is the identity because both its pullback projections agree with those of the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_pullbackTransitionMap: The pullbacks at both stages are formed over the same new base. The square formed by the pulled-back transition and the two projections to the original stages commutes by the second projection equation. Pasting it with the pullback square at the earlier stage gives the pullback square at the later stage, because the projection from the successor factors through the earlier one. The outer square and the earlier square are pullbacks, so the transition square is a pullback.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictPullbackSequenceOfBlowups_baseCh: The two lengths agree by construction. Take the second pullback projection to the original scheme as the comparison at every stage. At zero its compatibility with the initial maps is the pullback square. Every consecutive transition square is a pullback by the tower comparison, and every center is the pullback along the corresponding stage projection. These are exactly the strict pullback conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_comp_fst: By the defining projection equation of the pullback transition, its first projection equals the first projection of the later pullback. This expresses that the new base is held fixed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_comp_snd: The second projection of the pullback transition is the projection to the original later stage followed by the original transition to the earlier stage. This is its other defining projection equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_eq_comp: Both the direct map and the composite preserve the projection to the new base. Along the other projection, the composite is the later projection followed by the two original transitions. By functoriality their composite is the direct original transition, so the second projections agree as well. Pullback extensionality gives equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.pullbackTransitionMap_refl: Compare the two maps by their projections from the pullback. On the new base they give the same projection. On the original stage the transition from that stage to itself is the identity, so the second projections also agree. Uniqueness of pullback maps gives the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionMap_self_eq_id: The order arrow from a stage to itself is an identity. Taking its opposite and applying the tower functor preserves the identity, so the stage transition is the identity.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.CompatibleBaseIsoAt.blowupMorphism_squar: Compose the given equation with the forward base isomorphism. It cancels the inverse base isomorphism on the left and gives the desired commuting square.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.CompatibleBaseIsoAt.center_comap_eq: Pull the two ambient center ideals back along the first stage comparison. The commuting comparison square identifies the pullback through the proposed base isomorphism with the pullback through the second stage comparison and local isomorphism. Each local center is the pullback of its base center, and the local isomorphism identifies them. The resulting equality after pullback descends because the first comparison is flat and surjective.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.CompatibleBaseIsoAt.exists_iso_succ_blow: Compose the second blowup with the inverse of the current base isomorphism. This presents it as a blowup over the first base stage, along the pullback of its center. That pulled-back center is the first center by the descended equality. The uniqueness of the blowup along a given center yields an isomorphism of the two successor schemes over the first stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrictPullbackBlowupSeq.isomorphic_of_: Strict pullback preserves lengths, and the local isomorphism matches the two local lengths, so the original lengths agree. The stagewise pullback squares make the comparisons flat and surjective. Together with the local isomorphism and its center compatibility, these supply the descent data for constructing compatible base-stage isomorphisms through the final stage. The construction gives the initial and transition equations. At each stage faithful flatness descends the center equation. These facts make the base sequences isomorphic.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_isoObjZero_trans_symm_eq: The proposed stage-zero isomorphism passes through the common base using the two initial identifications. After composing both sides with the second initial isomorphism, the two base-comparison equations give maps that agree by the initial local isomorphism’s compatibility. Cancelling the second initial isomorphism gives the claim.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_compatible_isos_of_le: Induct on the length of the initial segment. At zero, the base-stage isomorphism passes through the common base and satisfies the chart comparison by the stage-zero equation. For a successor, the previous stage isomorphism already agrees with the local one. Faithfully flat ideal descent identifies the two center ideals there. The two blowups along these corresponding centers then have a successor isomorphism commuting with the transition maps. Keep all earlier isomorphisms. To check the new chart compatibility, compare the two maps from the local successor to the second base successor after projecting to the preceding base stage. The transition squares and the local isomorphism show these composites agree. The pulled-back center along their common composite is the local center pulled back to its blowup, so it is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. Uniqueness of the blowup lift gives equality of the two maps, completing the induction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.extendIsoFamilySucc_of_le: The enlarged family uses the previous family at any index at or below the previous endpoint, by the first case of its definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.extendIsoFamilySucc_self: The new endpoint is strictly greater than the previous endpoint. The definition therefore assigns it the newly specified isomorphism, with identity transport at that index.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.flat_and_surjective_of_isPullback_blowup: At zero the comparison square is a pullback because the two stage-zero structure maps are isomorphisms and the square commutes.
