Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartToLastObj_comp_lastStructMap_assoc: Compose the compatibility equation for the two final structural maps with the morphism to the field and reassociate. This gives precisely the equality of the two composites from the local final chart.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ringHom_smooth_appTop_of_smooth: Smoothness is local on the source, and on affine schemes it is equivalent to smoothness of the section-ring homomorphism. Apply this criterion to the chosen affine source chart and the affine target.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_appTop_affineCover_chartToLastObj: The map from the final chart to the field is smooth. Apply the affine chart criterion to one open in its affine cover. Reassociating the chart maps identifies the resulting smooth ring map with the stated one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_chartToLastObj_comp: The compatibility of the local and global final maps identifies the composite to the field with the local final structural map followed by the local base map to the field. This is smooth by the local resolution hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_lastStructMap_comp: Refine the open cover of the final scheme by the affine open cover of each chart. On each resulting affine open, the section-ring map to the field is smooth by the preceding local calculation. The affine source cover criterion gives smoothness of the global composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.smooth_of_ringHom_smooth_appTop: The target is affine and the source chart maps cover the source by affine opens. Smoothness of each corresponding section-ring map therefore implies smoothness on each chart. These local conditions imply smoothness globally.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appIso_inv_germ_stalkMap: Naturality of germs expresses taking the germ upstairs and pulling it to the source stalk as first pulling the section back and then taking its germ. The section map along an open immersion is inverse to the indicated section identification. These maps cancel, leaving the source germ map after identifying the inverse-image open with the original open.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.appIso_inv_germ_stalkMap_apply: Evaluate the commuting equation for the section identification and germ maps at the given section. The resulting equality of germs is the desired formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartToLastObj_preimage_smoothLocusCompl: For a point of the final local chart, the commuting square identifies its image in the global base with the image under the base chart map of its local base image. The inverse image of the global smooth-locus complement in the base chart equals the local smooth-locus complement. Applying these two facts pointwise gives equality of the inverse images.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_reducedInverseImage_chartToLastObj: Each reduced inverse image is the vanishing ideal of the corresponding inverse-image closed set. The local closed set is the inverse image of the global one by compatibility of the two structural maps. Pullback of a vanishing ideal along the chart open immersion is the vanishing ideal of that inverse image.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comap_vanishingIdeal_of_isOpenImmersion: On affine charts the pullback of the vanishing ideal along the open immersion is computed by inverse image under the section-ring identification. Inverse image preserves radicality. Its support is the inverse image of the original closed set and hence equals the given closed set. A radical ideal sheaf is the vanishing ideal of its support, so the two ideal sheaves agree.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularParameterSystem_map_ringEquiv: The isomorphism takes the unique maximal ideal of the first local ring to the unique maximal ideal of the second. It carries the ideal generated by the chosen parameters to the ideal generated by their images. Thus the images generate the new maximal ideal. Krull dimension is invariant under ring isomorphism, so their number still equals the dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularParameterSystem_of_ringEquiv_ap: The proposed list agrees pointwise with the image of the original parameter list under the isomorphism. The preservation of regular parameters under the isomorphism therefore applies to it.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_of_openCo: At a point of the ambient scheme choose the given chart and its local strict normal crossings description. The chart is an open immersion and identifies the local rings, so regularity and the regular parameter system transport to the ambient point. Transport the affine chart and its section parameters along the corresponding isomorphism of section rings. Compatibility with germs identifies their germs with the transported parameters. Under the section isomorphism the pulled-back ideal corresponds to the original ideal, and the product of the selected parameters maps to the product of their images. This gives a local strict normal crossings description at every ambient point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_reducedIn: The final local chart maps form an open cover of the final global scheme. On each chart the pullback of the global reduced inverse image is the local reduced inverse image of the local smooth-locus complement. The local resolution gives it strict normal crossings, and the open-cover criterion transfers the property to the global divisor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_eqToHom_germ: Identify the two equal opens. The transport becomes the identity on sections, and taking the germ gives the original germ map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_vanishingIdeal_eq: The reduced vanishing ideal of a closed set has that set as its support, by its construction on affine charts.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.surjective_iso_inv: For any element of the target of the inverse map, use its image under the forward map as a preimage. The two maps compose to the identity.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.canonicalAlgorithmRules_isCorrect: The correctness theorem for canonical rules assumes that strict transforms are the blowups of the corresponding closed subschemes. This compatibility is available, so the rules reduce inductively on dimension.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.chartIsolationHypotheses_principalizatio: Both vanishing assignments send a closed set to its reduced vanishing ideal. They are therefore equal pointwise. Apply the chart isolation result for the reduced assignment to this principalization algorithm and use the equality of assignments.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedLocusIsOpenForEmbeddings_princip: The canonical openness theorem applies using strict-transform compatibility, correctness of the canonical reduction, radicality of smooth subscheme ideals, and the chart isolation hypotheses for the vanishing-ideal assignment. It yields openness of the detached locus at every relevant stage for every embedding.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedPrincipalizationDiscardedLocusIs: For the given affine input, form the specified embedding into affine space. The discarded locus at any stage is the detached locus for these embedding data. The assumed openness of detached loci for every embedding applies to this one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.embeddedPrincipalizationYieldsBlowups_pr: The chosen affine embeddings have open discarded loci by detached-locus openness, and their ambient stages are Noetherian. Strict transforms satisfy the expected closed-subscheme blowup compatibility. The theorem constructing blowups from these data therefore applies to the embedded principalization sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isFunctorialPrincipalization_principaliz: Apply the functoriality theorem for canonical principalization. Its hypotheses follow from strict-transform compatibility, correctness of the dimension reduction, radicality of smooth subscheme ideals, and the closed-immersion commutation theorem for correct rules.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.transitionsAreBlowupsForEmbeddings_princ: Every detached locus is open for this principalization algorithm by the canonical openness result. The construction that separates the detached components then identifies the embedding transitions as blowups.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.IsStrongResolution.of_isomorphic: The final objects are isomorphic over the base, so smoothness over the field and properness of the original final map transfer to the new one. Restricting the final isomorphism over the smooth locus transfers the isomorphism property there. The homeomorphism of final spaces carries the dense smooth-locus inverse image to its counterpart. At each stage the comparison identifies both the centers and the projection to the base, so the new centers still lie over the singular locus. Finally, the strict normal crossings description of the reduced inverse image of that locus transports along the final isomorphism. Thus all strong resolution conditions hold.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.Isomorphic.exists_last: Use the stage isomorphism at the final index of the first sequence. Equality of lengths identifies the corresponding stage of the second sequence with its final object. The stagewise compatibility with projections to the base gives the required compatibility of the final structural maps.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.Isomorphic.symm: Use the inverse isomorphism at each stage and reverse the equality of lengths. The initial compatibility inverts, and the commuting transition squares remain commutative after replacing the vertical maps by their inverses. The center pullback identities reverse as well because successive pullbacks along an isomorphism and its inverse give the original ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.SequenceOfBlowups.Isomorphic.trans: Compose the isomorphisms at each stage and chain the equalities of lengths. The initial equations and the commuting transition squares compose. Pullback of a center along the composite is successive pullback, giving the two center identities in succession. These data satisfy all comparison conditions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.eqToIso_hom_comp_projectionToBase_of_eq: Identify the two equal indices. The induced stage isomorphism is the identity and leaves the projection to the base unchanged.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inv_mem_support_comap_of_iso: The support of the pulled-back ideal is the inverse image under the forward isomorphism of the original support. The image of the inverse point under the forward isomorphism is the original point, which lies in the support by hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_restrict_of_eq: Equal morphisms have equal restrictions to the same target open. Transport the given isomorphism property across this equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenMap_iso_hom: A scheme isomorphism induces a homeomorphism on underlying spaces. Every homeomorphism takes open sets to open sets.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularParameterSystem_congr: The two parameter lists agree at every index, so they are equal as functions. Substitute the second list into the stated regular parameter property.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isRegularParameterSystem_ringEquiv: The images of the parameters lie in the new maximal ideal. Conversely, an element of that maximal ideal is carried by the inverse isomorphism into the original maximal ideal, which is generated by the given parameters. Mapping such an expression forward puts the element in the ideal generated by the images. These images therefore generate the new maximal ideal, and invariance of Krull dimension gives the required number of them.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_reducedIn: At the corresponding point of the original scheme, choose an affine neighborhood and the local product description by regular parameters. The inverse isomorphism gives an affine inverse-image neighborhood and identifies its section and local rings with the original ones. Regularity and the regular parameter system transport along the local ring isomorphism, and compatibility with germs shows the transported sections realize those parameters. The new inverse-image closed set is the inverse image of the old one, so its vanishing ideal on the new chart is the image of the original ideal under the section-ring isomorphism. This image is generated by the product of the transported parameters, giving strict normal crossings at the chosen point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_hom_comp_projectionToBase_of_commute: Induct on the stage. At zero the assertion is the stipulated compatibility of the initial isomorphisms. At a successor factor each projection through the preceding stage. Use the commuting square for the successor transitions to move the stage isomorphism across that factor. The induction hypothesis then identifies the remaining composite with the preceding projection to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.iso_inv_comp_eq_comp_inv: Start from the commuting square for the forward isomorphisms. Precompose with the inverse source isomorphism and postcompose with the inverse target isomorphism. Cancelling the inverse pairs gives the commuting square in the opposite direction.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.map_mem_maximalIdeal_ringEquiv: The maximal ideal of a local ring consists of its nonunits. A ring isomorphism preserves and reflects being a unit, since its inverse is also a ring homomorphism. Thus the image of the given nonunit is a nonunit.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_specMap_asIdeal: The map on spectra sends a prime ideal to its inverse image under the ring homomorphism. Membership in that inverse image means that the element’s image lies in the original prime.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_of_mem_support_comap: The support of the pulled-back ideal is the inverse image of the original support. Its membership condition states exactly that the point’s image lies in the original support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.vanishingIdeal_preimage_fromSpec_of_isIs: The affine coordinate maps commute with the scheme isomorphism and the map on spectra of the section-ring isomorphism. Consequently, the inverse image of the subset in the new affine spectrum is the inverse image under that spectrum map of the subset in the original affine spectrum. The vanishing ideal formula for a ring isomorphism gives the result.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.vanishingIdeal_preimage_specMap: The ring isomorphism gives a bijection on prime ideals, with its inverse giving the inverse correspondence. If an element vanishes on all primes above the given set, apply the inverse ring isomorphism to it. Its inverse image belongs to every prime of the given set by the prime-membership correspondence. Thus the original element belongs to the image of the vanishing ideal. Conversely, an element of the original vanishing ideal maps to an element of every prime above the given set, and the ideal they generate is contained in the vanishing ideal upstairs.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineDetachedSingularPreimageEqBoundary: For any affine input the discarded loci are open and the discarded subschemes are smooth by hypothesis. The induced sequence’s centers lie over the singular locus, so restriction to the strict-transform summand gives that property for its centers off the detached loci. Apply the equality of inverse images for these affine principalization data at every relevant stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.ambientBlowupMorphism_comp_schemeAtToSpe: The projection from the successor stage to the ambient base factors through the preceding stage by the current blowdown. Composing with the ambient base’s map to the field gives the displayed compatibility.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.avoidsCenters_of_forall_notMem_boundary: Use the inductive boundary avoidance result on the ambient stage of these principalization data. It identifies avoidance of every current boundary support as sufficient for avoiding all earlier centers.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.avoidsCenters_of_forall_notMem_support_b: Induct on the stage. Initial avoidance is vacuous. At a successor the point avoids all the new boundary, including the new exceptional divisor. This divisor is the pullback of the current center, so the image point avoids the center. If the image belonged to a prior boundary support, the original point, being off the center, would lie in the strict transform of that support. That strict transform is also a member of the new boundary, a contradiction. Hence the image avoids all prior boundary members and avoids the earlier centers by induction. Together these give successor avoidance.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.base_apply_mem_support_ker: Every morphism factors through the closed subscheme defined by its kernel ideal. Thus the image of the chosen source point belongs to the range of that closed subscheme’s inclusion, which is the kernel ideal’s support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.base_comp_apply: The underlying point map of a composite is obtained by applying the first point map and then applying the second.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.boundary_preimage_subset_smoothLocusComp: A point of the discarded piece whose ambient image is on the boundary lies in the support of one boundary member. This implies failure of center avoidance. Because the original centers off the detached locus lie over singular points, the earlier induction on failure of center avoidance sends the point in the strict transform to the singular locus. The discarded piece’s map to the base factors through that point, giving the claimed containment.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedSingularPreimageEqBoundary_ofAff: One inclusion sends points on the ambient boundary to the original singular locus using the center condition. For the converse, suppose a point of the discarded piece lies over the singular locus but its ambient image lies in no boundary support. It then avoids all preceding centers. The local-ring comparison and smoothness of the discarded piece force its image to lie in the smooth locus, a contradiction. This proves equality of the two inverse images.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToBase_comp_eq_discardedι_comp_s: The map of the discarded piece to the original scheme factors through its strict transform and the initial strict transform. The initial map followed by the morphism to the field agrees with the ambient initial structural map on the strict transform. The successive strict-transform maps commute with all structural maps to the field, so substitution gives the stated equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.forall_mem_smoothLocusComplement_of_not_: Induct on the stage, with the initial case vacuous because no center has yet been encountered. At a successor, the point projects to the base through its image in the preceding strict transform. If its ambient image lies in the current center, the preceding strict-transform point lies in the complement of the detached locus because it comes from the next strict transform. It is therefore on the center off the detached locus, which maps into the original singular locus by hypothesis. If the ambient image avoids the current center, failure of successor avoidance means that this image failed to avoid an earlier center. The strict-transform square identifies the relevant preceding point, so induction puts its base image in the singular locus as well.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_of_formallySmooth_comp_is: Compose the formally smooth map from the hypothesis with the inverse isomorphism, which is formally smooth. The isomorphisms cancel, so formal smoothness of the composite gives formal smoothness of the original first map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.formallySmooth_of_isIso: An isomorphism of rings is formally smooth. A map from its target across a nilpotent quotient lifts by transporting the given map from its source along the inverse isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.idealSheafData_comap_injective_of_isIso: Pull the equality back along the inverse isomorphism. Successive pullback along the isomorphism and its inverse is pullback along the identity, leaving the original ideal sheaves equal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_comp_of_isIso_commRingCat: If both ring maps are isomorphisms, the composite is inverted by composing their inverses in reverse order.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_of_isIso_comp_right: Compose the isomorphic composite with the inverse of the second map. The second map and its inverse cancel, leaving the first map as a composite of isomorphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_stalkMap_of_isIso_stalkMap_comp: The stalk map of the composite is the stalk map of the second scheme morphism followed by that of the first. Since the second ring map in this composite is an isomorphism and the composite is an isomorphism, the first ring map is an isomorphism by cancellation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_stalkMap_of_isOpenImmersion: An open immersion identifies the source with an open subscheme of the target. Restricting to an open neighborhood does not change the stalk at a point of that neighborhood, so the stalk map is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_stalkMap_strictTransformToZero_of_: At zero the projection is the identity. At a successor, avoidance places the point above the complement of the current center, where the ambient blowdown is an isomorphism and the new strict-transform ideal is the pullback of the preceding one. The strict-transform map is therefore an open immersion near the point by the restricted kernel comparison. It induces an isomorphism on the stalk. The image point downstairs avoids all earlier centers by the avoidance criterion and the commuting square. By induction its projection to zero induces an isomorphism on stalks as well. The stalk map of the composite to zero is a composite of these isomorphisms.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_preimage_ι_comp_of_ker_c: Restrict the ambient map to the given open, where it is an isomorphism. Composing the restricted upper closed immersion with that isomorphism gives a closed immersion into the lower open. Its kernel agrees with the restricted lower closed immersion’s kernel, because their pullbacks along the ambient isomorphism agree by hypothesis and such pullback is injective. Equal kernels give an isomorphism between these two closed subschemes of the open. Compatibility of the original square and cancellation of the lower closed immersion identify the prescribed morphism on the upper open with that isomorphism followed by inclusion of the corresponding lower open. Thus it is an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_smoothLocusComplement_of_not_avoidsC: Apply the stagewise result to the given point. Its failure to avoid prior centers puts its image under the projection through stage zero in the complement of the smooth locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_centerOffDetached_of_mem_sup: The point lies in the complement of the detached locus and maps into the ambient center. By the support formula for pullbacks, its lift to the complement therefore lies in the support of the restricted center ideal. Lift it further to the closed subscheme of that ideal. The composite from this closed subscheme to the full strict transform has kernel equal to the center ideal off the detached locus. Its image point lies in that kernel’s support.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_support_strictTransform_of_mem_suppo: The image lies in the preceding support with the center removed, so the point belongs to the inverse image of that difference. It therefore belongs to its closure, which is the support of the strict-transform ideal.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.notMem_smoothLocusComplement_detachedToB: The discarded subscheme is the clopen subscheme of the reduced strict transform, so its inclusion induces a stalk isomorphism. The projection to the initial strict transform induces a stalk isomorphism by center avoidance, and the initial map to the base is an open immersion, giving another stalk isomorphism. Their composite is the discarded piece’s map to the base, so its stalk map is an isomorphism. The discarded piece is smooth over the field. Thus the composite from the base field to its local ring is formally smooth. Cancelling the stalk isomorphism gives formal smoothness of the structural stalk map at the image in the base. This places the base image in the smooth locus.

A point outside every ambient boundary support avoids all earlier centers by the boundary avoidance theorem. The stalk argument for such points then shows that its image in the original scheme belongs to the smooth locus.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.not_avoidsCenters_of_mem_support_boundar: Use the inductive boundary result for the principalization sequence of the given affine-space data. The boundary, ambient stage, and avoidance predicate are those of that sequence.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.principalizationSequence_not_avoidsCente: At stage zero the boundary is empty. At a successor, a boundary member is the new exceptional divisor or the strict transform of a previous boundary member. In the first case the image point lies on the current center because the exceptional support is its inverse image. In the second, the strict-transform support is contained in the pullback of the preceding support, so the image belongs to the preceding boundary and fails earlier avoidance by induction. Either case contradicts avoidance through the successor stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformToZero_comp_schemeAtToSpe: Induct on the stage. The initial projection is the identity. At a successor the induction hypothesis calculates the composite to the field through the preceding strict transform. The strict-transform transition commutes with the ambient blowdown, and that blowdown commutes with the structure maps to the field. Thus the composite is the new strict-transform inclusion followed by the new ambient structure map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransform_comap_ι_eq_comap_restric: The strict-transform ideal is the kernel of the closed immersion formed from the original ideal pulled back over the center complement, followed by inclusion of that open into the blowup. Restricting this kernel to the open gives the kernel of the closed immersion itself. This is exactly the restricted pullback of the original ideal.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_restrict_smoothLocus_apply_eq: The chart maps cover the base, so the chosen smooth point has a preimage in some chart. Since its image is smooth, that preimage lies in the open where this chart is restricted to the smooth locus. The restricted chart map sends it to the chosen point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_lastStructMap_restrict_smoothLocus: The restrictions of the original chart maps form an open cover of the smooth locus. Pulling the restricted global morphism back to each of these opens gives an isomorphism by the local calculation. Being an isomorphism is local on the target for an open cover, so the restricted global morphism is an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isIso_pullback_snd_restrict_smoothLocus: The final chart square is a pullback. Restrict it over the smooth locus by pasting the pullback squares for open restriction. The base change of the global restricted morphism to this chart is therefore identified with the local final map restricted to the inverse image of the smooth locus. This is the local smooth locus. The local resolution makes the restricted map an isomorphism, and the pullback identification transfers this property to the indicated projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isPullback_chartToLastObj: The two structural maps form a commuting square by compatibility of the chart map with the final global map. The final local object is isomorphic to the pullback, and under that isomorphism its projections are the local structural map and the chart map. Hence the square is a pullback.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.affineSmoothLocusPreimageDenseInDetached: It suffices to show that every generic point of a discarded component maps to the smooth locus. The discarded scheme embeds as a closed union of strict-transform components, so the image of a discarded generic point is generic in a strict-transform component. Tracking the strict transforms back to zero gives a generic point there, and the stage-zero open immersion takes it to an ambient generic point of the original affine scheme. The smooth locus of this reduced scheme over a characteristic-zero field is dense and open, so it contains that generic point. The composite used here is the discarded scheme’s projection to the base. Hence the smooth-locus preimage contains all discarded generic points and is dense.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.dense_of_forall_mem_of_isGenericPoint: Every point belongs to an irreducible component with a generic point. The generic point lies in the prescribed set by hypothesis, so the closure of that set contains the whole component and in particular the original point. Thus the set is dense.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isGenericPoint_image_of_isClosedE: Choose one of the ambient components in the specified family containing the image of the given generic point. It lies in the range of the embedding, so its inverse image is closed and irreducible and contains the closure of the given generic point. Maximality of the source component makes this inverse image equal to it. Its image is consequently the chosen ambient component. By continuity and closedness, the image of the generic point is generic for that component.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isGenericPoint_image_of_isOpenEmb: Take the closure of the image of the generic point. It is irreducible. If an irreducible set contains this closure, it meets the open image of the embedding. Its intersection with the open image is therefore dense in it. In the source, the closure of its inverse image is irreducible and contains the original component, so maximality makes that closure the original component. The intersection upstairs is consequently contained in the image of the original component, which by continuity lies in the closure of the image generic point. Density then forces the larger irreducible set into that same closure, proving maximality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_isGenericPoint_strictTransformToZ: At stage zero the map to stage zero is the identity. At a successor, component tracking sends the given generic point to a generic point of a component at the previous stage. Induction sends that point to a generic point of a stage-zero component. The recursive projection agrees with this composite.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isGenericPoint_image_of_isClosed: The image of the generic point lies in the closed image of the component, so its closure is contained there. Conversely, continuity sends the closure of the original generic point into the closure of its image. This gives the reverse containment and identifies the new generic point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isOpenImmersion_strictTransformZeroToBas: At stage zero the discarded summand is empty, so inclusion of the strict-transform summand into the total space is an isomorphism. The total space is isomorphic to the original base at this stage. Their composite is the strict-transform map and is an isomorphism, hence an open immersion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.mem_of_isGenericPoint_of_isOpen_of_dense: In a Noetherian space a dense set meets each irreducible component. Choose a point of the chosen component in the dense open. This point lies in the closure of the component’s generic point. Since the open contains the point, it must also contain the generic point.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comapAmbientCenter_le_centerOffDetached: The center off the detached locus is obtained by restricting the pulled-back ambient center to the complement and then taking its image ideal under the open inclusion. By the adjunction between ideal pullback and image, containment of the original ideal in that image is equivalent to containment of its restriction in itself.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.comp_inv_comp_hom_cancel: Reassociate the composite so the inverse is followed immediately by the forward isomorphism. Their composite is the identity, and removing it gives the stated morphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInl_eq: The inclusion of the previously detached coproduct into the enlarged coproduct is defined as its first summand inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInl_inr_totalTransition: On the previously detached summand, the next total transition sends it back to the same detached summand of the preceding total space. Restrict the defining coproduct map to that summand to get the equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInl_inr_totalTransition_as: Compose the formula for the transition on the previously detached summand with the given morphism, then reassociate.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInr_eq: The inclusion of the newly detached scheme into the enlarged detached coproduct is its second summand inclusion by definition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInr_inr_totalTransition: The new detached summand maps to the preceding total space through its inclusion in the preceding strict transform. This is the specified restriction of the total transition, so it gives the formula after both summand inclusions.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodInr_inr_totalTransition_as: Compose the transition equation on the newly detached summand with the last morphism. Reassociating gives the stated equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodMapOfLE_inr_totalMapOfLE: At equal indices both iterates are identities. At a successor, the forward map includes the older detached coproduct through the previous detached part. One backward total transition acts on that part by its inclusion in the preceding total space. The induction hypothesis then cancels the remaining forward inclusions and backward transitions to give the original inclusion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodMapOfLE_self: When the indices coincide, the recursive inclusion of detached coproducts is initialized as the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodMapOfLE_succ: The inclusion into the successor detached coproduct is obtained from the preceding inclusion by adjoining the new summand and then including the preceding coproduct as the first summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprodMapOfLE_succ_of_le: The recursive step at any successor endpoint first includes the original detached coproduct in the preceding one and then includes that preceding coproduct as the first summand of the new one.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprod_hom_ext: Apply the inductive coproduct comparison at the specified stage. Agreement after each individual detached summand inclusion is exactly its hypothesis.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprod_hom_ext_forall: Induct on the stage. At zero the coproduct is initial, so the two maps agree by uniqueness. At a successor, their restrictions to the newly detached summand agree by the given equality at that index. On the previously detached coproduct they agree on every earlier summand by the recursive inclusion formula, so induction gives equality on that part. The coproduct property then gives equality on the successor.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedCoprod_succ_hom_ext: At a successor the detached coproduct is the coproduct of its previous part and the newly detached piece. Two morphisms out of this coproduct coincide if they agree on the two inclusions, as assumed.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_detachedCoprodMapOfLE: Induct on the final index. At equal indices the coproduct map is the identity. At a successor, the induction hypothesis says that including the piece through the original coproduct agrees with its direct inclusion at the preceding stage. Following with the first summand inclusion is exactly the recursive definition of its inclusion at the new stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_inr_inducedBlowups_proj: The induced projection is the iterated total map to stage zero followed by the initial total-space isomorphism. On the chosen detached piece, the iterated map factors through its inclusion in the strict transform at detachment, then the transition to the initial strict transform, then the first summand inclusion. The last inclusion followed by the initial total-space isomorphism is the strict-transform isomorphism to the base. This is the desired projection from the piece.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_inr_totalMapOfLE: Apply the iterated transition result to the chosen detached piece and the two total stages. Since the earlier total stage is at or before detachment, the composite passes through the strict transform at detachment and then its projection to the earlier strict-transform summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_inr_totalMapOfLE_forall: Induct on the stage of the later total space. At zero there is no earlier detached piece. At a successor, if the piece was just detached, its inclusion is the new second summand. The first backward transition sends it into the strict transform at its detachment stage, and the iterated strict-transform compatibility gives the rest of the composite. If it was detached earlier, the first backward transition sends it to the corresponding unchanged summand of the preceding detached coproduct. The induction hypothesis then gives the formula.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_self: The piece detached at the current stage first appears in the successor coproduct. Its inclusion there is the second summand inclusion, with the index identification acting as the identity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.detachedToCoprod_succ_of_lt: The piece detached at the specified earlier stage already belongs to the preceding coproduct. By the recursive definition its new inclusion is its preceding inclusion followed by insertion of that coproduct as the first summand.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_coprod_of_isInitial: The first coproduct inclusion has a retraction defined by the identity on the first summand and the unique map from the initial second summand. The other composite is the identity on the first summand by the defining coproduct equation and on the second by initiality. Thus the inclusion is the forward map of an isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_iso_of_coprodIso_of_isInitial: The first inclusion into a coproduct with an initial object is an isomorphism. Compose it with the given coproduct isomorphism to obtain the required isomorphism and forward map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.exists_strictTransformZeroIso: The initial detached coproduct is initial. The first inclusion therefore identifies the initial strict transform with the initial total space. Compose with the total-space isomorphism to the original scheme. Its compatibility with the transported embedding identifies the composite into the initial ambient scheme with the strict-transform inclusion. Following this equation by the initial ambient isomorphism gives the claimed equation over the original ambient scheme.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.hom_comp_base_apply: The map on points of a composite applies the first map and then the second map to the given point.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowups_blowupMorphism: The successor morphism of the induced sequence is the image of the successor order arrow under its underlying total-space tower. By construction that arrow is the total transition.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inducedBlowups_transitionMap: Induct on the later endpoint. For identical indices the tower transition and the iterated total map are both identities. At a successor the tower transition factors by functoriality into the last successor morphism and the previous transition. The last is the total transition, and the previous agrees with the iterated total map by induction. This composite is exactly the recursive successor total map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_inducedBlowups_projectionToBase: Write the induced projection as the iterated total map to zero followed by the initial total-space isomorphism. Restricting the iterated map to the strict-transform summand gives the iterated strict-transform map to zero followed by the first summand inclusion. That inclusion composed with the initial isomorphism is the strict-transform isomorphism to the base. Their composite defines the claimed strict-transform projection.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_totalMapOfLE: Induct on the later endpoint. At equality both transitions are identities. At a successor use the single-step formula on the strict-transform summand to move the inclusion through the total transition. Apply the induction hypothesis to the remaining total map. The two successive strict-transform maps form the required iterated map.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_totalSpaceZeroIso_hom: The inverse total-space isomorphism factors as the inverse strict-transform isomorphism followed by the first inclusion. Hence the first inclusion is the strict-transform isomorphism followed by the inverse total-space isomorphism. Composing with the forward total-space isomorphism gives the claimed equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_totalTransition: The total transition on the strict-transform summand is defined as the strict-transform transition followed by its inclusion into the preceding total space. This yields the equality.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.inl_totalTransition_assoc: Postcompose the equation for the strict-transform summand of the total transition with the given morphism, and use associativity.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformMapOfLE_self: The recursive transition between strict transforms starts with the identity when its two stage indices are the same.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformMapOfLE_strictTransformι: Induct on the later endpoint starting at the earlier stage. In the equal-stage case both transitions are identities. At a successor, factor both transitions through the preceding endpoint. The square for one strict-transform step commutes with the ambient blowdown, and the induction hypothesis makes the remaining square commute. Composing these squares gives the desired equation.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformMapOfLE_succ_of_le: The recursion for the later endpoint at a successor composes the single transition from that successor stage with the transition already defined from the preceding endpoint.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformToBase_emb: The strict-transform projection first passes to the initial strict transform and then uses its isomorphism to the original scheme. Composing with the original embedding replaces this last part by the initial strict-transform inclusion followed by the ambient initial isomorphism. The transition compatibility moves that inclusion to the given stage and leaves the ambient transition to zero. This ambient transition and the initial isomorphism give the ambient projection to the base.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.strictTransformZeroIso_hom_emb: The stage-zero strict-transform isomorphism was chosen with the property that its composite with the original embedding is the initial strict-transform inclusion followed by the ambient initial isomorphism.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.support_centerOffDetached_subset_preimag: The ambient center ideal pulled to the strict transform is contained in the center ideal off the detached locus. Thus the center subscheme off that locus maps to the ambient center by the closed-subscheme lifting property. Every point in its support lifts to that subscheme, and its ambient image therefore lies in the support of the ambient center.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalMapOfLE_self: The recursive total-space transition starts with the identity when the source and target stages coincide.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalMapOfLE_succ: For a successor endpoint, the recursive total map first applies the last total transition and then the preceding total map to the fixed starting stage.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalMapOfLE_succ_of_le: The recursive formula for a successor endpoint gives the last total transition followed by the previously defined map. The choice of proof of the stage inequality does not affect the recursion.
Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.totalSpaceZeroIso_inv_eq: Compose the stage-zero strict-transform compatibility with the inverse ambient isomorphism. It shows that the strict-transform isomorphism and the restriction of the total-space isomorphism to the strict-transform summand have the same composite with the transported embedding. That embedding is a monomorphism, so those maps are equal. Precompose the equality with the inverse strict-transform isomorphism and cancel the total-space isomorphism to get the formula for its inverse.

Development/ResolutionOfSingularities/Em.isStrongResolutionRule_iff: A strong resolution rule is defined by requiring its sequence on each quasi-compact reduced input over a characteristic-zero field to satisfy the six strong resolution conditions. Expanding the definition of a strong resolution at that input gives exactly the same conditions in the same order.

Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLi.Formalism.VW.critLine:
A zero strictly to the right of the critical line contradicts the assumed nonvanishing at once. Suppose it lies strictly to the left. The gamma factor at s is nonzero, so the completed L-function also vanishes there. The inverse character is primitive because inversion preserves its conductor. Its functional equation now gives a zero of the completed L-function at 1 − s.

Dividing by the gamma factor transfers that zero to the ordinary L-function of the inverse character. The point 1 − s has real part greater than 1/2 and is distinct from 1, so this again contradicts the assumed nonvanishing. The remaining possibility is Re(s) = 1/2.
Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLi.Formalism.VW.gammaFactor_ne_zero: For an even character the factor is Γℝ(s), and for an odd character it is Γℝ(s + 1). Both arguments have positive real part. The real gamma factor is nonzero in that half-plane.
Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLi.Formalism.VW.rh_of_every: Take the trivial character of modulus 1, whose L-function equals the zeta function. The assumed nonvanishing for all characters therefore excludes zeta zeros with real part greater than 1/2 away from 1. The reduction for zeros of the zeta function now gives the Riemann Hypothesis.

Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/RhOfRi.Formalism.VW.rh_of_right:
Let s be a nontrivial zero distinct from 1. The value of zeta at 0 also excludes s = 0. The assumed nonvanishing rules out Re(s) > 1/2. If Re(s) < 1/2, set t = 1 − s. Then Re(t) > 1/2 and t is distinct from 1, so ζ(t) is nonzero. The functional equation expresses ζ(s) as the product of ζ(t), Γ(t), cos(πt/2), and 2(2π)^(−t). The gamma and power factors are nonzero.

If the cosine vanished, t would equal 2k + 1 for an integer k, giving s = −2k. A negative k contradicts Re(s) < 1/2. The value k = 0 gives s = 0, and a positive k gives an excluded trivial zero. Thus the cosine factor is also nonzero. This contradicts ζ(s) = 0, so Re(s) = 1/2.

Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.FullTiedNoG.toFull_base: Completing the datum copies the underlying tied data from X and adds g. Its base projection is therefore the original base of X.
Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.FullTiedNoG.toFull_g: Completing the datum sets the G-data to g. The G-data are therefore the supplied g.
Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.adSet: The change of datum replaces the assigned G-data and its dimension certificate. The adjacency conditions use the original lattice and step data, the Hermitian columns, and the data at T. The change of datum copies the Hermitian columns and the data at T field by field. Consequently the upward, downward, and dilation conditions at level zero and at positive levels are identical to the six supplied conditions in h. Use those six fields for the new adjacency structure.
Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.full_setting_level_zero: The adjusted tied datum is built by applying the Hermitian change of datum to the original base. That change copies the level-zero field, so the completed datum has the original level-zero data.
Formalism/LocalToGlobal/GroupLattices/Ti.hermitian_setting_level_zero: The change of datum copies the tied Hermitian fields from H. In particular, its level-zero Hermitian data are those of H.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.exists_constant_exponent_inequalities:
Take C = 100000. Put G = w+S+η and z = G+1, so b ≥ 100000(j+1)z ≥ 200000z. This gives max(G,1) < b ≤ min(b₀,b₁) and η < b. Hence b₀ ≤ b+η < 2b ≤ 2b₁, which gives both comparisons with ℓb₁ because ℓ ≥ 11.

For the final bound use g = max(G,1) ≤ z and H = b+η+S ≤ b+G in the preceding bounds for the two exponents. The definition a₀ = 2σ + rr + 2g·ell and ell ≤ 3j+1 then with σ denoting the sigma exponent give a₀ < 0.242b + (6j+20000)z by collecting the coefficients. For j ≥ 1, 6j+20000 ≤ 11000(j+1), so the second term is at most 0.11b. Thus a₀ < b/2 ≤ b₁/2.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.log_nat_le: At h = 0 the real logarithm is zero by convention. For h > 0, split log h as log(h/1000) + log 1000. Apply log t ≤ t−1 to both terms and add the bounds.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mpar_le: The integer quotient in Mpar is bounded by the real quotient (h+2g)/(ℓ−1). Since ℓ−1 ≥ 10 and the numerator is nonnegative, replace the denominator by 10. Adding 1 gives the claim.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.rr_le: For the two rational terms use ℓ ≥ 11 and (ℓ−1)^(j+1) ≥ 10². Since log ℓ ≥ 1 and log h ≥ 0 for natural h under the real logarithm convention, log base ℓ of h is at most log h. Use the upper bound for the logarithm of a natural number and substitute the three bounds into the assumption on rr.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sig_lt: The power ℓ^(j−1) is at least 1, so the Mpar term after division by that power is bounded by Mpar itself. For ℓ ≥ 11, the bound ℓ/(ℓ−1)² ≤ 11/100 follows after clearing denominators from (ℓ−11)(11ℓ−1) ≥ 0. Substitute the bound on Mpar, then use that the ceiling of a nonnegative real is strictly less than that real plus 1. The 1 already in the argument of the ceiling makes the total rounding allowance 2.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.arc_exponential_identity: Because G ≥ 0 and j′ ≤ ell, we have j′G ≤ ell·G. If the maximum is 2σ+2j′G+1, bound it by 2σ+2ell·G+1 and add the prefactor. If the maximum is r+κ, the left side becomes 2r+4σ+2κ. The right side is larger by the nonnegative quantity 2σ+2ell·G+1.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.eta_determinant_comparison: Apply the determinant comparison input with the supplied ring action and element Θ. Its remaining premise is the product congruence for an arbitrary tuple of elements of R′ and a test point. View each tuple entry as a matrix-valued function over the fraction field. The hypothesis on R′ gives the action compatibility for each of these functions, so the product congruence input applies and supplies the premise.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mem_span_of_C_pow_mul:
Write C(aᵛ)g = p C(aᵗ) + qXᵇ using membership in the two-generator ideal. For every degree n < b, the last term has coefficient zero. Comparing degree-n coefficients therefore gives aᵛgₙ = aᵗpₙ. Since a is nonzero and v ≤ t, cancel aᵛ to obtain gₙ = a^(t−v)pₙ.

Thus every coefficient of g − p C(a^(t−v)) below degree b vanishes. This difference is divisible by Xᵇ, so g is a linear combination of C(a^(t−v)) and Xᵇ.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mem_span_of_X_pow_mul:
Write X^ηg = F C(a) + G X^(b+η), where C(a) is the constant series a. If a = 0, the first term vanishes. Cancel X^η, which is nonzero in the power series domain, to obtain g = G X^b.

For a ≠ 0, rearrange to get F C(a) = X^η(g − G X^b). Its coefficients of degree below η vanish. Each is a times the corresponding coefficient of F, so that coefficient of F vanishes in the domain. Thus F = X^ηF′. Substitute this into the original equality and cancel X^η to obtain g = F′ C(a) + G X^b, which proves the desired ideal membership.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.column_assembly_bound: Use the chain length inequality to bound the length by the sum of layer lengths and the terminal length. For i in gen, the chosen generators and Fᵢ₊₁ span Fᵢ, so the quotient length bound for a finite spanning set applies with Bc = Fᵢ₊₁ and I = Fᵢ₊₁+P. This gives coefficient me′ in units of the length of O/(ℓ). For each other i, the assumed bound gives coefficient L. There are |gen| indices of the first kind and k−|gen| of the second because gen is contained in the index range. Add the layer estimates. Finally the bound for a submodule generated by a basis gives coefficient rank(M)·e for the terminal length. Factoring out the common length proves the formula.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.len_bound: Since Bc is contained in I, its image is zero in Z/(Z∩I). The equality Z = span(s)+Bc then says the classes of s generate the quotient. They are killed by a^e, and therefore give a surjection from |s| copies of O/(a^e). Each copy has length at most e times the length of O/(a). Use |s| ≤ g to finish.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.len_chain: At k = 0 the initial term is the quotient M/P, since F₀ is the full module. In the induction step apply the two-step length equality to Fₖ₊₁ ≤ Fₖ. It rewrites the old terminal length as the next layer length plus the next terminal length. Insert that equality into the bound for k and append the new summand.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.len_two_step: Include B/(B∩P) into A/(A∩P) and then quotient A by A∩(B+P). The inclusion is injective because an element of B represents zero in A/(A∩P) exactly when it is in P. The second map is onto. Its kernel consists of classes of a = b+p, with b in B and p in P. These are precisely the image of the first map, since a and b have the same class. Add lengths in the resulting short exact sequence.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sub_gen: Take a basis of F over the principal ideal domain and view its vectors in M. They form a finite spanning set of size at most the rank of F, which is at most the rank of M. Apply the quotient length bound for a finite spanning set with Bc = 0, I = P, and g equal to the rank of M, using the hypothesis that a^e kills the classes of F modulo P.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_len_add: Use the maps Y/X → Z/X → Z/Y induced by inclusion and quotient. The inclusion is injective because a representative from Y becomes zero exactly when it lies in X. The quotient map is surjective because the same representative in Z can be used in either quotient. Its kernel consists of classes represented by elements of Y, precisely the image of the inclusion. Length additivity for this short exact sequence gives the equality.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_len_le_of_le_sup: Use the map from A/(A∩X) to Z/(Z∩X) induced by inclusion. Given a representative z in Z, write z = a+x with a in A and x in X, using Z ≤ A+X. The class of z is the image of the class of a. The map is surjective, so the target has length at most the source.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_len_le_top: The map A/(A∩P) → M/P sends the class of a to its class in M/P. Every m in M can be written as a+p by the assumption M = A+P, so this map is surjective. Apply the length inequality for a surjection.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.column_chain_bound:
Induct on k. At k = 0 the sum is empty, and the terminal quotient represents the whole quotient since F₀ is the full module. For the induction step write U = Fₖ, V = Fₖ₊₁, X = P∩U, and Y = (V+P)∩U. Length additivity decomposes the old terminal term length(U/X) into length(Y/X) and length(U/Y). The latter is the new summand.

Since V ≤ U, the modular law gives Y = V+(P∩U). The map V/(V∩P) → Y/X is surjective by this equality, so length(Y/X) is bounded by the new terminal term. Substitute the two bounds into the induction hypothesis and append the new summand.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.comap_subtype_inf_of_le: An element of A already lies in C by the inclusion A ≤ C. Membership in B∩C on restricting to A is therefore equivalent to membership in B, giving equality of the two restricted submodules.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.comap_subtype_span_sup_eq_span_range_sup: Write A for the ambient span of s, which lies in Z. After mapping the two submodules into the ambient module via the inclusion of Z, the left side is (A+J) ∩ Z. The internal generators map to exactly the elements of s, so the right side maps to A+(J∩Z). These images agree by the modular law, since A ≤ Z. Injectivity of the inclusion gives equality of the submodules in Z.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.length_quotient_le_of_two_step:
Inside Z/(I∩Z), let N be the image of the span of s₀. The restriction identity for spans shows that N is generated by the classes of s₀. They are killed by ℓ^e′, so the length of N is at most g₀e′ times the length of O/(ℓ). Indeed, a module generated by g₀ such classes is a quotient of g₀ copies of O/(ℓ^e′), and each copy has length at most e′ times the length of O/(ℓ).

The quotient by N is Z modulo the restriction of span(s₀)+I. The classes of s generate this quotient because span(s)+I = Z, and these classes are killed by ℓ^e. The same estimate gives the bound with ge. Add both estimates along the exact sequence for N.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mem_cl: For the false orientation, membership in the window requires h−η ≤ u ≤ h−1. The strict inequality u < h−η excludes u from the window. Since u belongs to U, it belongs to the filtered complement for the false orientation.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.t3: The element u lies in the false-orientation complement by the preceding window comparison. Apply residue avoidance to u and k with the given lower and upper bounds on k. In this orientation the residue being tested is h−u.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.tele: Induct on the interval length k. At length zero the interval is empty and both sides equal M(a). For length k+1, add the endpoint a+k to the previous interval. The local relation at that endpoint gives f(a+k) + M(a+k+1) = g(a+k) + M(a+k), with arguments read modulo ℓ. Use this identity to move the new boundary term back to a+k, then apply the induction hypothesis to the old interval.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_of_step: Take the chain of length one with cuts a and b. Its only step is the supplied step from a to b.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.chain_trans: Concatenate the cut sequences, identifying the last cut of the first chain with the first cut of the second chain at b. Use the first chain's indices through its endpoint and subtract its length from each later index. Each adjacent pair lies in one of the original chains, including the pair that starts at b. Hence every pair is a valid step, and the endpoints are a and d.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.cluster_chain:
Induct on a natural bound for the distance B−a. Let f be the first marked point after a, which exists at or before B. The empty starting interval forces f > a+j. Set s = f−1−a. If the j places after f are empty, take e = f. Otherwise choose a marked g within that window and take e = g. The pair lemma gives an empty j-window after g and excludes marks strictly between f and g. Also g ≤ B, since otherwise B would either lie strictly between f and g or, if B = f, have a marked point in its own empty window.

In either case the tail (a+s,e] contains at most two marks, namely f and possibly g, and has length at most j+1. Apply fill to reach e. If e = B this is the desired chain. Otherwise e has an empty starting window and B−e is strictly smaller than B−a. Apply induction and concatenate.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.fill:
Use strong induction on the length s of the initial empty interval. If s < 2j, go directly from a to e. The length is at least j and at most s+j+1 ≤ 3j. The first j places are empty, and every marked point up to e lies after a+s. There are at most two such points by the tail assumption, so the direct step is valid.

If s ≥ 2j, first take a step of length j through the empty interval. From a+j, the remaining empty interval has length s−j ≥ j and still ends at a+s, so the tail assumptions are unchanged. The induction hypothesis gives a chain for this shorter interval. Concatenate the initial step and that chain.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.main:
If there are no marked points, take a = 0 and use fill on the empty interval of length n, with no tail. Otherwise start with a marked point t₀. If the next j places are empty, take t = t₀. If there is a mark g among them, take t = g, whose next j places are empty by the pair lemma.

Periodicity makes B = t+n a marked point and transfers the empty window after t to the window after B. Since n ≥ j+1 and j ≥ 1, the cut-chain lemma applies from t to B with distance bound n. This gives a chain spanning one period.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.pair:
At the marked point g, the cluster condition must take its second form because f is a marked predecessor within distance j. The unique permitted predecessor in the stated range is therefore f itself. All points strictly between f and g are excluded.

If there were a marked point h in (g,g+j], apply the same condition at h. The permitted predecessor would have to be g, at distance h−g. But f would be a second marked predecessor at distance (h−g)+(g−f), which is at most (h−g)+j. This violates the exclusion range at h. Hence the whole interval (g,g+j] is empty.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.expBound_statement:
Put H = h+η, d = ℓ−1, and L = lam(ℓ,H). Insert the upper bounds on s₁, e₂, and both occurrences of E. Bound b by H and the integer quotient in sig by h/d ≤ H/d. The terms involving a now sum to 8a/d. By the assumption on a and the definition of aR, this contributes at most 8H(2ℓ−1)/d³ + (32+8L)/d.

Collect the H terms to obtain H·[8(2ℓ−1)/d³ + 8/d² + 1/(ℓd)]. The coefficient bound gives at most 32H/ℓ². The remaining terms are 10η/d, (3+3/d)S, and 9L+10+(34+8L)/d. Since d ≥ 10, the S coefficient is at most 4. Since L ≥ 1, the last group is at most 24L. These are the required terms.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.hcoef_le: Bound the three terms by (41/2)/x², 10/x², and (11/10)/x², respectively. For the first two, clear the positive denominators and put t = x−11 ≥ 0. The differences become (9/2)t³+95t²+518t+172 and 2t²+24t+32. For the third, the cleared inequality is 10x ≤ 11(x−1). Adding the three bounds gives 31.6/x² ≤ 32/x².
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.lam_ge_one: If H = 0, log base ℓ of 2H is zero by the real logarithm convention. If H is positive, then 2H ≥ 1, so this logarithm is nonnegative since ℓ > 1. In either case adding 1 gives at least 1.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.first_sigma_valuation_bound:
Bound the sum on the union by the two interval sums with zero removed. On the first interval, reflect the negative integers and keep the positive ones. Valuation depends only on absolute value, so the two pieces are bounded by the factorial valuations at η−1 and η+a, using natural subtraction for η−1.

The second interval lies entirely below zero because b ≥ 2a+η+1. Reflection gives the interval from m+1 through m+a+S, where m = b−a−1. Its valuation sum is vℓ((m+a+S)!)−vℓ(m!). The binomial coefficient bound gives at most vℓ((a+S)!) + logℓ(m+a+S), with the integer logarithm in this expression.

Apply vℓ(N!) ≤ N/(ℓ−1) to the three factorial terms. Their numerator is at most 2a+2η+S. The integer logarithm is bounded by lam(ℓ,h+η), since m+a+S ≤ b+S ≤ h and the nonzero argument case follows by taking logs of ℓ^logℓ(N) ≤ N. For a zero argument the integer logarithm is zero. Finally lam(ℓ,h+η) is nonnegative, so increasing the logarithmic allowance to twice this quantity gives the stated bound.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.padicValNat_factorial_add_le_add_log: Factor (m+L)! as the product of m!, L!, and the binomial coefficient choosing L from m+L. These factors are positive, so their valuations add. The valuation of the binomial coefficient is at most the integer logarithm of m+L by the prime-factorization bound for binomial coefficients. Add this bound to the other two valuations.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sub_one_mul_padicValNat_factorial_le': Use the factorial valuation formula (ℓ−1)vℓ(N!) = N − sℓ(N), where sℓ is the base-ℓ digit sum. Its nonnegativity gives the desired bound.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sum_Icc_one_padicValNat_eq_factorial: Take m = 0 in the interval-factorial formula. The initial factorial is 0! = 1 with valuation zero, leaving the valuation of L! as the sum from 1 to L.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sum_Icc_padicValNat_add_factorial_eq: At L = 0 the interval is empty. To increase L by one, add its new upper endpoint m+L+1 to the valuation sum. At the same time the factorial is multiplied by m+L+1. Valuations add under multiplication of these positive integers, so the induction identity is preserved.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sum_erase_union_le: Removing zero from the union gives the union of the two sets with zero removed. The sum over this union plus the sum over the intersection equals the two separate sums. The intersection sum is nonnegative, so it can be dropped on the left.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.hCoef_num: Put t = x−11 ≥ 0. The polynomial expands to 7t³+153t²+920t+892. Every term is nonnegative.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.h_coefficient_bound: Subtract the three terms on the left from 32/x² and use the common denominator x²(x−1)³. The numerator is 7x³−78x²+95x−32, which is nonnegative by the preceding numerator estimate. The denominator is positive for x ≥ 11, so the difference is nonnegative.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.kappa_window_bound:
The killer-polynomial valuation formula gives nonvanishing and expresses the valuation at 1 as ell plus the sum of 1+ell+vℓ(i) over the nonzero indices i. Let S be those indices. The windows cover S, so counting with weight 1 bounds its size by the sum of their lengths.

Apply the same covering inequality with weight vℓ(i). In each window, the selected indices are nonzero and satisfy |i| ≤ D. The window-sum estimate then gives Lₖ/(ℓ−1) + log base ℓ of D for their valuation sum. Sum the window bounds and add ell and the bound on the constant contribution (1+ell)|S|.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sum_le_sum_cover: Each i in S belongs to at least one window, so its weight is bounded by the sum of its contributions over all windows. This uses nonnegativity of the weights. Sum over i, interchange the two finite sums, and collect precisely those elements of S lying in each window.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.second_exponent_bound: The proposed right side is nonnegative because ℓ ≥ 2 and all its terms are nonnegative. For the other entry of the maximum, cancel the two terms involving h″ and substitute the upper bound for c′. The terms involving b′ cancel. Now split (b+S+1)/(ℓ−1) into b/(ℓ−1) and (S+1)/(ℓ−1). The identity b/(ℓ−1) = b/(ℓ(ℓ−1)) + b/ℓ cancels the negative b/ℓ. Bound (S+1)/(ℓ−1) by S+1. The resulting bound is at most the claimed right side.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.C_mem_polyS: The constant polynomial C(c) has coefficient c in degree zero and zero in all higher degrees. Both values lie in S.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.F_eq: Every letter has degree one. For L = (c,1,g) its term is X times the constant-coefficient matrix obtained from cρ(g). Summing these identities factors out X, and the constant-coefficient map commutes with the matrix sum. This also holds for the empty list, whose sums vanish.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.F_perm: Permuting the triples permutes the list of their matrix terms. Its sum is unchanged by commutativity of matrix addition, so taking the determinant of the identity minus that sum gives the same polynomial.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.S1_mem_OmF: The carrier of S1 requires each multivariate coefficient function to lie in the subalgebra of functions from T. Unfolding that carrier replaces each such membership by the assertion that the coefficient function comes from T, which is the right-hand side.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.X_mem_polyS: The coefficient of X in degree one is 1, and all its other coefficients are zero. The subring S contains both values.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.alg_identity: Let P = 1+x+⋯+xᴺ and Y be the sum of the list ys. For each power of x, distribute left multiplication over the sum Y. The total sum inside the second factor is then PY. The finite geometric identity and x^(N+1) = 0 give (1−x)P = 1. Hence (1−x)(1−PY) = (1−x)−Y = 1−(x+Y). The products keep x and its powers on the left throughout.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.allD: Induct on the amount j by which the lower degree bound can be raised before it reaches N+1. If j = 0, all terms vanish in the truncation and the determinant equals 1. For the successor step, increasing the minimum degree from D to D+1 makes the induction hypothesis available. The degree-elimination lemma transfers that result back to lists of minimum degree D.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.base: In the quotient modulo X^(N+1), every scalar monomial in the list is zero because its degree is at least N+1. Thus the sum of matrix terms vanishes. The image of F is the determinant of the identity, which is 1.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.charpolyRev_map: Apply the coefficient ring homomorphism to the determinant that defines the reversed characteristic polynomial. It commutes with determinants, fixes the polynomial variable, and maps the constant matrix entries through f. Entry by entry the result is the defining matrix for the reversed characteristic polynomial of M with entries mapped through f.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.charpoly_comp: The reversed characteristic polynomial of ρ(g) is the determinant of I−Xρ(g), with the matrix entries regarded as constants. Substitute C(c)Xᵈ for X in this determinant for L = (c,d,g). Substitution fixes scalar entries and commutes with determinants. The resulting matrix is I minus the term attached to L.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.comp_mem_polyS: Expand p(q) as the finite sum of C(pₑ)qᵉ over the degrees in p. Each constant C(pₑ) belongs to the coefficient subring, and every power of q does too. Closure under products and finite sums gives the result.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.core: Truncate at degree k. The degree-elimination result with initial degree bound 1 puts the class of F in the image of the polynomials over S. Choose a polynomial q over S representing that class. The difference F−q is divisible by X^(k+1), so its coefficient in degree k is zero. Thus the degree-k coefficient of F is the corresponding coefficient of q and belongs to S.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.det_eq_coeff: In a subsingleton ring the two values agree. Otherwise let d be the matrix dimension. The characteristic polynomial has degree d, so reversing it makes its constant coefficient the degree-d coefficient of the reversed polynomial. The constant coefficient of the characteristic polynomial is (−1)ᵈ det M. Multiplication by (−1)ᵈ gives the asserted formula because its square is 1.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.det_poly_statement:
For each matrix aᵢ choose its finite representation as a sum of group matrices with coefficient functions from T. Multiply each coefficient function by the multivariate variable Xᵢ. The resulting polynomial-valued function belongs to S1 because its only possibly nonzero coefficient is the original function. Lift the group matrices to matrices of constant multivariate polynomials, retaining their dependence on the test point. Evaluation at a point commutes with the reversed characteristic polynomial, so its only possibly nonzero multivariate coefficient comes from the original characteristic coefficient function. The input hypothesis puts that function in T.

Use these weighted group matrices as the letters of the determinant argument, all with degree one in the auxiliary polynomial variable. The core result puts the coefficient in degree d, the matrix dimension, into S1. Since the letters all have degree one, their determinant polynomial is the reversed characteristic polynomial of the summed weighted matrix. The sign formula converts that coefficient to the determinant, still in S1.

At each test point, expand the finite sum and use the chosen representations of the aᵢ. The weighted matrix evaluates to the sum of Xᵢaᵢ with entries mapped to constant multivariate polynomials. Evaluation commutes with the determinant. Taking the requested multivariate coefficient now gives a function from T by the defining condition of S1.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.geom_list: For N = 0 both sides equal 1−x. At the next step the finite sum acquires x^(N+1). Left multiplication by 1−x adds x^(N+1)−x^(N+2) to the previous value 1−x^(N+1). This gives the required value at N+1. The calculation uses only powers of the same element and works in a noncommutative ring.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.key:
Work in the coefficient ring modulo X^(N+1). Let x be the matrix term of L₀ there. The positive X-degree of L₀ makes x^(N+1) zero. For each term y from the rest of the list, the new triples represent the products xy through xᴺy by the formula for the new matrix terms. Thus the eliminated list sums to (1+x+⋯+xᴺ)Y, where Y is the original sum of the rest.

Apply the algebraic identity to factor I−(x+Y) as (I−x) times the identity minus the new sum. The quotient map commutes with determinants, and the determinant of a matrix product is the product of determinants over the commutative coefficient ring. This gives the asserted factorization in the quotient.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.letter_mem: By the substitution formula, the single-letter determinant is the reversed characteristic polynomial of ρ(g) evaluated at C(c)Xᵈ. The characteristic coefficients lie in S by hypothesis, and the substituted monomial has its coefficients in S because c belongs to S. Composition preserves this coefficient condition. Passing to the quotient gives membership in the image subring.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mapMatrix_smul_zero: The entry in position (i,j) of the mapped matrix is the product of the images of a and Mᵢⱼ. The first factor is zero, so every entry vanishes.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.mem_mainNotions_iff_fromT: The carrier of the subalgebra is defined to consist of the functions from T. Membership therefore says exactly that the function comes from T.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.piN_eq_zero: Since d ≥ N+1, the monomial C(c)Xᵈ is divisible by X^(N+1). It therefore vanishes in the quotient by that principal ideal.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.stepD:
Induct on the number of letters of degree exactly D. With no such letters, all degrees are at least D+1 and the given higher-degree result applies. Otherwise move one degree-D letter to the front and factor it out by the determinant factorization. Its single-letter factor belongs to the image subring by the single-letter coefficient result.

In the remaining list, the old letters retain their coefficients and degrees. Each new letter multiplies an old coefficient by a positive power of the removed one, so the coefficient remains in S. Its degree is the old degree plus a positive multiple of D and is strictly larger than D. Thus the number of degree-D letters drops by exactly one, and the induction hypothesis puts the remaining determinant in the image subring. Multiply the two factors there.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.sum_flat: Induct on the outer list. The empty list gives zero. For a head a followed by a tail, the flattened list is h(a) appended to the flattened tail. Its sum after applying f splits accordingly, and the induction hypothesis identifies the second sum.
Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.term_newL: Write L₀ = (c₀,d₀,g₀) and L = (c,d,g). The new triple has scalar c₀ᵏc, degree kd₀+d, and monoid element g₀ᵏg. Multiplicativity of the representation and of the constant-polynomial map gives the matrix factor ρ(g₀)ᵏρ(g), with entries mapped into R[X]. Multiplying the scalar monomials gives C(c₀ᵏc)X^(kd₀+d). This is the product of the kth power of the term for L₀ with the term for L, in that order.

Formalism/TruncatedSeriesCounting/Trunca.g_ideal_valuation_statement:
Let S₁ = [b−a+1,b]. The hypothesis b ≥ 2a+η+1 puts S₁ strictly above the low interval for S₂, and the other interval for S₂ starts at b+1. Thus the two sets are disjoint. The Lagrange ideal lifting theorem supplies ideal membership at exponent E, the supremum over j₀ in S₁ of the valuation sum on S₂ and on S₁ with j₀ removed. Its association hypothesis is exactly the one assumed for the differences of c.

For a fixed j₀, split the sum into S₁ with j₀ removed and the high and low portions of S₂. Their differences j₀−j lie in windows of lengths a, S+a, and 2η+a, respectively. All differences are nonzero by disjointness and the removal of j₀. The interval endpoints and b+S ≤ h give |j₀−j| ≤ h+η. Apply the window valuation estimate to each of the three parts. The lengths add to 3a+S+2η, and each logarithm is at most lam(ℓ,h+η). This bounds every value in the supremum and hence E. If S₁ is empty, E is zero and the bound follows by nonnegativity.
